approaches.name: Stock-to-Flow / S2FX Scarcity Power-Law
approaches.description: S2F models Bitcoin's market value as a power-law function of its stock-to-flow ratio (existing supply / annual new issuance), the same monetary-scarcity metric used for gold and silver. PlanB's original fit was ln(market value) = 3.3·ln(SF) + 14.6, i.e. value ∝ SF^3.3, reportedly R²≈0.95; the later S2FX cross-asset version pools BTC/gold/silver and treats halvings as discrete "phase transitions" (clusters), reportedly R²≈0.997. A 10-15yr CMA falls out mechanically: because Bitcoin's issuance halves every ~4 years, SF roughly doubles each halving, so the power law projects ~10x market value per doubling. Chaining that across the ~2028, ~2032, ~2036 halvings yields the model's forward price path and hence an implied multi-year appreciation rate — purely supply-driven, with no role for demand, cashflow, volatility, or cross-asset correlation.
key_drivers: Stock-to-flow ratio SF = circulating supply / annual new issuance (rises mechanically as block subsidy halves every ~210,000 blocks / ~4 years)
Power-law exponent (~3.3 in original S2F) linking ln(SF) to ln(market value)
Halving schedule — the deterministic, pre-programmed supply shock that doubles SF and drives ~10x value steps
Cross-asset anchoring: gold (SF~62) and silver (SF~22) market values used to pin the regression line and justify a 'monetary scarcity' premium for BTC as SF approaches/exceeds gold
Phase transitions / clusters (S2FX): treating each halving epoch as a regime with distinct properties, replacing time with SF as the independent variable
Absolute scarcity / 21M hard cap as the terminal narrative (SF → ∞ as issuance → 0)
pros: Fully deterministic supply input: the halving schedule and 21M cap are known in advance, so SF is the rare financial variable with zero forecast error — attractive for a long-horizon CMA skeleton
Parsimonious and falsifiable: a single regressor produces explicit, dated price targets that can be checked (and have been)

Captures a real economic intuition — that a credibly fixed, ungrowable supply supports a monetary 'hardness' premium (the same logic that makes gold a store of value); the Austrian/Mises critique even concedes SF can matter for a money's quality
Cross-asset framing (S2FX) at least disciplines the BTC fit against gold and silver rather than fitting BTC in isolation

Morillon & Chacon (2022), the first peer-reviewed treatment, find the in-sample fit is robust to early-assumption choices (not pure data-mining) and that dynamic out-of-sample accuracy improves over time
cons: Spurious regression / non-stationarity: both ln(price) and ln(SF) are non-stationary, trending series, so the high R² is the textbook artifact of regressing one trend on another. Without cointegration the coefficients and R² are statistically meaningless (Burger, Bitcoinwords/WORDS review; has been shown cointegration generally does not hold)
SF is a near-deterministic step function of time, so S2F is effectively price-regressed-on-time in disguise — it cannot distinguish scarcity from any other variable that trended up over 2010-2020

Demand-blind by construction: ignores adoption, liquidity, ETF flows, macro/real rates, regulation. Mises critique: scarcity (a subjective demand condition) is conflated with the mechanical SF ratio; price comes from marginal valuations, not a physical supply metric

Out-of-sample failure: PlanB's S2F/S2FX predicted >$100k for 2021-2022; BTC closed Nov-2021 ~$57k and bottomed <$16k in 2022. The model has traded materially below trend since 2021 (off by ~$130k at points). 'Floor model' walk-back further eroded credibility

Diminishing-returns problem: S2F implies a constant ~10x per halving forever (no decay), contradicting the clear empirical decay of BTC's growth rate (142%→65%→17%/yr) — the model is structurally too bullish at long horizons and its targets (e.g. $288k, $500k+, eventually multi-million) are unbounded
Even when the fit 'works', Morillon & Chacon show an S2F-timing strategy underperforms buy-and-hold — no economic value added
Says nothing about volatility or correlations — it is a price-level model only, so it cannot directly populate most CMA cells (vol, corr to equities/FI/TIPS/gold)
S2FX 'phase transitions' have only ~4-6 data clusters; fitting a power law through 4 points (plus gold/silver) is gross overfitting and 'has not been replicated or reviewed' per PlanB himself

cited_outputs.appreciation_nominal: Not published as an annualized rate; S2F/S2FX publishes price-level targets implying ~10x market value per halving (~78%/yr compounded). Specific targets: ~$55k (post-2020 halving, original S2F) and $288k (S2FX next cluster, 2020-2024); later PlanB commentary cites $500k+. None realized on schedule.
cited_outputs.appreciation_real: n/a (source silent — model is nominal-USD price only; no inflation adjustment)
cited_outputs.volatility: n/a (source silent — S2F/S2FX is a deterministic price-level model and makes no volatility statement)
cited_outputs.corr_gold: n/a as a correlation; but the S2FX thesis explicitly places BTC on the SAME scarcity regression line as gold (gold SF~62, silver SF~22), asserting a structural co-valuation rather than a measured correlation. (Morillon & Chacon report S2F R²≈0.95; S2FX R²≈0.997 — fit, not correlation to other assets.)

synthesized_outputs.appreciation_nominal: ~12-18%/yr (judgment, not a model output). S2F's own logic says ~10x/halving (~78%/yr) forever, but that is the model's central flaw; imposing the empirically-required appreciation decay (realized 142%→65%→17% over full/10y/5y windows) and the fact that BTC's SF will soon exceed gold's — removing the 'catch-up to gold' leg that powered past returns — collapses the forward rate to roughly a low-double-digit monetary-debasement-plus-marginal-adoption pace. I deliberately discount the model's literal targets ($288k-$500k+).
synthesized_outputs.appreciation_real: ~9-15%/yr real (subtracting ~2.5-3% long-run CPI). Reflects BTC as a maturing scarce asset whose excess return compresses toward a gold-like-but-higher store-of-value premium.
synthesized_outputs.volatility: ~55-60%/yr (judgment; S2F is silent, so anchored to realized trailing-5y/10y vol of 57%/69%). The floor sits AT realized ~57% — the sub-2yr ETF sample does not yet evidence compression below realized — with a defensible decade-average band of ~50-60%. Vol stays multiples of equities.
synthesized_outputs.corr_growth_eq: +0.45 to +0.60 (judgment; S2F is silent so anchored to realized trailing-5y corr of 0.56, which has risen as BTC institutionalized into risk-asset portfolios). Note this directly contradicts the model's 'pure scarcity, demand-independent' premise.
synthesized_outputs.corr_value_eq: +0.30 to +0.40 (judgment; realized trailing-5y 0.37)
synthesized_outputs.corr_fi_nominal: +0.15 to +0.25 (judgment; realized trailing-5y 0.19 — modestly positive via shared duration/liquidity sensitivity)
synthesized_outputs.corr_tips: +0.25 to +0.35 (judgment; realized trailing-5y 0.30; real-rate sensitivity shared with other long-duration stores of value)
synthesized_outputs.corr_gold: ~0.0-0.10 (judgment). S2FX bills BTC as 'digital scarcity' that should co-move with gold, but realized correlation is essentially zero (-0.01 full / +0.03 10y / +0.045 5y). I keep it in the 0.0-0.10 band, NOT the higher 'digital-gold' linkage the model implies. Internal contradiction worth naming: a scarcity thesis that says BTC absorbs gold's monetary role REQUIRES co-movement to justify the share transfer, yet the data shows none — you cannot simultaneously claim 'BTC takes gold's monetary share' and treat the near-zero realized gold correlation as comfortable. The honest read is that S2F's gold linkage is asserted, not measured.

approaches.rich_notes:
METHODOLOGY. Original S2F (PlanB, 2019): monthly data, OLS of ln(market value) on ln(SF). Reported fit ln(MV)=3.3·ln(SF)+14.6 → MV = e^14.6·SF^3.3, R²≈0.95, F-significance 2.3e-17. Because issuance halves ~every 4 years, SF roughly doubles each halving; exponent 3.3 → ~2^3.3 ≈ 10x market value per doubling. Post-2020-halving target ~$55k. S2FX (2020) 'removes time' and pools BTC with gold (SF~62) and silver (SF~22) plus four BTC monthly clusters interpreted as 'phase transitions'; reported R²≈0.997 across six points; next-cluster market value $5.5T → ~$288k/BTC at ~19M supply. PlanB himself flagged S2FX as 'a first step, not yet replicated or reviewed.'

HOW A CMA FALLS OUT. The model is a deterministic price-LEVEL forecaster: feed the known future SF path (2028/2032/2036 halvings) into the power law to get target prices, then back out an implied annualized appreciation. It is silent on volatility and on correlation to every other asset class — those cells cannot be populated from S2F at all and must be borrowed from realized data, which I do for the synthesized column.

THE CORE STATISTICAL INDICTMENT (this is the consensus academic/quant verdict, and I represent it as such, not as one side of a debate). Both ln(price) and ln(SF) are non-stationary I(1)-type trending series. Regressing one trend on another mechanically produces high R² and 'significant' coefficients with heavily autocorrelated residuals — the textbook spurious-regression result (Granger-Newbold). R² is not interpretable for non-stationary series. The defense is cointegration; multiple reviewers (Burger/Amdax via WORDS Bitcoin Journal Parts II & IV; numerous others) find cointegration generally does NOT hold, and that Engle-Granger/Johansen prerequisites are unmet. Crucially, SF is a near-deterministic step-function of TIME, so S2F is essentially 'price regressed on time' — it cannot identify scarcity as the cause versus any other quantity that trended up 2010-2020. PlanB failed to address serial correlation, which guts the predictive-power claim.

ECONOMIC INDICTMENT (Mises, Murphy & Newman 2022). The model conflates 'scarcity' (a subjective demand-side condition — insufficiency relative to wants) with the mechanical stock-to-flow RATIO. Price emerges from marginal buyers'/sellers' subjective valuations, not from a physical supply metric; there is 'no necessary relationship between price paid and physical supply.' They concede SF can bear on a money's QUALITY, but only insofar as actors subjectively value hardness — not as a deterministic price formula. So even the sympathetic Austrian read rejects S2F-as-price-model while granting S2F-as-monetary-narrative.

OUT-OF-SAMPLE FAILURE (decisive). S2F/S2FX 'worst case' ~$98k for Nov-2021; BTC closed ~$57k. 2022 model implied >$100k; BTC bottomed <$16k. Sustained sub-trend trade since 2021 (gap ~$130k at points; CryptoSlate/Protos). PlanB pivoted to a separate 'Floor Model' and walked back his own invalidation criterion — a classic unfalsifiability move. The peer-reviewed Morillon & Chacon (2022) is the most balanced source: in-sample robust and not pure data-mining, dynamic accuracy improves with data, BUT an S2F long/short timing strategy badly underperforms buy-and-hold — i.e., even if the level relationship has SOME signal, it adds no investable value.

DIMINISHING-RETURNS / DECAY (why this matters most for a 10-15yr CMA). S2F bakes in constant ~10x-per-halving growth with NO decay. The realized record flatly contradicts this: from this project's scripted empirical_anchor.json (Coinmetrics BRRNY monthly), nominal annualized appreciation is 142% full-window (2010-2026), 65% trailing-10y, 17% trailing-5y; vol 103%→69%→57%. The growth rate is clearly decaying as the asset matures and as base effects bite. A naive S2F CMA would extrapolate the level (huge) rather than the decaying rate (modest) — the single biggest reason not to use S2F output as a forward CMA. My synthesized nominal 12-18% extrapolates the DECAY curve and additionally removes the 'catch-up to gold's SF' tailwind (BTC's SF will exceed gold's within ~2 halvings, so the scarcity-premium re-rating that drove past returns largely exhausts).

CORRELATION NOTE. The S2FX thesis structurally predicts BTC should be valued on the same scarcity line as gold, implying high gold co-movement. Realized gold correlation is ~0 (-0.01 full / +0.03 10y / +0.045 5y). Meanwhile the correlation S2F denies should exist — to growth equities — is the one that has RISEN most (0.26→0.36→0.56), because real-world BTC trades as a liquidity-sensitive risk asset, not a demand-independent scarcity token. This is direct empirical evidence against the model's premise, and I weight the realized data over the model's implication in the synthesized correlations.

BOTTOM LINE. Treat S2F/S2FX as a NARRATIVE about monetary hardness, not as a CMA engine. Its only genuinely useful input — the deterministic, zero-error future SF path — is real, but the mapping from SF to price is spurious, demand-blind, decay-blind, and has failed out of sample. Use it (if at all) to justify a structural debasement-hedge premium in the qualitative thesis, never to set the appreciation number; borrow vol and all correlations from realized data.

issues: S2FX exponent inconsistency (minor, not an error): the research attributes exponent 3.3 to the ORIGINAL S2F (ln MV = 3.3 ln SF + 14.6, R2~0.95) and the 0.997 R2 to S2FX. Correct. But PlanB's published S2FX cross-asset fit is MV = exp(12.76)*SF^4.1167 — exponent ~4.17, not 3.3. The research never states the S2FX exponent, so it avoids the error, but the casual reader may carry 3.3 across to the cross-asset model. The ~10x/halving arithmetic (2^3.3) is tied to the original S2F exponent and is correct for that model only.

The $288k target is the 2020-2024 cluster value (the cycle that just elapsed), not a still-forward 'next-cluster' target. rich_notes phrases it as 'next-cluster market value $5.5T -> ~$288k' which was accurate framing at PlanB's 2020 publication date but reads as forward-looking out of context. Should be dated explicitly.

Out-of-sample numbers are directionally correct and well-known but lightly sourced: 'worst case ~$98k Nov-2021', 'BTC closed ~$57k', 'bottomed <$16k 2022', '~$130k gap'. The $57k Nov-2021 close and <$16k Nov-2022 bottom are accurate. The exact '$98k worst case' and '~$130k off' figures come from Protos/CryptoSlate reporting, not a primary regression output — fine as reportage but they are secondary, not model-stated.

The 'spurious regression / cointegration generally does not hold' claim is asserted as 'consensus academic verdict.' This is well-supported (Burger/WORDS, multiple reviewers) but it is worth flagging that Morillon & Chacon — the ONE peer-reviewed source — did NOT fully endorse the spurious-regression dismissal; they found in-sample robustness and improving dynamic accuracy. The research does represent both, but the rich_notes 'BOTTOM LINE' leans harder on dismissal than the single peer-reviewed source supports. Balanced overall, but the peer-reviewed nuance shouldn't be flattened.

Missing critique: the research omits the 'free parameter / no error bars' point and the survivorship/look-ahead issue specific to S2FX's 6-point fit, beyond calling it 'overfitting.' It also omits the strongest single academic refutation framing — that S2F cannot be falsified once PlanB substitutes a 'floor model,' which it mentions but does not tie to Popperian unfalsifiability as a named defect. Minor; the substance is present.

Round-2 correction (corr_gold/vol): Gold-corr re-centered from 0-0.15 to 0.0-0.10 with the TAM/co-movement contradiction made explicit; vol floor raised from 45% to ~57% (realized trailing-5y) since ETF-era compression below realized is not yet evidenced.
verdict.corrections: Add the S2FX cross-asset exponent (~4.17) explicitly so the 3.3-vs-4.17 distinction between original-S2F and S2FX is unambiguous, and note the ~10x/halving step derives from the original-S2F 3.3 exponent. Date the $288k target as the 2020-2024 cluster (already-elapsed), not a forward target. Keep the synthesized appreciation at ~12-18% nominal / ~9-15% real — these are defensible and correctly subordinate the model's literal targets to the realized decay curve (142%->65%->17%), which matches the scripted anchor exactly. Keep vol ~45-55% (anchored to realized 57%/69%) and all correlations as stated: realized gold corr ~0 (-0.011/0.033/0.045), growth-eq 0.26/0.36/0.56, value-eq 5y 0.367, FI 5y 0.192, TIPS 5y 0.301 — all reproduce the anchor file verbatim, no change needed. Soften the 'consensus' framing slightly to acknowledge Morillon-Chacon's partial in-sample defense rather than implying unanimous academic rejection.

approaches.name: Metcalfe's Law Network-Value (NVM)
approaches.description: This approach treats Bitcoin as a payment/communication network whose fair value scales with a power of the number of active users (wallets/addresses), per Metcalfe's Law (V proportional to n^2) or its generalizations (n*log(n) Odlyzko; or an empirically estimated exponent near 1.7). Price = (network-value function of users) / (coin supply), where supply follows the known issuance schedule (Peterson fits a Gompertz curve). A 10-15yr CMA falls out indirectly: you forecast long-run S-curve user adoption (which decelerates as the network saturates), apply the chosen Metcalfe exponent to get terminal network value, divide by terminal supply, and annualize the implied price path. Because both user growth and the per-user value multiple compress as adoption matures, the model mechanically produces decaying — not constant — forward appreciation. The relative-valuation variants (Kalichkin NVM, Wheatley-Sornette MMV) are NOT return forecasters; they only flag over/undervaluation vs current network activity and are used to time bubbles, not to set a CMA.
key_drivers: Number of active users / non-zero-balance addresses / wallets (the network size n)
Metcalfe exponent on n: classical n^2 vs Odlyzko n*log(n) vs empirically-fit ~1.7
Adoption S-curve / saturation: logistic or Gompertz user-growth path that decelerates over time (Sornette: ~35% -> 21% annual user growth over 5yr)
Coin supply schedule (Gompertz/known halving issuance) as the denominator turning network value into price
Velocity / transactional utility assumption embedded in the per-user value constant
Mean-reversion of the market-to-Metcalfe (MMV/NVM) ratio for relative timing, not level
pros: Grounds value in an observable, hard-to-fake fundamental (on-chain active users) rather than pure price extrapolation or sentiment
Parsimonious and falsifiable: a single network-size driver plus a known supply schedule; Peterson reports very high in-sample fit (R^2 ~0.93-0.95)
Naturally generates appreciation DECAY: as adoption saturates the S-curve, both user growth and value-per-user compress, so the model does not assume a constant high return forever
Relative-value variants (NVM, MMV) have demonstrated some ex-ante use flagging bubble peaks (Wheatley-Sornette identified 4 over-valuations; LPPLS bracketed crash timing)
Provides an economic mechanism (network effects) that is at least theoretically tied to utility, unlike scarcity-only models (S2F) that ignore demand entirely
cons: The headline statistical fit is largely SPURIOUS: price and active-users are both non-stationary trending series; high R^2 from log-log OLS does not survive proper time-series controls. Civitarese (2018) finds the series do NOT cointegrate and cannot reject reverse causality (price drives wallet creation, not vice versa); the Glasgow/Ledger critique shows the strong positive relationships vanish once autocorrelation and non-stationarity are handled.

Exponent is unidentified and chosen ad hoc: n^2 vs n*log(n) vs ~1.7 give wildly different terminal values, and Wheatley-Sornette show forcing the classic n^2 fits significantly WORSE than ~1.7 (p<1e-16). The CMA is highly sensitive to an arbitrary parameter.

User/address metrics are a crude, manipulable proxy: total addresses overcount (one user holds many; exchanges custody millions); active-address counts are gamed by consolidation, Lightning/L2 migration off-chain, and ETF/custodial adoption that creates ZERO new on-chain addresses — breaking the network-size signal post-2021/2024.

It is a relative/timing tool masquerading as a level forecast: Kalichkin himself states NVM forecasts CORRECTIONS not appreciation direction; using it to derive a 10-15yr return is a category error the marketing layer routinely commits.

Long-run extrapolation is explicitly unreliable — Wheatley-Sornette call long-term predictions 'effectively meaningless' because model uncertainty dominates. Practitioner forecasts ($1.5M/2035 etc.) launder a fragile in-sample fit into a precise CMA the underlying econometrics do not support.
Post-2021 structural break: institutional/ETF holdings, treasury companies and custodial concentration decouple price from on-chain active users, the model's sole driver.

cited_outputs.corr_gold: n/a (source silent) — Metcalfe literature models BTC purely from network size and is silent on cross-asset correlation

synthesized_outputs.appreciation_nominal: ~10-14%/yr (JUDGMENT, not a computed stat). Under Metcalfe logic the driver is active-user growth times a saturating per-user multiple. Realized BTC appreciation decayed 142%->65%->17% as it matured; an S-curve forces continued decay. Mid-single-digit-to-low-teens forward user CAGR, with the value-per-user multiple flat-to-compressing as on-chain activity migrates to L2/custodial/ETF, lands a 10-15yr nominal CMA near the low end of the realized-decay path (~10-14%), well below the practitioner ~31% which over-extrapolates an in-sample fit.

Judgment, consistent with the model's emphasis on recurrent non-stationary bubbles, with the floor anchored at realized trailing-5y vol (no compression below realized yet evidenced).
synthesized_outputs.corr_growth_eq: ~+0.30 to +0.45. Network adoption is a risk-on/liquidity-sensitive driver, so BTC behaves like a high-beta growth/tech proxy. Judgment.

synthesized_outputs.corr_tips: ~0.0 to +0.10. No real-yield mechanism in a network-size model; effectively orthogonal. Judgment.
synthesized_outputs.corr_gold: ~0.0-0.10. The Metcalfe model implies no structural gold link at all; realized BTC-gold co-movement is ~0 (-0.01 full / +0.045 5y). I hold it at the bottom of the 0.0-0.15 band and explicitly reject the digital-gold reading — a network-value thesis gives no mechanism forcing gold co-movement, and the data supplies none.

approaches.rich_notes:
METHODOLOGY. Core Metcalfe claim: value of a network proportional to n^2 (number of users). Applied to BTC, price = f(active users) / supply. Peterson (2018, SSRN 3078248; Alternative Investment Analyst Review 7:9-18) models demand via number of bitcoin wallets and supply via a Gompertz sigmoid issuance curve, reporting an exceptionally high fit (R^2 ~0.93-0.95). His later practitioner work ('Lowest Price Forward / Never Look Back Price', 'Bitcoin Spreads Like a Virus') adds a square-root-time / Gompertz adoption layer and produces dated price targets: ~$100K by Jan-2024, $1M by Mar-2028, and most relevantly a ~$1.5M-by-2035 Metcalfe target (~31% 10yr CAGR off ~$100K). THESE TARGETS ARE MARKETING/PRACTITIONER OUTPUT, not the peer-reviewed result — represent them as such.

GENERALIZED METCALFE (Wheatley, Sornette et al., Royal Society Open Science 2019, doi:10.1098/rsos.180538; arXiv 1803.05663 — note the seed brief mislabels this 'PLoS ONE', the correct venue is Royal Society Open Science). Key quantitative results: log-log regression ln(p)=alpha+beta*ln(u) gives beta=1.69 (SE 0.0076), alpha=1.51, R^2=0.95 over 2,782 daily obs (Jul-2010 to Feb-2018). Crucially forcing beta=2.0 (classic Metcalfe) fits SIGNIFICANTLY WORSE (p<1e-16) — so the 'square law' is itself rejected in favor of a lower exponent. They build a Market-to-Metcalfe Value ratio MMV = p * e^-3 * u^2 (using their support specification) and identify >=4 historical episodes where market cap massively exceeded fundamental network value (bubbles). They combine this with the LPPLS (log-periodic power-law singularity) model to bracket crash timing ex-ante. User-growth modeling predicts DECELERATION: annual user growth shrinking ~35%->21% over five years, ~2.6M active users by 2023. Authors' own caveat (quote, paraphrased): long-term predictions are 'effectively meaningless' because model uncertainty dominates parameter uncertainty — a direct warning against using this for a 10-15yr CMA level.

RELATIVE-VALUE VARIANTS. Kalichkin's NVM (Cryptolab Capital, 2018) explicitly sidesteps choosing an exponent by bounding network value between Odlyzko n*log(n) (lower) and Metcalfe n^2 (upper) and normalizing actual NV between them: NVM = (Actual NV - LowerBound)/(UpperBound - LowerBound), ranging -1 (undervalued) to +1 (overvalued), driven off Daily Active Addresses. KEY: Kalichkin states NVM is a RELATIVE valuation/correction signal, NOT a long-run appreciation forecaster — 'High NVM suggests Bitcoin is overvalued... compared to the Metcalfe NV estimation,' and even high NVM may reflect growing DAA not inevitable decline. So any CMA built on NVM/MMV is a misuse.

THE SKEPTICAL CASE (this is the honest center of gravity). (1) Civitarese (2018, SSRN 3107895): cointegration test between price and adjusted wallet connections — the series do NOT cointegrate, REJECTING Metcalfe's law as a long-run equilibrium; cannot reject reverse causation (BTC returns drive new wallets, not wallets drive price). (2) Glasgow/Ledger critique (eprints.gla.ac.uk/298705, 2021): prior strong positive Metcalfe results are SPURIOUS — they regress non-stationary trending series with simple log transforms, ignoring autocorrelation and non-stationarity; with proper controls the relationship 'does not survive proper econometric specification,' and some prior studies cherry-pick by excluding poorly-fitting windows or use crude total-address proxies instead of non-zero-balance addresses. (3) General point: high R^2 between two trending I(1) series is the textbook spurious-regression trap (Granger-Newbold). So the in-sample 0.95 R^2 is close to meaningless for out-of-sample/forward inference.

STRUCTURAL BREAK / PROXY DECAY. The single driver (on-chain active users) is increasingly decoupled from price post-2021 and especially post-2024: spot-ETF and custodial/treasury adoption add demand and price with ZERO new on-chain active addresses; Lightning/L2 and exchange-internal transfers move activity off the base layer; address counts are gamed by consolidation. This breaks the network-size signal exactly over the forward CMA window, biasing any naive Metcalfe forecast.

WHY MY SYNTHESIZED CMA IS LOWER THAN THE PRACTITIONER NUMBER. The model's own internal logic (saturating S-curve user growth, decelerating from ~35% toward low-20s% and continuing down) plus the realized appreciation-decay path (142->65->17%/yr) imply forward nominal appreciation in the ~10-14% range over 10-15yr, not ~31%. The ~31% practitioner figure assumes the in-sample multiple holds and ignores both the saturation the model itself predicts and the address-proxy break. I therefore anchor to the LOW end of the decay path. Correlations: the Metcalfe literature is SILENT on every cross-asset correlation (it models BTC purely from network size), so all correlation figures are my own judgment, framed by treating BTC as a high-beta, liquidity-sensitive adoption asset — modest positive to growth equities, near-zero to value/FI/TIPS, modestly positive (not high) to gold, deliberately undercutting the digital-gold thesis which this model does not support.

CITATION HYGIENE. approaches.name: Network Value-to-Transactions (NVT) Ratio
approaches.description: NVT treats Bitcoin like an equity P/E: network value (market cap) in the numerator, daily USD on-chain transaction volume in the denominator as a proxy for the network's "earnings"/utility throughput. The thesis is that fair value is whatever multiple of settlement activity the market is willing to pay, and that extreme NVT readings mean-revert — high NVT flags overvaluation/tops, low NVT flags undervaluation/bottoms. It is a relative-value and timing/mean-reversion framework, not a discounted-cashflow or supply-scarcity model. A 10-15yr CMA does not fall cleanly out of NVT at all: NVT produces no native long-horizon expected return. To force one, you must assume NVT mean-reverts to some equilibrium band and that real on-chain settlement value (the denominator) compounds at some growth rate over the horizon; expected appreciation then ≈ growth in transaction value ± any drift in the equilibrium multiple. Because on-chain throughput is a maturing, decelerating series (and is increasingly leaking off-chain to L2/exchanges/ETF custody), the honest NVT-consistent CMA extrapolates BTC's appreciation decay downward, not its historical level.
key_drivers: Daily on-chain USD transaction volume (the denominator / 'earnings' proxy) — its level and growth rate
Network value / market cap (numerator)
The equilibrium NVT band the market assigns and any secular drift in it
Quality of the transaction-volume measure: raw vs adjusted (stripping change outputs, self-spends, mixer/exchange-internal repetition — Coin Metrics finds raw overstates economic volume by ~3.3x)
Smoothing choice: NVT Signal (NVTS) uses a 90-day MA of volume to make the ratio a leading top/bottom indicator
Share of economic activity that stays on-chain vs migrating to Lightning/L2, centralized-exchange internal ledgers, and ETF custody (off-chain leakage degrades the denominator over time)
Velocity (NVT is effectively inverse monetary velocity), which reflects HODL vs spend behavior
pros: Intuitive analogue to a familiar equity multiple (P/E), making it communicable to traditional investors
Grounds valuation in an observable, auditable on-chain fundamental (settlement throughput) rather than pure price/sentiment
Has empirically bracketed several historical tops (high NVT) and bottoms (low NVT) ex-post, and NVT Signal added some lead time as a smoothed timing overlay
Cheap and transparent — computable from public blockchain data; Coin Metrics/Glassnode publish adjusted versions that materially clean the denominator
Conceptually forces a discipline that BTC's value should bear some relationship to its use as a settlement network, a useful counterweight to pure scarcity narratives
cons: Not a return model. NVT is a mean-reversion/timing ratio; it yields no native long-horizon expected appreciation, so any 10-15yr CMA is bolted-on assumption (denominator growth + multiple drift), not output of the framework.

Denominator is badly contaminated and structurally decaying. On-chain volume is inflated by change outputs/self-spends/mixers (raw overstates ~3.3x) AND increasingly understated as real activity moves to Lightning/L2, exchange-internal settlement, and ETF custody. Both errors are large and time-varying — the proxy for 'earnings' is breaking.

No stable equilibrium / non-comparable across regimes. Even the publishers (Glassnode) warn 2013 NVT is not one-to-one with 2021 NVT; the 'fair' band drifts, so absolute readings can't anchor valuation.

Documented in-sample failure post-2021. In 2025 NVT gave contradictory signals within one cycle (overvalued ~58 in April pre-rally; 'undervalued' near $120k in October). It is part of the broadly-failed 2024-26 cohort of on-chain top indicators (alongside MVRV Z, Pi Cycle, S2F).

Tiny sample / curve-fit risk. Calibrated on only 3-4 halving cycles; like S2F and naive Metcalfe, NVT-based valuation is fragile to regime change and lacks out-of-sample validation — academically these on-chain 'fundamentals' show weak, unstable predictive power for returns.
Circularity: market cap (numerator) is price; using a price-driven ratio to value price embeds reflexivity, especially when speculation inflates both price and on-chain churn simultaneously.
Institutionalization (ETFs) decouples price from on-chain activity entirely — the marginal buyer never touches the chain, severing the link NVT depends on.

approaches.rich_notes:
METHODOLOGY. NVT = Network Value (market cap, USD) / Daily on-chain transaction volume (USD). Introduced by Willy Woo (2017), explicitly framed as 'Bitcoin's P/E ratio': on-chain transfer value substitutes for earnings as a proxy for network utility. NVT is technically the inverse of monetary velocity. Interpretation (Glassnode/Coin Metrics): high NVT = market cap outrunning utilization → overvaluation/top; low NVT = throughput outrunning price → undervaluation/bottom; constant NVT = sustainable trend. NVT SIGNAL (NVTS), refined by Dmitry Kalichkin on Woo's work, replaces raw daily volume with a 90-day moving average to damp denominator noise and turn the ratio into a leading top/bottom timing indicator.

DENOMINATOR PROBLEM (central, fatal to a CMA). The 'earnings' proxy is doubly broken. (1) OVERSTATEMENT: raw on-chain volume is inflated by change outputs, self-spends, mixers, and exchange-internal repetition — Coin Metrics/Fidelity find raw overstates true economic volume by ~3.3x; adjusted series (TxTfrValAdjUSD: strips obvious change UTXOs and UTXOs respent within ~4 blocks) are required. (2) UNDERSTATEMENT/LEAKAGE: real activity increasingly never hits the base chain — Lightning/L2, centralized-exchange internal ledgers, and (post-2024) ETF custody. So the denominator simultaneously contains noise and misses signal, and the mix changes over time. Glassnode itself states 2013 NVT is 'unlikely to be one-to-one' with 2021 — i.e., no stable equilibrium multiple, which is exactly what you'd need for a valuation anchor.

WHY THIS IS NOT A CMA TOOL. NVT produces no expected return, vol, or correlation natively. It is a within-cycle mean-reversion/timing ratio. To extract a 10-15yr appreciation you must layer two assumptions: (a) NVT reverts to an equilibrium band, and (b) the denominator (real settlement value) compounds at rate g; then long-run price growth ≈ g ± drift in the multiple. Since on-chain settlement value is maturing AND leaking off-chain, the defensible g is low and decelerating — which is why the honest NVT-consistent CMA EXTRAPOLATES BTC's appreciation decay (142%→65%→17% across full/10y/5y windows) DOWNWARD, not its historical level. I therefore set nominal ~10-13%/yr, below the trailing-5y 17%.

DOCUMENTED FAILURE (be honest). NVT is in the cohort of on-chain top indicators that broke in the 2024-26 cycle. PANews (2026): in 2025 NVT gave contradictory signals within one cycle — flagged overvaluation (~58) in April before a major rally, then suggested undervaluation near $120k in October. Structural causes cited: L2/exchange-internal/ETF custody eroding the data foundation; institutional ETF flows decoupling price from on-chain activity; and the small-sample curve-fit problem (calibration on only 3-4 halving cycles → fragile to regime change). This parallels the academic rejection of naive S2F (purely supply-side, ignores demand, spurious cointegration with non-stationary trending series) and naive Metcalfe — NVT shares the same small-N, non-stationary, out-of-sample-unvalidated weakness, though it is at least grounded in an observable usage variable rather than pure scarcity.

CIRCULARITY/REFLEXIVITY. Numerator is market cap (price). Using a price-containing ratio to value price embeds reflexivity, acute when speculation simultaneously inflates price and on-chain churn (so NVT can stay 'fair' while both are in a bubble). RVT (Checkmate, 2019) swaps realized cap for market cap in the numerator to dampen day-to-day sentiment, a partial fix but inherits all denominator problems.

CORRELATION REASONING. The NVT literature is silent on cross-asset correlations (it is a single-asset on-chain tool, NOT a digital-gold or macro framework), so all synthesized correlations are baseline-anchored, not NVT-derived. I lean on the trailing-5y realized window (most relevant to a forward CMA, post-2010-2013 micro-cap distortion removed): growth-eq 0.56, value-eq 0.37, FI 0.19, TIPS 0.30, gold 0.045. Forward view: equity correlations stay elevated or rise as ETF/institutional ownership makes BTC trade as a long-duration risk asset; gold correlation kept low (0.05-0.20) — near-zero historically (full-window -0.01), with only mild upward drift from shared debasement-hedge demand, and crucially NVT supplies NO mechanism forcing BTC-gold co-movement.

BOTTOM LINE. NVT is a useful communicative relative-value/timing ratio with a genuine but degrading fundamental anchor (settlement throughput). As a basis for a 10-15yr CMA it is weak-to-unusable: no native return/vol/correlation output, a denominator that is both noisy and structurally decaying, no stable equilibrium, demonstrated in-cycle failure, and tiny-sample overfit. Any number it 'supports' is an analyst assumption wearing an on-chain costume.

issues: Minor internal inconsistency in the synthesized nominal: the note says it extrapolates the decay path 'below the trailing-5y 17% toward roughly nominal-GDP-plus-a-modest-monetization-premium,' yet lands on ~10-13%/yr, which is ABOVE the trailing-5y realized 17%? No — it is below 17%. But ~10-13% is well above US nominal GDP (~4-5%); the 'nominal-GDP-plus-modest-premium' descriptor implies ~7-9%, so the stated 10-13% range is at the higher end of its own logic. The range and the verbal anchor are slightly out of step. Defensible but should reconcile.

The April 2025 'overvalued ~58' reading cited from PANews appears to refer to the NVT Golden Cross (NVTS-derived oscillator), not the raw NVT ratio whose absolute values are far higher. The con bullet and rich_notes present it as plain 'NVT ~58,' which conflates two related-but-distinct metrics. The structural failure point is valid; the metric label is imprecise.

The synthesis claims the honest NVT-consistent CMA 'extrapolates the decay downward' to below trailing-5y, but then sets vol (45-55%) and correlations essentially AT or only modestly below the trailing-5y realized levels — i.e., it applies aggressive mean-reversion to the return but near-flat extrapolation to vol/corr. That asymmetry is reasonable (NVT says nothing about vol/corr) but is an analyst choice, not NVT-derived, and the note should be even more explicit that ALL of vol/corr are pure baseline carry-forward, not 'NVT-consistent.'

Real return of ~7-10% assumes ~3% inflation against nominal 10-13%; arithmetic is consistent (13-3=10, 10-3=7). No error, but pairing the TOP of the nominal range with the TOP of the real range double-counts the optimistic case slightly; fine as a band.

No academic critique is materially missing for NVT specifically. One could add that NVT has never been formally validated as a return predictor in peer-reviewed work (the literature treats it as a practitioner heuristic, not a tested factor) — the note gestures at this ('out-of-sample-unvalidated') but could cite that the academic on-chain-factor literature finds these signals subsumed by momentum/liquidity.

approaches.name: Cost-of-Production / Mining-Cost Floor
approaches.description: Models BTC as a "virtual commodity" whose value is anchored to the marginal cost of mining it. Hayes (2015, 2019) derives a break-even price P* = E_day / (BTC_mined_per_day), where daily energy cost E_day = (electricity $/kWh × 24h × ASIC efficiency in W/GH × hashrate) and BTC/day = θ·β·ρ/δ (block reward β, hashrate ρ, difficulty δ). In a competitive mining market, miners produce until marginal cost equals price, so the cost of production is theorized as a lower bound (floor) around which the market price "gravitates." A 10-15yr CMA does NOT fall cleanly out of this: the model produces a current floor level, not an expected return. To get a forward appreciation number you must forecast the trajectory of the floor itself — i.e., project how the four block-reward halvings, secular ASIC-efficiency gains, and the electricity-price/hashrate path push the per-coin cost up over a decade — and then assume price tracks that floor. That forecast is highly indeterminate, which is the approach's core weakness as a CMA tool.
key_drivers: Block reward β (halves every ~210k blocks / ~4yr: 6.25→3.125 BTC in Apr-2024, →1.5625 ~2028) — mechanically DOUBLES per-coin cost at each halving, the main upward driver
Mining difficulty δ / network hashrate ρ — self-adjusting every 2016 blocks to hold ~10-min block time; rises with miner entry, raising cost
ASIC energy efficiency (W/GH, J/TH) — secular technological improvement (500 W/GH in 2010-13 → <0.02 J/GH today) is the main DOWNWARD driver, partially offsetting halvings
Electricity price ($/kWh) — JPMorgan: a 1¢/kWh change moves the production-cost estimate by ~$4,300/BTC; sensitivity mechanically doubled post-2024 halving
Competitive-market marginal-cost-equals-price assumption — the load-bearing economic premise that turns a cost into a 'floor'
Difficulty-adjustment feedback loop — stabilizes cost (counteracts efficiency-driven decline) but also makes cost endogenous to price
pros: Grounds BTC in a measurable real-world input (energy), giving a concrete, refreshable dollar number rather than pure narrative — appealing to commodity-style investors
Hayes (2019) finds the marginal cost of production has statistically significant explanatory power for price; pre-2017 the market price visibly oscillated around the model price

The halving schedule is fully deterministic, so the UPWARD ratchet in per-coin cost is one of the few genuinely forecastable mechanisms in BTC valuation — gives a non-arbitrary reason to expect the floor (and thus a price tracking it) to rise over a decade
Widely used as a practitioner sentiment/valuation overlay (JPMorgan, Glassnode, MacroMicro publish a live production-cost series as an over/under-valuation gauge), so it has real desk adoption
Provides an intuitive miner-capitulation signal: when price < cash cost, weak miners shut down, difficulty falls, and the system mean-reverts — a real, observable dynamic
cons: CIRCULARITY (fatal): supply is price-INELASTIC (predetermined issuance schedule), so when price falls miners exit, difficulty drops, and cost falls to FOLLOW price. Causality runs price→cost, not cost→price. Bernstein (2026): 'the price of bitcoin is as flexible as a blob of silly putty.' This breaks the 'floor' logic that the whole CMA rests on.

The 'floor' is empirically breached in BOTH directions: price traded ~20-40% BELOW production cost for months in Oct-2022/FTX and again in Feb-2026 (price ~$70k vs cost ~$87k), while in bull runs price ran multiples ABOVE cost. So it is neither a floor nor a ceiling — at best a loose attractor.

Hayes HIMSELF cautions against imputing an intrinsic value from it: 'extreme volatility and frequent market price fluctuations… could make identifying such an intrinsic value meaningless in application.' The author disowns the strong CMA use.

Post-2017 structural break: the visible pre-2017 oscillation around the model price decoupled; with ETFs, treasury buyers, and financialization, price detached from cost. The naive model does not survive the modern regime.

Indeterminate as a return forecast: the cost floor's future level depends on the hashrate AND efficiency paths, which are themselves driven by price and AI/data-center competition for chips and power (JPMorgan notes miners now decoupling toward AI) — so the 'forecast' smuggles in a price assumption.

Tells you nothing about correlations, volatility, or risk premia — it is a level/anchor model, not a distributional CMA. All return-moment outputs must be borrowed from realized data or another framework.

Terminal contradiction: once issuance ends (~2140) there is NO marginal cost of production, yet BTC would presumably still have value — the framework cannot value the asset in the limit it is converging toward (Bernstein).

approaches.rich_notes:
CORE MODEL (Hayes 2015, equations verbatim from NSSR WP 05/2015): BTC/day* = [(β·ρ)/(δ·2^32)]·sec_hr·hr_day, rewritten BTC/day* = θ·(β·ρ)/δ with θ = 24·2^32/3600 = 28,633,115.30667. Daily energy cost E_day = (price_kWh · 24 · W_per_GHs · GH/1000). Break-even/objective price p* = E_day / (BTC/day*) (Eq. 4). Worked example (Mar-2015): 11.5¢/kWh, 0.95 J/GH, 1 TH/s rig → $2.622/day cost, 0.010604 BTC/day at difficulty 47.4bn → p* = $247.27/BTC vs market ~$255-260 — 'surprisingly close.' He also gives inverse solves: break-even electricity (Eq.5), break-even difficulty (Eq.6), break-even efficiency (Eq.7).

HAYES'S OWN HALVING INSIGHT (the only clean CMA mechanism): block reward halves every ~4yr (50→25 in 2012, →12.5 in 2016, etc.). Holding difficulty constant, halving β cuts BTC/day in half, so p* roughly DOUBLES. In his example, substituting 12.5 for 25 sends break-even from $247 to $494.54 'all else constant.' Counterweight: real-world efficiency gains (he cites Garcia et al.: avg 500 W/GH over 2010-13; best ASICs 0.50-0.60 W/GH in 2015; today <0.02 J/GH) push the floor DOWN. The difficulty-adjustment mechanism 'stabilize[s] the predicted decrease in production cost,' and halvings 'counteract the decreasing tendency.' Net direction over a decade is genuinely ambiguous — which is exactly why this is a weak CMA generator.

AUTHOR'S DISCLAIMER (critical, must not be laundered): Hayes writes 'While it may be tempting to objectify these results to impute a true intrinsic value for bitcoin, I would caution against making such a leap. Even if the models… can theoretically determine an intrinsic value, extreme volatility and frequent market price fluctuations… could make identifying such an intrinsic value meaningless in application.' The originator explicitly disowns the strong floor/CMA use.

CIRCULARITY / DIRECTION-OF-CAUSALITY (the decisive critique):
- Bernstein (2026): 'traditional ideas about production costs don't fit bitcoin' because supply follows 'a predetermined schedule, unaffected by price fluctuations.' Difficulty adjusts every ~2016 blocks to hold total issuance constant regardless of price, so when price falls and high-cost miners exit, the survivors get a larger share — 'the price of bitcoin is as flexible as a blob of silly putty.' Conclusion: causality runs price→cost. Plus the terminal contradiction — after issuance ends (~2140) there is NO marginal cost yet BTC presumably retains value, so a cost model cannot value the limiting asset.
- BSIC (2021): 'the cost of production is impacted by the price of bitcoin, which makes this valuation approach less compelling.' Both Hayes and the generic CoP model are 'heavily dependent on assumptions' about the global hardware pool.

EMPIRICAL FLOOR FAILURE (kills the strong 'floor' claim):
- Oct 2022–Nov 2022 (FTX): production total cost ran WELL ABOVE spot; price below cost from ~Oct 6, 2022; miners hit highest selling pressure in ~5yr, capitulation drove price further down — the 'floor' did not hold.
- Feb 2026: CoinDesk — 'Bitcoin trades 20% below its production cost' (~$70k price vs ~$87k cost) as miner stress intensified; all-in cost ~$137,800 (incl. depreciation/financing/SBC) per late-2025 estimates. So price sustains BELOW cost for extended periods.
- Conversely, 2017 and 2021 bull runs saw price multiples ABOVE cost. So the relationship is a loose, lagging attractor — not a bound.

PRACTITIONER ADOPTION (why it still matters): JPMorgan (Panigirtzoglou) folds the Cambridge CBECI into a production-cost model treated as 'the lower boundary of Bitcoin's price range' (miners 'sell at or above this level'). Their cost series: ~$21k → revised ~$18k (2023, post-CBECI methodology change), ~$36-40k post-Apr-2024 halving, ~$92-94k late-2025, projected ~$180k post-2028 halving; sensitivity ~$4,300/BTC per 1¢/kWh, which DOUBLED post-2024 halving. Glassnode and MacroMicro publish live production-cost / over-under-valuation dashboards. JPMorgan itself now flags miners DECOUPLING from BTC price as they pivot to AI/HPC compute — further eroding the cost-price link.

POST-2017 STRUCTURAL BREAK: pre-2017 the market price visibly oscillated around the model price (the empirical support in Hayes 2019); financialization (ETFs, corporate treasuries, leverage) detached price from cost thereafter. Any naive cost-floor CMA fitted to pre-2017 data is out-of-regime.

GOLD/DIGITAL-GOLD ANGLE: the CoP literature frames BTC as a mined 'virtual commodity' (explicit gold analogy — both have a marginal cost of extraction and a hard/known supply schedule). This is the cleanest intellectual bridge to the digital-gold thesis WITHIN this family. BUT the analogy is asymmetric: gold supply is price-ELASTIC (higher price → more marginal mines open → more output), which makes gold's cost curve a genuine soft floor; BTC supply is price-INELASTIC (fixed issuance), so the same mechanism does not operate, and the gold-style floor argument does not transfer. None of the CoP sources publishes a BTC-gold correlation — that has to be supplied from realized data or the digital-gold/store-of-value literature, not from this family.

CMA BOTTOM LINE: This approach yields a LEVEL (a current cost-implied price), not a return distribution. To force a 10-15yr CMA you must (a) project the cost-floor trajectory (deterministic halvings up, uncertain efficiency/power/hashrate down) and (b) assume price tracks it — assumption (b) is empirically false in both directions. My synthesized ~6-9% nominal / ~3-6% real is a deliberately conservative read of 'price grows with the production-cost floor of a maturing mining industry,' consistent with the realized appreciation DECAY (142→65→17%/yr) rather than the historical level, and explicitly a judgment, not a computed statistic. Volatility and all five correlations are NOT outputs of this model and are marked as judgments anchored to realized BTC behavior with a maturing-asset haircut.

issues: Minor dating error: the $137,800 all-in cost is Q2 2025 (public miners, CryptoRank/cash-cost $74,600 + depreciation/SBC), not 'late-2025 estimates.' The text inconsistently dates it. Verified figure is Q2 2025.

Citation #2 venue precision: Hayes (2019) 'Bitcoin price and its marginal cost of production' is in Applied Economics Letters 26(7); the arxiv.org/abs/1805.07610 link is the preprint, not the journal of record. Harmless but the link/venue pairing is loose.

The synthesized appreciation logic contains a subtle internal tension the notes half-acknowledge but the headline number papers over: a STRICT cost-floor read says price growth = cost-floor growth, but the cons section correctly establishes the floor does NOT bind (breached both directions, causality price->cost). So the 6-9% nominal is really borrowing the realized-appreciation-DECAY trajectory and bolting it onto a cost-floor narrative — it is not actually derived from the cost model. This is disclosed ('JUDGMENT, not a computed stat') but the '~+18%/yr gross from two halvings clawed back by efficiency' arithmetic gives a false sense of model-derivation.

corr_gold synthesized at ~0.15-0.35 is on the high side given the scripted baseline anchor is ~0 gold correlation. The note's own reasoning (BTC supply price-INELASTIC vs gold price-ELASTIC, so the gold-cost-floor analogy does NOT transfer; gold's low realized BTC correlation) argues for pulling the midpoint toward ~0.05-0.20, not 0.15-0.35.

Missing academic critique: the model's electricity-cost input is a single global average, but mining is dominated by miners paying FAR below grid price (stranded/curtailed power, flared gas, sub-1c/kWh PPAs). The 'marginal' miner cost is unobservable and the published 'production cost' overstates the true marginal cost — a well-known measurement critique not surfaced in the cons.

Missing critique: difficulty adjusts only every ~2016 blocks (~2 weeks) with a 4x clamp per adjustment, so the 'instant mean-reversion / miner-capitulation signal' in the pros is materially lagged and damped — the self-correction is slow enough that price can sit below cost for months (which the cons separately confirm empirically), partially undercutting the pro.

Volatility synthesis (~50-65%) is reasonable but the note frames the cost model as IMPLYING lower vol ('the floor is a slow-moving anchor'); since the cons establish price detaches freely from the floor, the cost model implies essentially NOTHING about vol — the 50-65% is purely a realized-data haircut and should be labeled as such rather than partly attributed to the model.
Round-2 correction (corr_gold/vol): Gold-corr re-centered from 0.15-0.35 to 0.0-0.10 with the commodity-analogy contradiction made explicit; vol floor lifted from 50% to ~57%.
verdict.corrections: Date the $137,800 all-in cost as Q2 2025 (public miners, incl. depreciation/SBC), not 'late-2025.' Tighten Hayes-2019 citation to 'Applied Economics Letters 26(7), 2019' with the arxiv link flagged as preprint. Pull corr_gold midpoint down to ~0.05-0.20 (closer to the ~0 realized/scripted baseline) given the explicitly non-transferable gold analogy. State plainly that the 6-9% nominal / 3-6% real is imported from the realized-appreciation-decay path, NOT derived from the cost model (the model yields a level, not a return — keep this framing in the headline, not just the footnote). Note the single-global-average electricity input overstates true marginal cost (sub-grid miners), and that difficulty's ~2-week lagged/clamped adjustment weakens the 'mean-reversion floor' pro.

approaches.name: Power-Law Time Regression (Santostasi / Burger Corridor)
approaches.description: Models BTC price as a deterministic power law of time since genesis: P(t) = A·t^n, fit by OLS of log(price) on log(days-since-2009). The canonical fit (Santostasi/Burger) gives n≈5.6 and R²≈0.96 on a log-log chart, with parallel upper/lower "corridor" lines defining a fair-value band rather than a point estimate. A 10-15yr CMA falls out mechanically: because annualized appreciation under P~t^n equals n/age, the model itself FORECASTS decay — ~33%/yr at today's ~17yr age, sliding to ~18%/yr by 2040 — yielding ~27% nominal CAGR over a 2026-2041 window off the central line. The corridor width (roughly -50%/+200% around fair value) supplies the dispersion/volatility view. Crucially the model is silent on volatility-as-a-stat and on cross-asset correlations; those must be imported from realized data.
key_drivers: Time since genesis (t in days) — the sole regressor
Fitted power-law exponent n≈5.6 and intercept A
Asserted network/Metcalfe feedback loop linking addresses, price, and hash-rate as mutual power laws of time
1/t appreciation decay built into the functional form
Corridor band multiples defining the fair-value dispersion
Time-origin and fit-window choices (to which the exponent is highly sensitive)
pros: Internally encodes appreciation DECAY — unlike naive 'BTC compounds at 100%+' extrapolations, the power law mechanically slows returns as the asset ages (n/age), which is the right qualitative shape for a maturing CMA
Empirically tight in-sample: R²≈0.96 over ~12 orders of magnitude and ~15 years; visually compelling on log-log

Recent peer-reviewed work (arXiv 2605.21316) finds that DESPITE weak statistical structure, the power law out-of-forecasts ARIMA, exponential smoothing and random-walk-with-drift at 12-24 month horizons (p<0.05) — so it has genuine, if modest, predictive content
Parameter-light and falsifiable: a single exponent and intercept; deviations from the corridor are observable
Gives an explicit fair-value band (not just a point), which maps naturally onto a CMA central case plus dispersion
Author imposes a self-discipline ('do not use past ~2040'), acknowledging the model is an interpolation of an adoption S-curve, not eternal physics
cons: The headline structural claim is statistically weak: 8 of 11 Clauset-Shalizi-Newman tests REJECT the power law (lognormal preferred), and the fitted exponent varies by ~3x (α̂≈5.65 to 16.5) across reasonable shifts of the time origin — violating shift-invariance and revealing the fit is not a robust law

A 3-component sigmoid (multi-wave adoption) beats the power law in-sample on AIC/BIC — i.e., the power law is not even the best-fitting curve, it just generalizes better out-of-sample by being simpler

Any monotonically rising series looks linear on a log-log plot; log-log axes massively compress error and flatter curve-fits — the 'tight fit' is partly an axis artifact (the core critique of the Burger corridor as retrofitting, not prediction)

No economic anchor: t (calendar time) is not a value driver. The asserted Metcalfe causal loop (addresses~t^3, price~addresses^2) is the same family the academic literature largely rejects in naive form (spurious cointegration, non-stationarity), and Wheatley-Sornette's own generalized Metcalfe (exponent 1.69) is used to flag BTC as repeatedly OVER fundamental value, not to bless the trend
Survivorship / single-path: the law is fit to the one realized BTC history; it cannot price catastrophic-failure tail mass, so it overstates expected return by ignoring the left tail

Post-2021 regime risk: ETF era, institutionalization and the maturity break mean the historical exponent may not persist; the corridor has already been quietly re-parameterized downward as upper bands over-predicted
Says nothing about volatility-as-risk or correlations — useless for the portfolio-construction half of a CMA without external inputs
Crypto-native marketing has weaponized it ('$1M floor by 2037') in ways the more careful authors did not intend; provenance must be separated from hype

synthesized_outputs.appreciation_nominal: ~22-27%/yr nominal (judgment). Read the central power-law line forward 10-15yr: n/age decay takes instantaneous appreciation from ~33%/yr (age 17) to ~18%/yr (age 31), and the 2026-2041 corridor CAGR computes to ~27%. I haircut to ~22-25% for left-tail/failure mass the single-path fit ignores. This is well below BTC's realized 142%→65%→17% decaying history and is deliberately the DECAY extrapolation, not the level.
synthesized_outputs.appreciation_real: ~18-21%/yr real (subtracting ~3-3.5% long-run US inflation). Judgment, not a model output.
synthesized_outputs.volatility: ~55-60%/yr annualized (judgment). The model is silent; realized vol (~57% trailing-5y) is the floor, with the band ~50-60% over 10-15yr. I do NOT credit compression to ~40% — the sub-2yr ETF sample does not yet evidence a floor below realized — but vol still runs ~3x equities.
synthesized_outputs.corr_growth_eq: +0.45 to +0.65 (judgment). Power law says nothing; realized post-ETF BTC-NASDAQ is 0.76-0.92 and BTC-S&P 0.5-0.88. I assume partial mean-reversion of the ETF-era spike, leaving BTC moderately-to-strongly tied to growth/tech equities over the horizon.
synthesized_outputs.corr_value_eq: +0.20 to +0.35 (judgment). Lower than growth equities; BTC behaves as a long-duration risk asset, loosely linked to value.
synthesized_outputs.corr_fi_nominal: -0.05 to +0.15 (judgment). Near-zero; episodic positive co-movement during liquidity-driven risk-on/off, no structural link.
synthesized_outputs.corr_tips: 0.00 to +0.15 (judgment). Weak; BTC is liquidity/real-rate sensitive but not a reliable real-rate hedge.
synthesized_outputs.corr_gold: ~0.0-0.10 (judgment). The 'digital gold' reading is not supported: BTC-gold co-moved 2022-2024 but broke down in 2025, and BTC remains far more equity-correlated than gold. The power-law itself implies no gold mechanism. Internal-contradiction note: a corridor thesis that frames BTC as gold's successor needs co-movement to justify the share transfer, yet realized co-movement is ~0 — so BTC is NOT a gold substitute over the horizon.

approaches.rich_notes:
METHODOLOGY. The canonical model is an OLS regression of log10(BTC price) on log10(days since the 2009 genesis block), producing a straight line on a log-log chart. The widely-circulated fitted form (Bitcoin Magazine Pro / Glassnode trackers, 2025) is P = 10^(-1.847796462) * (days/365.25)^5.616314045, R²=95.65% on daily closes. Santostasi (2018) frames the price exponent as ~6 (P~t^6), and adds companion 'laws': active addresses ~ t^3, hash-rate ~ t^12, with price~addresses^2 and hash-rate~price^2 — i.e., a self-consistent web of power laws he attributes to a Metcalfe-type adoption/security feedback loop, arguing this makes the regression CAUSAL rather than spurious autocorrelation. He explicitly cautions the model should not be used beyond ~2040. Burger (2017/2019) independently fit the same log-log line but added a CORRIDOR — parallel upper ('bull mode') and lower ('normal mode') power lines — and made bracketed calls: $100K no earlier than 2021/no later than 2028 (and never below $100K after 2028); $1M no earlier than 2028/no later than 2037.

HOW THE CMA FALLS OUT. The single most important property for a 10-15yr CMA: under P~t^n, the instantaneous annualized appreciation is exactly n/age. With n≈5.6 and BTC ~17yr old in 2026, that is ~33%/yr today, decaying to ~27% by 2030 (age 21), ~22% by 2035 (age 26), ~18% by 2040 (age 31). Computing CAGR directly off the central fit: 2026-2036 = 29.7%, 2026-2041 (the 15yr CMA window) = 26.7%, 2030-2040 = 24.5%. So the model's OWN logic delivers the appreciation-decay the CMA brief demands: it forecasts ~25-27% nominal over the horizon, far below BTC's realized 142%/65%/17% trailing decay path but consistent with continued maturation. I haircut my synthesized central to ~22-25% to reflect the single realized path's omission of failure/left-tail mass.

VOLATILITY & CORRELATIONS. The power-law literature is genuinely SILENT on both. It has no stochastic/variance term — only a deterministic line plus a fair-value band. The corridor width (fair $120K, lower $60K = 0.5x, upper $360K = 3.0x) implies an average log half-width ~0.9, i.e. ~0.6 long-run log-sd of cross-sectional dispersion — but that is a fair-value band, NOT an annualized return volatility, and conflating them would be an error. For vol and all five correlations I therefore import realized data and apply the same maturity-decay reasoning: BTC realized vol ~54% in 2025 and structurally falling post-ETF (Fidelity/iShares), so ~40-50% over the horizon. Realized correlations post-ETF: BTC-NASDAQ 0.76-0.92, BTC-S&P 0.5-0.88, BTC-gold positive 2022-2024 then broke down in 2025; BTC stays a long-duration risk asset far more equity-correlated than gold. This DIRECTLY undercuts the 'digital gold' thesis on the data: my synthesized BTC-gold corr is only +0.10 to +0.25.

CRITIQUE / WHY NOT TO LAUNDER HYPE. Three independent, credible problems. (1) Statistical structure is weak — arXiv 2605.21316 ('Weak Structure, Strong Forecasts'): 8/11 Clauset-Shalizi-Newman tests reject the power law in favor of lognormal; the fitted exponent swings ~3x (5.65 to 16.5) across reasonable time-origin shifts, breaking shift-invariance; and a 3-component sigmoid stack beats the power law in-sample on AIC/BIC. The power law is not even the best in-sample curve — it merely generalizes better. (2) Log-log retrofitting — the Amdax/Marcel Burger debunking and the recency-of-fit critiques note any rising series looks linear on log-log, error is visually compressed, and the corridor is plausibly retrofit, not predictive; upper bands have already been quietly re-parameterized down because they over-predicted. (3) No economic anchor — calendar time is not a value driver; the Metcalfe causal story is the same family the academic literature rejects in naive form (spurious cointegration, non-stationarity, post-2021 break). Tellingly, the one peer-reviewed Metcalfe treatment (Wheatley/Sornette/ETH, Royal Society Open Science 2018-19; generalized Metcalfe exponent 1.69, each user linked to ~N^(2/3) others) uses the network fundamental to show BTC repeatedly TRADES ABOVE fair value in bursting LPPLS bubbles — i.e. the rigorous version of this family is a bubble DETECTOR, not a trend-blessing CMA engine.

BOTTOM LINE FOR THE CMA ROW. Useful as a sanity-checked central appreciation path BECAUSE it forces decay (~22-27% nominal, ~18-21% real over 10-15yr), modestly supported by genuine out-of-sample forecasting skill at 1-2yr horizons. But it is structurally fragile, economically unanchored, blind to tail risk, and silent on the risk/correlation inputs a portfolio CMA needs — so it should anchor only the return point estimate, with vol and correlations sourced from realized data, and the whole thing flagged as an interpolated adoption-S-curve segment that the authors themselves disown past ~2040.

issues: Internal tension between the n/age decay and the synthesized point: the model's own central-line CAGR over 2026-2041 is 26.7% (verified exactly) and n/age never falls below ~18%, yet the synthesized nominal is haircut to '22-27%' with a stated central of ~22-25%. The lower bound (22%) is fine as a left-tail haircut, but the band straddles the un-haircut model output rather than sitting clearly below it. The synthesis should label 26.7% as the raw model read and ~22-24% as the haircut central, not present '22-27%' as if 27% were itself a haircut.

The Burger '$1M floor by 2037' phrasing is technically a misstatement of Burger's actual bracket: $1M arrives no later than 2037 (upper band), and the $1M floor applies AFTER 2037, not 'by' 2037. The synthesis does flag this exact phrase as crypto-marketing weaponization to be separated from the careful authors, so it is not laundering, but the cited_outputs field reproduces 'Burger: $1M floor no later than 2037' without that caveat attached inline.

The corridor-to-vol translation is stated carefully (a fair-value cross-sectional band, NOT annualized return vol) but the synthesized 40-50% vol is entirely imported and the claim 'BTC ~54% in 2025, structurally declining post-ETF' is asserted without a cited realized series; given the scripted baseline shows 57-103% realized vol, a 40-50% forward number is an aggressive maturation assumption that should be flagged as the optimistic end, not the central.

The synthesized BTC-gold corr of +0.10 to +0.25 is well supported and correctly undercuts the digital-gold thesis, consistent with the scripted ~0 gold correlation. No issue here — this is a strength — but the synthesis nowhere reconciles the strongly positive growth-equity corr (+0.45 to +0.65) it assigns with the realized post-ETF 0.76-0.92 BTC-NASDAQ it cites; the assumed mean-reversion of ~0.3 correlation points is a large, unjustified judgment call.

Missing critique: the synthesis does not mention that the power law's OLS-on-log-log fit has heteroskedastic, serially autocorrelated residuals, so the R²=0.9565 and any t-stats are statistically inflated (Newey-West / the regression-on-trending-time spurious-regression problem of Granger-Newbold). It cites shift-variance and lognormal-preference but omits the autocorrelated-residual / spurious-trend-regression critique, which is the most damning econometric objection to fitting price on calendar time.

Round-2 correction (corr_gold/vol): Gold-corr re-centered from 0.10-0.25 to 0.0-0.10 with co-movement contradiction explicit; vol floor raised from 40% to ~57% (named by critic as floor-below-realized).
verdict.corrections: Relabel the appreciation row: raw central-line model CAGR is 26.7% nominal (2026-2041) and 24.5% (2030-2040) — present these as the deterministic model output, then state ~22-24% as the left-tail-haircut synthesized central, rather than a '22-27%' band that overlaps the un-haircut figure. Attach the Burger caveat inline in cited_outputs: $1M is the upper-band arrival no later than 2037; the $1M 'floor' applies only after 2037. Flag the 40-50% vol as the optimistic-maturation end and reconcile it explicitly against the scripted 57-103% realized range (a more defensible central is ~50-65%). Add the spurious-trend-regression / autocorrelated-residual critique (Granger-Newbold) to the cons as the core econometric objection to regressing price on calendar time. Note the growth-equity corr assumes ~0.3 of mean-reversion off realized 0.76-0.92 — keep but label as an aggressive judgment.

approaches.name: Store-of-Value / Gold-Parity TAM Substitution
approaches.description: Bitcoin is modeled not via discounted cashflows (it has none) but as an emergent monetary/store-of-value (SoV) asset competing for a slice of an existing addressable market — primarily investable gold, sometimes the broader "global market portfolio" or all SoV wealth (gold + offshore deposits + bond/sovereign-wealth hedges). The CMA is built bottom-up: (1) size the target TAM (e.g., ~$6.2T private investable gold per JPMorgan, or ~$18T total gold per ARK), (2) project that TAM's growth, (3) assume a terminal share Bitcoin captures by the horizon year (often probability-weighted across bear/base/bull adoption scenarios), (4) divide implied market cap by Bitcoin's near-fixed/asymptotic supply to get a price target, and (5) annualize price-target-over-spot into an expected CAGR. JPMorgan adds a volatility/risk-capital adjustment (Bitcoin consumes ~1.8x the risk capital of gold, so parity is on a vol-scaled, not dollar-for-dollar, basis). A 10-15yr CMA falls out directly as the annualized return from today's spot to the horizon-year probability-weighted market cap, with volatility assumed to decay toward gold-like levels and correlation to gold assumed low-to-modest (the "digital gold" thesis paradoxically does NOT require high gold correlation — it requires gold-like demand drivers).
key_drivers: Target TAM size: private investable gold (~$6.2T, JPM) vs total gold (~$18T, ARK) vs broad SoV/global-market-portfolio (~$200T, ARK)
Terminal capture share Bitcoin reaches by horizon (e.g., CF Benchmarks base 33% of gold mktcap; ARK base 2.5% / bull 6.5% of global portfolio; JPM parity = 100% of vol-adjusted private gold)
TAM growth rate (gold mktcap compounding ~3-5%/yr on CB buying + inflation)
Bitcoin's near-fixed, asymptotic supply (~21M cap, ~19.9M mined) — converts mktcap to price with minimal dilution
Volatility/risk-capital ratio vs gold (JPM: BTC ~1.8x gold's risk capital; converges as institutionalization grows)
Probability weights across bear/base/bull adoption scenarios (CF Benchmarks: 60/20/10 + 10% gold-parity)
Adoption S-curve maturity / institutional flows (ETFs, sovereign reserves, corporate treasuries) as the share-gain mechanism
pros: Theoretically coherent for a no-cashflow asset: anchors value to a measurable comparable market (gold) and a supply schedule, rather than to price-history extrapolation
Transparent and decomposable — you can stress each lever (TAM, share, weight) and the math is auditable; CF Benchmarks and ARK publish full scenario tables
Naturally produces a DECAYING expected return: as BTC's share of gold rises toward parity, marginal upside shrinks, which is the correct shape for a maturing asset's forward CMA
JPMorgan's volatility-adjustment is a genuine methodological improvement — comparing risk-capital rather than raw dollars avoids the naive 'BTC = gold mktcap' overstatement
Probability-weighting (CF Benchmarks) makes the framework usable as an actual CMA input rather than a single hype target
Supply-side is the most defensible part of the chain: Bitcoin's issuance schedule is genuinely near-deterministic
cons: The terminal capture share is an assumption, not a derivation — it is where all the optimism hides; ARK's 6.5% bull share and CF Benchmarks' 33% of gold are asserted, not estimated from any structural model

Marketing, not peer-reviewed: ARK and CF Benchmarks pieces are sell-the-asset documents from firms long Bitcoin (ARK runs ARKB; CF Benchmarks is the index provider for spot BTC ETFs) — conflict of interest is severe

The 'digital gold' premise is empirically shaky: realized BTC-gold correlation is near zero (~0.06, CF Benchmarks' own number) and BTC behaves as a high-beta risk asset, not a safe haven — it sold off WITH equities in 2022 and decoupled UPWARD from gold in 2025, contradicting the substitution thesis
JPMorgan's $170k is explicitly a 6-12 MONTH fair value, not a 10-15yr structural CMA — repurposing it as a long-horizon anchor is a category error

Gold's own market cap is not a fixed pie BTC drains from — gold demand (CB buying) and BTC demand have been positively correlated at times, so 'substitution' may be double-counting a shared macro driver (debasement/real-rate regime)

Adjacent SoV-narrative models (Stock-to-Flow, Metcalfe) that the same firms cite are largely REJECTED in the academic literature: S2F regressions are spurious — non-stationary series, serially correlated residuals, failed Engle-Granger/Johansen assumptions (Marcel Burger; ScienceDirect 2024), and S2F broke catastrophically post-2021 (predicted $100k+ during the 2022 crash to ~$16k); Metcalfe fits are over-fit and unstable out-of-sample
Path/timing risk is ignored: a probability-weighted terminal mktcap says nothing about a 70-80% drawdown en route, which a 10-15yr holder must survive
No mean-reversion anchor: if BTC overshoots gold parity, the model has no force pulling it back, unlike a DCF or yield-based valuation
