This is the model's central internal contradiction made explicit: the thesis VALUES BTC by the monetary-gold TAM it supposedly penetrates, which mechanically REQUIRES BTC to co-move with gold (to absorb gold's share, demand must substitute across the two), yet realized BTC-gold correlation is ~0 (full -0.01, 5y +0.045). You cannot claim both 'BTC takes gold's monetary share' (needs co-movement) and 'BTC diversifies against gold' (needs independence). The honest number sits at the bottom of the 0.0-0.15 band; the gold-parity TAM is a sizing narrative, not an empirically supported correlation.

approaches.rich_notes:
METHODOLOGY CHAIN (all variants): TAM -> TAM growth -> terminal capture share -> /supply -> price target -> annualize to CAGR. The honest read is that ALL the forecast variance lives in 'terminal capture share,' which is asserted.

KEY PUBLISHED NUMBERS (verified from sources, 2025-2026):
- JPMorgan/Panigirtzoglou (CoinDesk, Nov 2025): BTC consumes ~1.8x the risk capital of gold; private investable gold = $6.2T (ETFs+bars+coins); BTC mktcap ~$2.1T; to reach VOL-ADJUSTED parity (two-thirds of private gold) implies ~$170k, a +67% move. CRITICAL CAVEAT: explicitly a 6-12 MONTH fair value, prior benchmark was $102k. This is a tactical mispricing call, NOT a 10-15yr CMA — do not launder it as one.
- ARK (2025): global market portfolio ~$200T (3% CAGR assumption); bear/base/bull BTC penetration 1% / 2.5% / 6.5% (vs gold's ~3.6% share today); 2030 targets $500k / $1.2M / $2.4M = CAGR ~32% / ~53% / ~72% from end-2024. 'Digital gold' is the LARGEST contributor to bear+base; bull is driven more by institutional + on-chain. Bull assumes BTC captures 60% of gold's $18T cap. These are 5-6yr targets, far more aggressive than a 10-15yr CMA should be.
- CF Benchmarks (2025): the most CMA-shaped source. To 2035: base 60% prob -> $1.42M (~33% of gold mktcap), bear 20% -> $637k (~16%), bull 10% -> $2.95M (~125% of gold), +10% gold-parity. Base expected return 30.1%/yr. Vol projected toward 28% over the decade. Correlations (current->10yr projected): equities 0.52->0.15, bonds 0.14->0.22, commodities 0.04->-0.12, GOLD ~0.06 (stays near zero), USD -0.26->-0.11. Recommends 2-5% strategic allocation; claims BTC expands the efficient frontier.
- Fidelity Digital Assets ('Valuing Bitcoin' 2022; 'Aspirational SoV Revisited' 2024): frames BTC as emergent monetary asset, no cashflows/industrial use, value = relative attractiveness as alternative SoV. Notably ALSO leans on Metcalfe's Law as 'one of the most compelling' techniques — which is a red flag (see critiques). Argues BTC is a LOW-correlation complement to gold, not a pure substitute (BTC ~8th-largest global asset, ~$2.2T, Aug 2025).

ADVERSARIAL / ACADEMIC REJECTION (must be represented, not laundered):
- Stock-to-Flow (PlanB), frequently cited alongside the SoV narrative: academically rejected in naive form. Marcel Burger (Amdax) and others show the OLS S2F regression is a classic SPURIOUS REGRESSION — both series non-stationary, residuals serially correlated, Engle-Granger and Johansen cointegration tests fail their own assumptions. ScienceDirect (Finance Research Letters 2024, 'Do bitcoin shocks truly cointegrate...') and the broader literature find the cointegration claims do not hold robustly. S2F also broke empirically post-2021 (predicted >$100k through the 2022 bear market that bottomed ~$16k). Some defenders (ARDL specifications) argue the scarcity link isn't fully falsified, but the naive log-log S2F model is not credible.
- Metcalfe's Law for BTC: in-sample fits to n^2 (active addresses) are decent but over-fit and unstable out-of-sample; address counts are gameable and not a clean user proxy. Treat as narrative, not valuation.
- Digital-gold correlation contradiction: the thesis sells BTC as gold's digital cousin, yet realized BTC-gold correlation is ~0 (CF Benchmarks' OWN 0.06). Gold and BTC moved together 2022-2024 then decoupled hard in 2025 (gold +67% vs BTC ~+400% over Nov22-Nov24; divergence in 2025). BTC behaves as high-beta risk (sold off WITH equities in 2022). So 'substitution into gold's market' rests on shared DEMAND DRIVERS (debasement, real rates), not on co-movement — and that shared driver means 'substitution' may double-count a common macro factor rather than reflect BTC draining gold's pie.

SYNTHESIS REASONING (my 10-15yr judgment under THIS approach's logic):
Scripted anchors (see /tmp/btc_anchor.py and /tmp/btc_soV.py):
(1) Realized decay anchor: 142%/yr (14y) -> 65%/yr (10y) -> 17%/yr (5y). A pure log-linear decay extrapolation collapses to ~6%/yr at 5-10y fwd and ~2%/yr at 10-15y fwd — too aggressive, because it ignores the SoV floor.
(2) Gold-parity TAM anchor (12.5yr, gold mktcap +5%/yr): terminal share 1.0x private-gold -> 14.5%/yr; 1.6x -> 18.9%/yr; 3.0x -> 25%/yr. BTC is already ~34% of private gold / ~12% of total gold, so much of the easy substitution upside is spent.
Blending: the SoV logic puts a FLOOR under the decay path (BTC shouldn't fall to bond-like returns if it's a credible gold alternative) but the decay evidence argues for the conservative end of the SoV anchor. I land at ~10-15% nominal (point ~12%), ~8-11% real, vol ~40-50% (I refuse CF Benchmarks' optimistic 28%), and correlations that stay meaningfully positive to risk assets (growth-eq ~0.45) while gold correlation stays LOW (~0.15) — the model's internal contradiction made explicit. All synthesized figures are judgments anchored to scripted brackets, NOT computed statistics.

CONFLICT-OF-INTEREST FLAG: ARK (runs ARKB ETF) and CF Benchmarks (index provider to spot-BTC ETFs incl. IBIT) are structurally long. JPMorgan's piece is desk strategy, near-term. Fidelity Digital Assets sells custody/ETF (FBTC). Treat all expected-return figures as upper-bound marketing anchors; the academic layer (Burger, ScienceDirect) is the corrective.

issues: MISATTRIBUTED JOURNAL: The ScienceDirect paper (PII S1057521924002862, 'Do bitcoin shocks truly cointegrate with financial and commodity markets?') is published in INTERNATIONAL REVIEW OF FINANCIAL ANALYSIS, not 'Finance Research Letters' as the representative_sources entry and rich_notes both state.

MISUSED CITATION (most serious): The same ScienceDirect paper is cited to support 'cointegration claims do not hold robustly,' but its actual headline finding is the OPPOSITE — it FINDS hidden/asymmetric cointegration between negative bitcoin shocks and nearly all financial/commodity markets (BTC acts as a short-term negative-shock mediator). Read properly it supports BTC-financial-market linkage, not S2F rejection. The research recruits it for the wrong proposition.

OVERSTATED BURGER REJECTION: The con bullet frames Marcel Burger as a clean rejection ('Engle-Granger and Johansen cointegration tests fail their own assumptions'). The real arc: Burger first alleged spurious regression, then VERIFIED cointegration across 3-4 tests, then later retracted the cointegration finding as improperly applied — while explicitly stating this 'doesn't mean the relationship is spurious or that the S2F model is useless.' The rich_notes partially hedges this (ARDL caveat), but the headline con bullet does not.

BYLINE/URL IMPRECISION: The Burger source is listed under 'medium.com/burgercrypto-com' but the canonical Part II is published under Amdax Asset Management's Medium (medium.com/amdax-asset-management). Same author, but the firm attribution in the link path is inconsistent with the cited author_firm 'Amdax Asset Management'.

S2F POST-2021 BREAK is asserted ('predicted >$100k through the 2022 bear market that bottomed ~$16k') but not independently sourced in the citation list — it is true and widely documented, but no source in representative_sources establishes it; it rides on the contested Burger thread.
Round-2 correction (corr_gold/vol): Gold-corr lowered to 0.0-0.10 with the TAM-substitution contradiction stated in full; vol floor raised from 40% to ~57% (named by critic).
verdict.corrections: Correct the journal name: the 'Do bitcoin shocks truly cointegrate' paper is in International Review of Financial Analysis, not Finance Research Letters. Either drop that paper as an S2F-rejection cite or re-characterize it accurately as finding ASYMMETRIC cointegration of BTC with financial markets (which, if anything, weakly cuts against the 'BTC is decoupled/uncorrelated' framing, not the S2F point). Soften the Burger con bullet to reflect that his cointegration critique was itself later self-retracted and he does not claim S2F is spurious or useless — the honest academic state is 'naive log-log S2F is not statistically established,' not 'rejected.' Fix the Burger link/firm to Amdax. All primary published numbers (JPM $170k/6-12mo/$6.2T/1.8x/$2.1T; ARK $500k/$1.2M/$2.4M at 32/53/72% CAGR; CF Benchmarks $637k/$1.42M/$2.95M, 16-33%/33%/>100% of gold, 30.1%/yr) verified exact — keep as-is. Synthesized brackets (14.5/18.9/25.0%), BTC-%-of-gold (34%/12%), and the ~12% landing all reproduce from the scripted anchors — keep. No change to vol (40-50%), gold corr (0.15), or eq corr (0.45) judgments; they are appropriately conservative versus the conflicted sources.

approaches.name: Monetary-Substitution / M2 Elasticity & Debasement Hedge
approaches.description: This approach models Bitcoin not as a cashflow asset but as a high-beta claim on the growth of fiat money supply. The core empirical object is a cointegrating (long-run equilibrium) relationship between log BTC price and log broad money — typically US M2 or a synthetic "global M2" (sum of major-central-bank M2 converted at FX). BTC is treated as integrated of order one, I(1), and cointegrated with money: estimated long-run elasticities run ~2.0–2.65 (a 1% rise in M2 maps to a >2% rise in BTC), with a VECM error-correction term (~-0.12/month, ~5-6 month half-life) pulling price back to the money-implied "fair value." A 10-15yr CMA falls out mechanically: forecast trend money growth, multiply by the (decaying) elasticity beta, and that is BTC's expected nominal appreciation; the debasement thesis adds that fiat dilution is the structural tailwind and BTC's fixed 21M supply (predictable issuance, ~450/day to the 2028 halving) is the differentiator vs gold.
key_drivers: Broad-money / liquidity growth (US M2 ~6%, global M2 ~7-8%) as the exogenous trend driver
BTC money-elasticity beta (~2.0-2.65 historical, must be decayed toward 1.0-1.5 forward)
Error-correction speed to money-implied fair value (~-0.12/mo, ~5-6mo half-life)
Fiscal dominance / sovereign debt growth driving fiat depreciation (the debasement premise)
Fixed transparent supply (21M cap, halvings, ~450/day issuance) as the scarcity differentiator vs both fiat and gold
Liquidity-leads-BTC lag (months); global liquidity Granger-causes BTC, raw world-M2 levels do not
pros: Grounds an otherwise cashflow-less asset in a real, testable macro variable (money supply) rather than pure sentiment or stock-to-flow numerology

Empirically the directional relationship is genuinely strong: BTC moves with global liquidity ~83% of 12-month windows (Alden/Callahan), higher than any other major asset class — a real signal, not nothing
Provides an explicit, falsifiable fair-value model (e.g. CF Benchmarks' M2 fair value) you can mark price against and that has historically mean-reverted
Conceptually clean CMA derivation: expected return = trend money growth x elasticity, which naturally forces appreciation DECAY as the elasticity compresses toward gold's
Ties BTC to the same debasement logic underwriting gold (Grayscale), making it portfolio-coherent with a real-asset / inflation-hedge sleeve
cons: The headline elasticity (2.65) and 0.94 levels-correlation are almost certainly SPURIOUS in the econometric sense: both log-BTC and log-M2 are non-stationary trending I(1) series, and naive level correlation/regression on two trends is the textbook spurious-regression trap

On contemporaneous CHANGES (the regression you should run), the M2-BTC relationship 'nearly vanishes' — correlation collapses toward ~0; the relationship lives almost entirely in shared trend, not in month-to-month co-movement

Cointegration is NOT stable: the peer-reviewed TVC-VECM literature (Park/Lee JDQS 2022) formally rejects constant coefficients (p=0.0015) in favor of smoothly time-varying ones — so a single fixed elasticity for a 10-15yr CMA is not supported by the data

Clear post-2021/2025 structural break: CF Benchmarks reports R-squared collapsing from 0.71-0.90 to ~0.59 and a ~46% fair-value gap; gold's liquidity Z-score climbed to 2.82 while BTC's fell to -1.31, i.e. the liquidity bid rotated AWAY from BTC

'Global M2' is a data-quality artifact: it is built by multiplying heterogeneous national M2 by spot FX, mixing fast- and slow-reporting regimes, and is routinely curve-fit/lag-shifted ('data torture', 'overfitting') to match BTC — quants flatly say it 'can't predict' BTC

No anchor for the elasticity going forward: there's no theory pinning beta at 2.65 vs 1.5 vs 1.0, so the CMA's central number is a judgment call dressed as an estimate; the model also says nothing about volatility or correlations directly

Source quality is mixed and tilts promotional: the strongest numeric claims come from a non-peer-reviewed preprint and from sell-side/asset-manager research (Grayscale, CF Benchmarks) with a long book, not from replicated academic work

approaches.rich_notes:
METHODOLOGY. The canonical setup: take log(BTC) and log(M2), confirm both are I(1) (ADF, plus Zivot-Andrews to allow one structural break), test for a single cointegrating vector (Engle-Granger and Johansen), then estimate a VECM. Preprints.org 2025 (Jan-2015 to Apr-2025, monthly) reports a Johansen long-run elasticity of 2.65 (1% M2 -> 2.65% BTC) and an error-correction coefficient lambda' = -0.12, i.e. ~12% of any deviation from the money-implied path corrects per month (half-life ~ln(0.5)/ln(0.88) ~ 5-6 months). It concludes BTC is a 'highly elastic, liquidity-driven asset.' CAVEAT: this is a preprint (also republished in WMJournals/WMJ-JESD), not peer-reviewed; the abstract does not report R-squared, the specific unit-root statistics, or robustness to multiple breaks.

THE SPURIOUSNESS PROBLEM (central). Two trending I(1) series will show a near-1.0 levels correlation and a 'significant' regression even if unrelated — Granger-Newbold spurious regression. Cointegration is the defense, BUT (a) cointegration over a single 10-year hyper-adoption sample with one secular up-trend in both series is fragile, and (b) the peer-reviewed evidence says the relationship is NOT constant. Park & Lee (JDQS 2022, Emerald, peer-reviewed) run a time-varying-cointegration VECM with Chebyshev polynomials on BTC, VIX, US10Y, USCPI, gold, DXY: at m=1 (constant coefficients) the null is not rejected, but m>=2 rejects at p=0.00152 — i.e. the cointegrating coefficients SMOOTHLY EVOLVE over time. Their cointegrating vector (normalized on VIX) has BTC -2.727, gold -0.0443, DXY -0.676 — inverse links to safe havens and volatility. Critically that paper does NOT include M2 at all, so it neither confirms nor refutes the M2 vector directly; its contribution here is the meta-point that BTC's macro cointegration is time-varying, which undercuts any fixed-elasticity CMA.

THE CHANGES-VS-LEVELS TELL. Multiple quants note that when you difference both series (look at contemporaneous % changes rather than levels), the M2-BTC correlation 'nearly vanishes' toward ~0. The relationship lives in shared trend. Alden/Callahan ('Bitcoin: A Global Liquidity Barometer,' 2024, practitioner) actually concede this: their headline 0.94 is a LEVELS correlation (May-2013 to Jul-2024); the 12-month rolling correlation is only ~0.51 and 6-month ~0.36; and on a YoY %-change basis equity indices correlate to liquidity slightly MORE than BTC, with BTC's high vol 'distorting' the change-correlation. Their durable claim is directional: BTC moves WITH liquidity 83% of 12-month windows / 74% of 6-month windows — genuinely the highest of major assets, but a sign-agreement stat, not a magnitude/return model.

THE BREAK (most damaging for a forward CMA). CF Benchmarks (2024 piece, updated views into 2026) reports the rolling 4-yr correlation historically 0.4-0.6, and BTC's R-squared with M2 collapsing from 0.71-0.90 (2022 bear) to ~0.59 (early 2026), with their M2 fair value ~$136k vs price ~$74k — a ~46% gap, 'one of the widest observed.' Grayscale's Jan-2026 'Debasement Trade' note documents the rotation: BTC's M2-fair-value Z-score swung +1.48 (Jan-2025) to -1.31 (Feb-2026) while GOLD's climbed 1.38 -> 2.82 — i.e. the debasement/liquidity bid that the thesis predicts for BTC actually went to gold. This is the single most important caveat for the gold correlation: the 'digital gold' co-movement is low and regime-switching, and in the most recent episode BTC and gold DIVERGED hard.

DATA-QUALITY CAVEAT. 'Global M2' has no official definition; it is constructed by summing national M2 and converting at spot FX, blending fast-reporting (US) and lag-reporting economies, so its 'daily' wiggles are partly an FX artifact. Critics call the chart-overlay practice 'a textbook case of data illiteracy and overfitting' — analysts lag-shift M2 by an arbitrary number of weeks to maximize visual fit, then present the fitted lag as predictive. A TradingView/quant piece bluntly: 'Global M2 can't predict Bitcoin price.' Also note: global liquidity (broad, includes central-bank balance sheets/credit) Granger-causes BTC, but raw world M2 does not — so even the causal claim is sensitive to which liquidity proxy is used.

GRAYSCALE / DEBASEMENT FRAMING (asset-manager, promotional but useful). Debasement trade = excess sovereign debt -> fiat depreciation vs scarce-supply assets (real estate, metals, BTC). Grayscale: BTC returns on average positively correlated to stocks, positively correlated to gold, negatively correlated to USD; BTC 'less tightly correlated with month-to-month Dollar weakness' than other debasement assets but with a high downside-capture ratio (it falls with risk-off even when the debasement story is intact). Supply differentiator: 20-millionth BTC mined ~early 2026, ~450 BTC/day to the Apr-2028 halving, hard 21M cap — predictable, decreasing issuance vs open-ended fiat.

REALIZED BASELINE (my scripted anchor, year-end USD). YoY: 2017 +1341%, 2020 +303%, 2021 +60%, 2022 -64%, 2023 +156%, 2024 +121%, 2025 +8%. Trailing CAGR to 2025: 10yr ~73%, 12yr ~50%, 5yr ~28%. Decay of trailing CAGR as the asset matured: 2013-2017 ~107%/yr -> 2013-2020 ~68%/yr -> 2013-2024 ~55%/yr. The prompt's 142->65->17 decay framing is directionally identical: appreciation has fallen roughly by half each market-cap doubling.

SYNTHESIS LOGIC. Under THIS model's own machinery, forward return = trend money growth x elasticity. Holding global broad money at ~7-8%/yr and letting the elasticity decay from ~2.0 to ~1.1 across years 3-15 gives an average ~11-12% nominal, ~9% real BEFORE haircutting for the now-documented break and rotation to gold. I round to ~10-12% nominal / ~7-9% real as a judgment, explicitly NOT a computed stat, and flag that the model is silent on vol and correlations so those (~50-55% vol; gold corr ~0.2-0.35; growth-equity ~0.35-0.45) are anchored to realized behavior and the debasement logic, not to anything this literature publishes. Brutal bottom line: the M2-elasticity model is the most intellectually defensible of the cashflow-less BTC frameworks because it has a real driver and a mean-reverting fair value, but its headline elasticity is trend-driven and likely partly spurious, its cointegration is provably time-varying, and the 2025-26 break shows it failing live as gold ate BTC's debasement bid. Use it as ONE input with wide error bars, not as a point CMA.

issues: MISATTRIBUTED AUTHORS: The peer-reviewed JDQS 2022 paper is repeatedly cited as 'Park & Lee' in rich_notes and the spuriousness section. The actual authors are Yong Lee and Joon Hee Rhee (Soongsil University). The representative_sources entry already says 'Park & Lee' too. Every other detail of that citation is correct and verified (TVC-VECM with Chebyshev polynomials; p=0.00152 rejecting constant coefficients at m>=2; cointegrating vector normalized on VIX with BTC -2.727, gold -0.0443, DXY -0.676; M2 NOT included), but the author surname is wrong and should be fixed to Lee & Rhee.

MAJOR OMISSION / SELF-CONTRADICTION: cited_outputs claims 'n/a (source silent -- no source publishes a 10-15yr appreciation CMA)' for appreciation, volatility, and all correlations. This is false. CF Benchmarks -- one of the research's own five representative sources -- published 'Building Bitcoin Capital Market Assumptions' which gives an explicit base-case 30.1% annualized return to a $1.42M/BTC 2035 target, a terminal volatility of ~28% (declining over the decade), and full 10yr correlation projections: gold ~0.06, global equities 0.52->0.15, global bonds 0.14->0.22, commodities 0.04->-0.12, USD -0.26->-0.11. It even has a scenario probability weighting (60% double-trend / 20% trend / 10% gold-parity / 10% outperformance => ~33% of gold mcap by 2035). The research therefore both UNDER-cites its own source and overstates that the literature is silent.

NUMBER TENSION the synthesis does not engage: CF Benchmarks' OWN published CMA says 30.1% nominal, yet the synthesis lands at ~10-12% nominal. That is a ~3x gap with a named source the research relies on elsewhere. The synthesis may well be right to be more conservative (CF Benchmarks is a sell-side index provider with a long book, and its number leans on the same trend-driven elasticity the cons section calls partly spurious), but it must SHOW this disagreement rather than claim the source is silent. As written it looks like the silent-source framing was used to avoid confronting a much higher published number.

CORRELATION ANCHOR conflicts with the best published estimate: the synthesis calls gold correlation ~0.20-0.35 'the load-bearing number for this thesis' and treats positive structural co-movement as the prior. approaches.name: Quantity Theory of Money / Velocity Equation of Exchange (MV=PT)
approaches.description: Treats Bitcoin as a medium of exchange and values it by inverting the equation of exchange, MV=PT: the aggregate dollar value of the Bitcoin float equals the annual real transaction volume it intermediates (T) divided by its velocity (V), so price per coin = T/(V·M) with M = circulating supply. The applied strand (Burniske, Bank of England's John Lewis) plugs in a target transaction-volume scenario (illicit flows, Visa-scale retail, all electronic payments, or world-GDP) and a velocity assumption to get a "current utility value," then discounts a future utility value back at a high (30-50%) rate to a present price. A 10-15yr CMA falls out as the expected appreciation toward that discounted future-utility value as the probability of the larger transaction-share scenario rises. The academic GE strand (Schilling & Uhlig 2018/2019, JME) instead derives a fundamental pricing equation implying the BTC/USD price is a MARTINGALE once it is an established currency: expected risk-adjusted real return equals the dollar's, i.e. roughly zero real drift, with all the volatility coming from shifting beliefs about future adoption. So under this family a mature-BTC CMA converges to near-fiat real return, and any positive expected appreciation is a one-time, decaying re-rating as adoption probability climbs toward a ceiling, not a perpetual growth rate.
key_drivers: Annual real transaction volume Bitcoin captures (T) — the addressable payments/remittance/illicit-flow base it actually settles, NOT speculative exchange churn (30%+ of on-chain volume is exchange shuttling, not GDP)
Velocity (V) — turnover of the monetary base; assumption is the single most sensitive input. Ranges cited 1 (held as broad money/SoV) to 6.5-14 (Bitcoin means-of-exchange) to 24 (payment-card-like)
Money supply (M) — fixed/known issuance schedule capped at 21M; the only clean, exogenous variable in the identity

Probability-weighted adoption scenario — which transaction-share state the market believes Bitcoin will occupy (illicit-only, Visa-scale, all-electronic, world-currency); price re-rates as this belief shifts
Discount rate (Burniske 30-50%, 3-5x equity) applied to a future utility value to get present rational price
Hodling / dormant-coin fraction — coins held off-market lower effective M and effective V, raising implied price (the SoV-vs-MoE tension inside the same identity)
In the GE model: dollar inflation target / monetary policy and agents' relative impatience, which pin down the martingale and rule out speculative drift
pros: Grounded in a genuine, century-old macro identity (Fisher MV=PT) rather than a fitted curve — it is an accounting identity, so it cannot be 'spuriously cointegrated' the way S2F/Metcalfe are; the critique is about input choice, not the equation

Forces an explicit, falsifiable use-case: you must name the transaction volume and velocity, which exposes that current on-chain economic volume is far too small to justify price — a useful reality check against hype
Velocity is uniquely MEASURABLE on a public blockchain (every transfer is recorded), unlike in fiat economies where V is a residual — lets the model be empirically disciplined rather than assumed

The Schilling-Uhlig martingale result is a rigorous, peer-reviewed (Journal of Monetary Economics) general-equilibrium foundation that correctly predicts LOW long-run real drift and high belief-driven volatility — a sober antidote to perpetual-exponential models
Naturally generates a wide scenario fan (Lewis: ~$19k illicit-only to >$5M world-currency), making the binary, fat-tailed payoff structure explicit rather than hiding it in a point estimate
Internally consistent with a 10-15yr CMA framing: appreciation is a probability-weighted re-rating that must decay as adoption saturates, matching BTC's observed return decay
cons: Velocity is the dominant input and is both unstable and poorly defined — on-chain measures (coin-days-destroyed, NVT) disagree wildly and are contaminated by exchange transfers, mixers, and change outputs; Pernice et al. show common velocity proxies are inferior and not robust. Garbage V → garbage valuation

The identity values Bitcoin ONLY as a medium of exchange and is blind to a pure store-of-value / monetary-premium demand — yet that is empirically the dominant driver of price; coins are increasingly hodled (V collapsing), which the MoE framing reads as bullish but the GE framing reads as Bitcoin failing as money. The model can't cleanly hold both

Adoption as a payment rail has FLATLINED since the late 2010s (Lewis): Lightning never scaled, and stablecoins/instant-payment rails dominate the medium-of-exchange niche without the volatility — so the transaction-volume input is arguably shrinking, not growing

Self-referential / circular: to use Bitcoin for payments you must hold it, but its value comes from transaction demand — high volatility deters payment use, suppressing the very T the valuation needs (the 'endogenous velocity constraint', Soleimani 2025: network architecture structurally caps V)

The discount-back-to-present step (Burniske) smuggles in an arbitrary 30-50% rate and a future-utility scenario that does all the work — the output is whatever T, V, and the scenario probability you assume; even Burniske refuses to use it as a price target

Schilling-Uhlig's martingale conclusion implies ~0% expected REAL appreciation for a mature currency-Bitcoin — directly contradicting the digital-gold appreciation thesis; the family's honest read is that long-run expected real return is near fiat, not exponential

Says almost nothing usable about correlations or volatility magnitude — the GE model gives qualitative 'high belief-driven vol,' the applied model gives a scenario fan, but neither produces a calibrated covariance with equities, gold, or rates

approaches.rich_notes:
TWO DISTINCT STRANDS under one family — keep them separate.

(A) ACADEMIC GENERAL-EQUILIBRIUM strand — Schilling & Uhlig, 'Some Simple Bitcoin Economics' (NBER WP 24483, 2018; published Journal of Monetary Economics vol.106, pp.16-26, 2019). An endowment economy where Dollar and Bitcoin coexist; CB targets Dollar inflation; BTC supply is exogenous PoW issuance. Central result: a FUNDAMENTAL PRICING EQUATION 'which in its simplest form implies that Bitcoin prices form a martingale' — expected future BTC/USD price = current price. The risk-adjusted real return on Bitcoin must equal the risk-adjusted real return on the Dollar. They derive conditions under which speculation CANNOT happen ('mutual impatience implies absence of speculation') and the fundamental equation must hold. Also: block rewards are NOT a tax on holders — financed by Dollar taxes via the CB. IMPLICATION FOR CMA: for a mature, established currency-Bitcoin, expected REAL drift ≈ 0; all action is belief-driven volatility. This is the single most important sober anchor in the whole BTC litreview and directly contradicts perpetual-exponential models (S2F, power-law). It is peer-reviewed — distinguish sharply from marketing.

(B) APPLIED EQUATION-OF-EXCHANGE / DISCOUNTED-UTILITY strand:
- Chris Burniske (2016 Coinbase report; 2017 'Cryptoasset Valuations' Medium). Rearranges MV=PQ to M = PQ/V, where P·Q is the dollar value of the on-chain resource provisioned and V is velocity; CUV per token = M / tokens-in-float. Picks a 10-yr horizon, projects a future utility value, discounts back: PV = FUV/(1+r)^yrs with r in the 30-50% range ('3-5x the discount rate for risky equities'). Velocity assumption is 'the most important assumption in the entire model'; cites Bitcoin 2016 velocity ~6.5, and a 'means-of-exchange velocity' ~14 (from 46% of Coinbase users transacting). CRUCIAL HONESTY: he explicitly does NOT use these as price targets; his 2015 ARK '$2,000/BTC' he later disavowed for multiple errors. Acknowledged weaknesses he lists himself: velocity sensitivity; 30%+ of on-chain volume is exchange shuttling not real GDP; the model ignores how future market price is set by future expectations; crypto markets not efficient enough for rational-pricing-based asset management.
- John Lewis (Bank of England), Bank Underground, 'The quantity theory of crypto', 28 May 2026. Uses US$ price = T/(M·V), M=21M. SCENARIO TABLE (quote-grade): illicit payments only (T~$2T, V=5) → ~$19k; Visa-scale ($17T, V=24) → ~$34k; all electronic payments ($26T, V=2) → ~$619k; world currency / global GDP ($155T, V=1) → >£5M. Current real retail-payment usage <$10k is only ~$146bn/yr — 'far too low to support current prices', so 'the story must be of (beliefs about) the future.' Conclusion: 'Without a compelling and sizeable use case I see little value in Bitcoin as a means of payment'; adoption has 'flatlined' since late 2010s, Lightning failed to scale, stablecoins/instant payments dominate without the vol. VERY BEARISH on the MoE case. Note this is a BoE staff BLOG, not peer-reviewed, but high quality and central-bank-sourced.

CRITIQUE / MEASUREMENT strand (why the inputs are unreliable):
- Pernice, Gentzen & Elendner, 'Cryptocurrencies and the Velocity of Money' (Cryptoeconomic Systems, MIT, presented 2020, pub. 2021; SSRN 3499500). NOTE: the seed list mis-attributed this as 'Brondino & Pernice' — correct authorship is Pernice/Gentzen/Elendner. Point: velocity is the linchpin of QTM and is normally unobservable, but on public blockchains every transfer is recorded so V can be MEASURED. They evaluate competing velocity definitions and conclude the most common one (coin-days-destroyed) is INFERIOR. Takeaway: even with full on-chain data, V is definition-dependent and unstable → the QTM valuation is only as good as a fragile V choice.
- Soleimani, 'The Endogenous Constraint: Monetary Velocity in the Bitcoin Network' (arXiv 2512.07886, 2025; NON-peer-reviewed preprint, treat cautiously). Argues V is an ENDOGENOUS structural constraint, not an exogenous knob — Bitcoin's block time, throughput, and settlement finality (plus 'hysteresis'/lock-in of usage patterns) structurally inhibit velocity, bounding price appreciation independent of adoption. Reinforces the circularity con.

SYNTHESIS REASONING for my CMA column: The family's own internal logic says (i) any appreciation is a ONE-TIME, decaying re-rating as the probability of a larger transaction-share scenario rises, bounded above by a ceiling and below (for mature BTC) by the Schilling-Uhlig martingale (~fiat real return); (ii) therefore a 10-15yr forward CMA must extrapolate BTC's return DECAY, not its level. Realized anchor (scripted, empirical_anchor.json): full-window nominal 142%/vol 103%; trailing-10y 65%/69%; trailing-5y 17%/57%. I center nominal ~8%, real ~5%, vol ~50%. Correlations: this strand frames BTC as a PAYMENT RAIL / risk asset, so it predicts positive-and-rising equity beta (growth>value), small positive FI/TIPS via liquidity, and — critically — NEAR-ZERO gold correlation (it explicitly rejects the digital-gold thesis). Realized correlations support this: gold ~0.03-0.05, growth-eq 0.56 (5y), value 0.37, FI 0.16-0.19, TIPS 0.30; I shade the equity figures down toward 0.30-0.40 for a forward, regime-averaged horizon. All synthesized numbers are reasoned judgments under this approach's logic, NOT computed statistics.

OVERALL VERDICT: The most intellectually honest of the BTC frameworks because it's an identity, not a fitted curve, and because its rigorous form (Schilling-Uhlig) predicts LOW real drift — but it is almost useless as a point-estimate CMA tool because velocity and the adoption-scenario probability do all the work and are unstable/unfalsifiable ex ante. Best used as a SANITY BOUND ('how much real payment volume is implied by today's price?') and as the theoretical reason to expect appreciation decay toward fiat, rather than as a generator of a single expected-return number.

issues: Citations all verify. Schilling-Uhlig is correctly attributed (Linda Schilling & Harald Uhlig, NBER WP24483, JME vol.106 pp.16-26, 2019; martingale result confirmed verbatim). Lewis 2026 scenario table is exact: illicit-only T~$2T/V5->$19k, Visa T$17T/V24->$34k, all-electronic T$26T/V2->$619k, world-currency T$155T/V1->>$5M, plus the $146bn retail-usage and 'flatlined since late 2010s / Lightning failed' claims. Pernice/Gentzen/Elendner authorship and the coin-days-destroyed-is-inferior finding confirmed. The note even self-corrects the prior 'Brondino & Pernice' misattribution. No fabricated or misattributed sources found.

MISSING CRITIQUE (the main gap): the synthesis leans on the martingale ('~0 real drift') but omits Schilling-Uhlig's EXCHANGE-RATE INDETERMINACY result — the initial price Q0 is undetermined and a worthless-Bitcoin (price=0) equilibrium always coexists with positive-price equilibria. That is the standard, more damning academic read: the GE model cannot pin down a LEVEL at all, only constrain the path given an arbitrary starting point. This strengthens the 'useless as a point-estimate CMA' verdict and should be stated explicitly rather than softened into 'low real drift.'

Mild internal-consistency tension on volatility: synthesis centers vol at ~50%, BELOW realized trailing-5y (57%), justified by 'belief distribution narrows as asset matures.' But the same family stresses that ALL action is belief-driven and the payoff is binary/fat-tailed (Lewis: small probability shifts -> sizeable price swings). Asserting vol COMPRESSES while simultaneously asserting the driver is unstable adoption-probability jumps is in slight tension. 50% is defensible but the compression argument is the weakest link.

Soleimani (2025, arXiv 2512.07886) is a non-peer-reviewed preprint and is correctly flagged as such, but it is load-bearing for the 'endogenous velocity constraint' con. The con should not rest primarily on a non-refereed source; the same circularity point is better supported by Lewis and by the volatility-deters-payment-use logic already present.

The nominal CMA (~8%) sits below the most recent realized trailing-5y window (17%), which is consistent with continued decay and therefore defensible, but the synthesis should make explicit that it is forecasting BELOW the latest realized point (not just decaying toward it) so the reader can judge whether that pace of decay is too aggressive.
Round-2 correction (vol): Vol floor raised from 45% to ~57%; gold-corr (~0.05) left unchanged per instruction (QTM is on the do-not-touch list and already in band).
verdict.corrections: Add the Schilling-Uhlig exchange-rate INDETERMINACY result explicitly: Q0 is undetermined and a price=0 (worthless-Bitcoin) equilibrium always coexists with positive-price ones. This is the canonical academic critique and it reinforces (does not weaken) the 'sanity-bound only, useless as point estimate' verdict — the model constrains the price PATH given an arbitrary start, not the LEVEL. Soften the volatility-compression claim or note its tension with the belief-driven-jump mechanism; 45-60% (center ~50%) is acceptable but the rationale should acknowledge that unstable adoption-probability dynamics could equally keep vol AT or ABOVE realized 57%. State plainly that the ~8% nominal / ~5% real forecast is BELOW the latest realized 5y window (17%), i.e. an explicit continued-decay assumption. No numeric corrections required to the correlation block — gold ~0.05, growth-eq ~0.40, value ~0.30, FI ~0.15, TIPS ~0.20 are all consistent with realized anchors and shaded sensibly toward regime-averaged forwards; the near-zero gold correlation is the correct and important 'tell' that this family rejects the digital-gold thesis.

approaches.name: On-Chain Cost-Basis Valuation (Realized Cap / MVRV / SOPR / Thermocap / HODL Waves)
approaches.description: This family values Bitcoin off its aggregate on-chain cost basis rather than any cashflow or supply-scarcity narrative. Realized Cap "pricestamps" every UTXO at the price it last moved and sums them, producing the network's invested-capital base; Realized Price is that per-coin. Market value is then read RELATIVE to this cost basis: MVRV (= MarketCap/RealizedCap) and SOPR measure aggregate unrealized/realized profit, Thermocap measures cumulative miner security spend, and Realized-Cap HODL Waves decompose the cost basis by coin age. Critically, none of these are absolute valuation models — they are mean-reversion OSCILLATORS calibrated to historical cycle extremes (MVRV ~0.8 at bottoms, >3.2 at tops). A 10-15yr CMA does not fall out cleanly: the only structural forward signal is that Realized Cap acts as a slowly-rising floor (it draws down only -14% to -23% when spot falls -75% to -92%), so a CMA must be built by projecting the growth rate of invested capital (net capital inflow) and assuming MVRV mean-reverts toward ~1.5-2x over a full cycle rather than by reading any point figure off the chart.
key_drivers: Realized Cap = cumulative realized profit minus realized loss = net USD capital ever locked into the network (the invested-capital base / on-chain cost basis)
Realized Price = Realized Cap / circulating supply (aggregate holder cost basis per coin); functions as a soft floor
MVRV ratio = Market Cap / Realized Cap = aggregate unrealized-profit multiple; mean-reverting oscillator (bottoms ~0.8, tops ~3.2-3.7)
MVRV Z-Score = (MarketCap - RealizedCap)/stdev(MarketCap); normalizes extremes for cross-cycle comparison
SOPR (Spent Output Profit Ratio) = realized price of spent coins / price paid; >1 = supply in profit being sold, <1 = capitulation
Thermocap = cumulative USD value of all block rewards + fees ever paid to miners (aggregate security spend); Market-Cap/Thermocap is an on-chain 'P/E'-style ratio
Realized-Cap HODL Waves = age-banded decomposition of Realized Cap (who holds cost basis, long-term vs short-term holders)
Net capital inflow / 'realized cap growth rate' — the only variable that drives a long-horizon trajectory rather than a cyclical signal
pros: Grounded in observable on-chain ledger data (UTXO move-prices), not a narrative or fitted regression — Realized Cap is an accounting identity, not a model assumption

Realized Cap / Realized Price empirically behaves as a rising floor: it has fallen only ~-14% to -23% in bear markets vs spot's -75% to -92%, giving a genuine downside-anchor concept useful for tail/loss-given-bear estimation

MVRV/SOPR oscillators have real ex-post discriminating power at extremes — readings have repeatedly bracketed cycle tops and bottoms (MVRV<1 ≈ ~15% of days marked capitulation, MVRV>3.2 ≈ cycle peaks)
Cost-basis framing maps cleanly to investor behavior (mean reversion toward what holders paid), so it is a behaviorally-honest middleware even if not a CMA
Thermocap ties valuation to a real economic floor (energy/security spend), giving an independent cross-check on the cost-basis story
Unlike Stock-to-Flow and Metcalfe, this family does NOT publish a single point-forecast, so it is harder to weaponize into a spurious 10yr target — its honesty is a feature
cons: Fundamentally an OSCILLATOR, not a valuation model: it tells you where price sits relative to cost basis, never where cost basis (or price) should be in 10-15 years. There is no native long-horizon expected-return output — any CMA is grafted on by the analyst.

Reflexive/circular: Realized Cap is a transformation of past PRICE (each coin stamped at its move-time price). High prices raise realized cap which raises the 'floor' — so the floor is endogenous to the bubble, not an independent fundamental. A permanent 70% drawdown would drag realized price down with it over time.

Thresholds are data-mined on a tiny sample (2-3 full cycles): MVRV>3.7 'overvalued', Z>6.5 'top', M/T~0.000004 'top' are curve-fits with severe lookahead bias and small-n overfitting. Each cycle has hit LOWER MVRV peaks (2013 ~5.7 → later cycles <3) — the calibration visibly decays, mirroring the S2F/Metcalfe post-2021 break critique. Naive use is unsafe.

Predictive performance degrades post-2017/post-futures as markets became more efficient (academic backtests of cost-basis oscillators show Sharpe collapse after 2017); ETF/institutional custody also breaks the on-chain signal because coins move off-chain into wrappers and stop pricestamping.
Supply-side metric noise: lost coins, exchange/wrapper consolidation, and ETF custody distort UTXO age and cost-basis attribution, biasing realized cap and HODL waves.

No correlation, volatility, or cross-asset structure is produced at all — the framework is silent on every CMA covariance input. It cannot, by itself, populate a correlation matrix vs equities/gold/TIPS.

approaches.rich_notes:
METHODOLOGY. Realized Cap (Coin Metrics, Carter/Le Calvez ~2018) = sum over all UTXOs of (coins × price at last on-chain move). Equivalently the cumulative sum of realized profits minus realized losses since genesis — i.e., net USD capital locked into the ledger. Realized Price = Realized Cap / circulating supply = aggregate holder cost basis. MVRV (Puell & Mahmudov, 2018) = Market Cap / Realized Cap = aggregate unrealized-profit multiple; "MVRV − 1 = avg unrealized PnL." MVRV Z-Score = (MarketCap − RealizedCap)/σ(MarketCap). SOPR = realized value of spent coins / value at creation. Thermocap = cumulative USD of all block rewards + fees (aggregate security/energy spend); Market-Cap/Thermocap is an on-chain pseudo-P/E. Realized-Cap HODL Waves (Unchained/Bansal 2018) band the realized cap by coin age.

KEY QUOTES / THRESHOLDS (Glassnode "Mastering the MVRV Ratio"): MVRV 2.2 = 120% aggregate profit; 1.0 = breakeven; 0.8 = −20%. Cycle calibration: MVRV>3.2 ≈ peaks (~6% of days since 2017), >2.4 euphoria (~20%), <1.0 capitulation (~15%), <0.8 cycle lows (~5%). 2013 MVRV hit 5.4-5.7; later cycles topped progressively LOWER (<3 by 2021) — the decay of the threshold is itself the strongest evidence against naive forward use. Other lit cites MVRV>3.7 "overvalued", Z>6.5 "top", M/T≈0.000004 "top." Every report explicitly disclaims "no investment advice / no price forecast."

THE LOAD-BEARING FORWARD SIGNAL. Glassnode "The Realized Cap Foundation": Realized Cap bear-market drawdowns are only −14% to −23% vs spot −75% to −92%, and "Bitcoin has historically found bear market floors at increasingly elevated price ranges over time." This is the ONLY structurally forward-looking element in the whole family — a slowly-rising soft floor — and even it is framed as past behavior, not a fair-value theorem.

BRUTAL HONESTY / CRITIQUES. (1) Oscillator ≠ valuation model: produces no expected return, vol, or correlation. Any CMA is the analyst's graft, not the framework's. (2) Reflexivity/circularity — Realized Cap is a transform of past PRICE, so the "floor" is endogenous to the prior bubble; a permanent regime-down would erode realized price too. It cannot independently anchor fair value. (3) Overfitting / small-n: 2-3 cycles, lookahead-calibrated thresholds, visibly decaying peak-MVRV per cycle — the same pathology the academic literature pins on Stock-to-Flow (spurious cointegration, non-stationarity, post-2021 break) and Metcalfe (naive log-log regressions reject out of sample). Cost-basis oscillators are less egregious than S2F because they don't publish a point target, but their thresholds are no less curve-fit. (4) Efficiency decay: Cretarola/Figà-Talamanca (MDPI Information 2022) — crypto-asset-pricing oscillators backtest profitably pre-2017 but Sharpe collapses after BTC futures launch as markets grew efficient. (5) Measurement breakdown under institutionalization: ETF custody and exchange/wrapper consolidation move coins off-chain or into reused addresses, so post-2024 the UTXO age/cost-basis signal is increasingly blind to the real marginal holder — arguably the framework is least reliable exactly when AUM is largest.

SYNTHESIS REASONING. The scripted empirical anchor (empirical_anchor.json) shows BTC nominal appreciation decaying 142% (full, 2010-2026) → 65% (trailing-10y) → 17% (trailing-5y), vol 103%→69%→57%, and a RISING equity correlation (growth-eq 0.26→0.36→0.56). A 10-15yr forward CMA must extrapolate that decay, not the level. Under THIS approach's cost-basis logic specifically, appreciation is bounded by how fast net invested capital (Realized Cap) can keep growing against an ever-larger base — a decelerating series — plus a modest one-time MVRV mean-reversion to ~1.5-2x. That argues for low-double-digit nominal (~10-13%), i.e. another step below the trailing-5y 17%, with real ~7-10%. I keep vol high (~45-55%) but trimmed, because the rising realized-price floor genuinely compresses left-tail severity over time. Correlations are pure judgment (framework silent): I inherit the anchor's rising-equity-beta trend (growth 0.40-0.55, value 0.30-0.40), small positive FI/TIPS (0.15-0.30), and — importantly for the digital-gold thesis — only a LOW positive gold corr (0.05-0.20). The cost-basis lens provides NO mechanism that would force BTC-gold co-movement up to the 0.5+ a digital-gold narrative wants; historical BTC-gold corr is ~0 (full window −0.01), so I nudge it only slightly positive for a maturing debasement-hedge cohort. All synthesized figures are explicit judgments, not computed statistics.

issues: CITATION MISATTRIBUTION (hard error): The peer-reviewed MDPI paper 'Information' 13(12):560 (2022), cited as the post-2017 efficiency-decay evidence, is authored by Zixiu Yang & Dean Fantazzini, NOT 'Cretarola, Figa-Talamanca et al.' as listed in representative_sources AND in rich_notes critique (4). Cretarola/Figa-Talamanca wrote a DIFFERENT, related strand (sentiment/confidence-based Bitcoin option-pricing models, e.g. SSRN 2908921 / 3042029) but are not the authors of the cited oscillator-backtest paper. The wrong name is repeated twice. Must be corrected to Yang & Fantazzini (2022), MPRA 115508 / DOI 10.3390/info13120560.

The cited Yang-Fantazzini paper's oscillators are crypto-asset pricing models (NVT, NVRV, Metcalfe/NVML, etc.), not the specific MVRV/SOPR/Thermocap cost-basis oscillators this approach centers on. NVRV (network-value-to-realized-value) IS a realized-cap-based metric, so the citation legitimately supports the cost-basis-oscillator-degradation claim — but the research overstates it slightly by implying the paper backtests this family directly. It backtests a broader set in which only some are cost-basis metrics.
The realized-cap link (coinmetrics.io/realized-capitalization/) now resolves to /general-research/realized-capitalization/ — stale path, not fabricated.

MVRV-ratio peak figures (2013 ~5.4-5.7) are stated more precisely than the public record cleanly supports; the cleanly-verified series is the MVRV Z-Score peak decay (~8.8 in 2017 to ~7.1 in 2021). The DIRECTION (declining peaks each cycle) is robustly confirmed for both ratio and Z-score, so the overfitting/decay critique stands; only the exact ratio numbers carry mild uncertainty.

Minor: 'cost-basis oscillators show Sharpe collapse after 2017' is a slight generalization — Yang-Fantazzini found 'almost all' methods worsened, with a few (NVML/Metcalfe) retaining significant Sharpe. So the collapse is broad but not universal; the con is directionally fair but could be stated as 'most, not all'.
Round-2 correction (vol): Vol floor raised from 45% to ~57%; gold-corr (0.05-0.20, framework-silent, not a digital-gold mechanism) left unchanged.
verdict.corrections: Fix the author attribution everywhere: the MDPI Information 13(12):560 (2022) source is Yang, Z. & Fantazzini, D. — 'Using Crypto-Asset Pricing Methods to Build Technical Oscillators for Short-Term Bitcoin Trading' (also MPRA 115508). Remove 'Cretarola, Figa-Talamanca et al.' from that entry (they can be cited separately as the sentiment/option-pricing strand if wanted, but they did not write this paper). Soften critique (4) to: 'most (not all) crypto-asset-pricing oscillators backtest profitably pre-2017 but lose significance after the 2017 futures launch as efficiency rises (Yang & Fantazzini 2022); a few (Metcalfe/NVML) retained significant Sharpe.' Optionally hedge the 2013 MVRV-ratio peak as '~5+ (ratio); Z-score ~8 in 2017 to ~7 in 2021' to match the cleanly-verifiable series. No changes needed to the synthesized CMA numbers — the ~10-13% nominal / 7-10% real / 45-55% vol / low gold-corr graft is defensible and correctly self-flagged as judgment extrapolating the decay (142->65->17%) one step below trailing-5y, consistent with the silent framework and the scripted baseline (57% vol, ~0 gold corr).

approaches.name: Cross-Sectional Factor & Macro-Liquidity Regression
approaches.description: This family treats BTC as a risk asset whose returns are decomposed by regression onto priced factors rather than valued from cashflows or scarcity. Two strands: (1) the cross-sectional/asset-pricing strand (Liu-Tsyvinski-Wu) builds crypto-native factors — a crypto market factor (CMKT), size (CSIZE) and momentum (CMOM), plus network-adoption and investor-attention proxies — and shows a 3-factor model spans the cross-section of coin returns; (2) the macro-liquidity strand (Onramp, post-ETF studies) regresses BTC on global M2, the dollar (DXY) and real rates. A 10-15yr CMA does NOT fall out of these models directly: they are descriptive/explanatory (what moves BTC, and how much variance loads on each factor) rather than predictive of a long-run level. To get a CMA you must feed the regression long-run factor-premium and factor-path assumptions (an equity-risk-premium-style estimate for the crypto market factor, plus a view on the secular liquidity/adoption path) and let the betas translate them — which is why the expected-return output is inherited from the analyst's factor views, not produced by the model.
key_drivers: Crypto market factor (CMKT) — the dominant systematic driver; coin betas to the aggregate crypto market explain most cross-sectional variation
Size factor (CSIZE) — small-cap coins earn a premium; BTC as the largest coin loads negatively, implying lower expected excess return than the alt-coin universe
Momentum factor (CMOM) — strong time-series and cross-sectional momentum; 1-4 week momentum predicts returns (a behavioral/attention driver, not a fundamental one)
Investor-attention / sentiment proxies (Google/social search, flows) — Liu-Tsyvinski find attention strongly forecasts short-horizon returns
Network-adoption factors (active addresses, users) — priced; production-cost factors (hashrate/mining) are NOT priced
Macro-liquidity trio: global M2 (liquidity impulse), USD/DXY, and real yields (discount rate) — weak monthly link, materially stronger at 6-24m horizons
Post-ETF institutionalization — rising loading on the equity/growth (Nasdaq) factor as ETF/corporate flows tie BTC to quarterly equity rebalancing
pros: Empirically grounded and falsifiable — uses standard asset-pricing machinery (Fama-MacBeth, GRS tests, rolling betas) rather than curve-fitting a price level
Correctly characterizes BTC's risk profile: high idiosyncratic/crypto-specific variance, low historical loading on traditional macro factors — directly informative for the correlation cells of a CMA
Captures regime change: the macro-liquidity and post-ETF strands document BTC's rising equity beta and near-zero gold correlation, which a static historical correlation would miss
Honest about predictability: the academic strand attributes short-horizon predictability to attention/momentum (behavioral), not to a fundamental anchor — avoids over-claiming
Separates systematic from idiosyncratic — useful for portfolio construction (how much BTC risk is diversifiable vs priced)
cons: Does NOT produce a long-run expected return on its own — it is descriptive; the CMA appreciation number is smuggled in via an assumed crypto-market-factor premium, so the model launders the analyst's prior rather than generating a forecast

Short, regime-shifting sample: factor premia (esp. CMKT and CMOM) are estimated on ~2014-2022 data dominated by a secular bull market; out-of-sample momentum/size premia in equities have decayed, and there is no reason crypto premia are stable over 10-15yr
Betas are unstable: the very post-ETF literature it relies on shows BTC's equity beta jumping from ~0 to 0.5-0.9, so any CMA built on a point-estimate beta is fragile
The macro-liquidity link is weak month-to-month and the firm-published (Onramp) version is marketing-adjacent — it reports regime medians, not betas, and avoids point forecasts

Naive scarcity/network cousins (Stock-to-Flow, naive Metcalfe) are statistically REJECTED — S2F is spurious regression on two non-stationary, non-cointegrated series with autocorrelated residuals; Metcalfe transaction-count effects are insignificant/negative once autocorrelation and endogeneity are corrected, and both break post-2021. A factor-regression CMA must not borrow their implied appreciation paths
High multicollinearity / small-N: with only BTC (not a panel) the macro regressions have few independent observations at the 6-24m horizons where the signal allegedly lives, inviting overfitting

Logic: under factor-regression discipline BTC's long-run return = its crypto-market-factor beta times an assumed crypto-market premium. Extrapolating the realized decay (full 142% -> 10y 65% -> 5y 17%), the marginal/forward window is already near a maturing-asset risk premium. I take BTC as a high-beta (~1.5-2x) equity-like risk asset over 10-15yr and add a thinning but non-zero adoption/liquidity tailwind, landing ~10% — well below the 17% trailing-5y and far below the 65% 10y, because betas and premia mean-revert as the asset institutionalizes

Decaying from realized 103% (full), 69% (10y) toward the realized trailing-5y ~57% as float deepens and ETF/institutional ownership dampens swings, but the floor is held AT ~57% — I do not assume convergence below realized within the horizon, since the sub-2yr ETF sample does not yet evidence it. Structurally far above equities.

synthesized_outputs.corr_tips: ~0.25-0.35. Slightly higher than nominal FI via the shared real-rate/liquidity channel emphasized by the macro strand; ~0.30
synthesized_outputs.corr_gold: ~0.05-0.15. The thesis-critical cell: despite the 'digital gold' narrative, BOTH realized data (5y 0.045) and the post-ETF literature show near-zero, non-rising co-movement. I hold it low (~0.10) and explicitly reject treating BTC as a gold substitute for diversification math

approaches.rich_notes:
CORE MECHANISM. The factor-regression family answers 'what drives BTC returns and how much,' not 'what is BTC worth.' Liu-Tsyvinski-Wu (JF 2022) is the canonical academic anchor: three crypto-native factors — market (CMKT), size (CSIZE), momentum (CMOM) — span the cross-section of coin returns; ten characteristic-sorted long-short strategies are all absorbed by the 3-factor model. Companion paper (Liu-Tsyvinski, RFS 2021) delivers the load-bearing CMA result: 'Cryptocurrencies have no exposure to most common stock-market and macroeconomic factors or to the returns of currencies and commodities'; returns are instead predicted by crypto-specific momentum and investor-attention proxies. A later strand adds that crypto returns load on NETWORK-adoption factors (user growth) but NOT production factors (mining cost) — directly rejecting the cost-of-production / S2F intuition.

WHY NO NATIVE CMA. None of these papers publishes a 10-15yr appreciation forecast. They report premia (e.g., top-quintile ~11.2%/week, bottom ~2.6%/week; squared weekly Sharpe 0.057 unhedged) and risk decompositions. To get a CMA you must (a) assume a long-run crypto-market-factor premium and (b) assume a factor path (liquidity/adoption), then let betas map it through. That makes the appreciation number an INPUT in disguise — the single most important honesty caveat for this row.

MACRO-LIQUIDITY STRAND. Onramp's M2/DXY/real-rates piece is practitioner/marketing-adjacent: it finds month-to-month M2-BTC correlation 'weak' but '6-24 month horizons strengthen materially,' reports regime medians (expanding-liquidity regimes -> higher median 6/12m returns, lower prob of negative 12m return) and explicitly avoids point forecasts and beta values. Useful for regime overlay, not for a premium estimate. Treat as colour, not academia.

POST-ETF BREAK (critical for correlations). arXiv 2501.09911 (Institutional Adoption and Correlation Dynamics) and arXiv 2512.12815 (ETF Approval & Hedging Properties): rolling BTC-S&P500 correlation jumped from ~0 to ~0.5 sustained, peaking ~0.87 in 2024; BTC-gold correlation 'remained relatively low and did not show a significant positive shift,' explicitly contradicting 'digital gold'; BTC-USD stayed negative/negligible. Conclusion quoted: BTC transitioned 'from an independent, speculative hedge to a conventional risk asset that moves in tandem with global equity markets,' best treated 'as a high-growth technology proxy rather than a defensive asset.' This is why my synthesized growth-equity correlation is the highest cell and gold is held near zero.

BRUTAL HONESTY ON S2F / METCALFE (per brief). Stock-to-Flow: academic and quant critiques converge that S2F regresses two NON-STATIONARY series (price and S2F ratio) without established cointegration; Engle-Granger and Johansen tests fail their preconditions, residuals are heavily autocorrelated, so the headline fit is SPURIOUS REGRESSION. The relationship visibly broke after 2021 (price fell far below the S2F path). Naive Metcalfe: once autocorrelation and endogeneity are corrected, transaction-count coefficients are insignificant or negative; the 2020-21 relationship is non-linear/unstable; best used only as a loose long-term upper bound, not a forecast. A factor-regression CMA must NOT import the implied appreciation paths of either — doing so would launder hype. I have deliberately excluded any S2F/Metcalfe-implied number from the synthesized outputs.

REALIZED ANCHOR (scripted, /GOLDBTC/btc/cma_litreview/empirical_anchor.json). Full window 2010-07..2026-05 (190m): nominal appreciation 142.2%/yr, vol 102.9%, corr growth-eq 0.263 / value-eq 0.241 / FI 0.098 / TIPS 0.152 / GOLD -0.011. Trailing-10y (121m): 65.5%/yr, vol 68.7%, corr growth 0.362 / value 0.292 / FI 0.158 / TIPS 0.248 / GOLD 0.033. Trailing-5y (61m): 17.0%/yr, vol 57.5%, corr growth 0.564 / value 0.367 / FI 0.192 / TIPS 0.301 / GOLD 0.045. The decay path 142->65->17 and the rising equity / flat gold correlations drive every synthesized cell. My forward appreciation (~10%) sits BELOW the trailing-5y level because (i) the decay is monotonic and (ii) factor-regression logic says a maturing, high-beta asset's premium compresses toward an equity-risk-premium multiple, not its bull-market history.

JUDGMENT FLAGS. All synthesized numbers are reasoned judgments under this approach's logic, not computed statistics. Widest uncertainty is on appreciation (could be negative in a secular liquidity-contraction decade) and on whether the equity beta keeps climbing (institutionalization argues yes) vs the crypto-specific idiosyncratic share staying large (Liu-Tsyvinski argue historically yes). Gold correlation is the highest-conviction LOW cell — both realized data and the post-ETF literature reject the digital-gold co-movement story.

issues: Citation accuracy is high but one NBER attribution needs care: the RFS 2021 'Risks and Returns of Cryptocurrency' is correctly NBER w24877 (RFS 34(6):2689-2727). The JF 2022 3-factor paper is NBER w25882 / JF 77:1133-1177. The JSON only labels w24877 and the JF/Wiley link, which is internally consistent, but anyone reusing this should not attach w24877 to the 3-factor paper.

Forward-appreciation logic is partly self-contradicting. The synthesis says BTC is a 'high-beta (~1.5-2x) equity-like risk asset' and lands ~10% nominal, but the realized 5y appreciation (17.0%) was earned at LOWER realized equity correlation/beta than implied by a 1.5-2x equity beta on a ~7-9% equity premium (which would give ~11-18%). The ~10% is defensible as a midpoint but it is NOT mechanically derived from the stated beta x premium; it is anchored to the decay curve and then rationalized. The honesty caveat ('appreciation is an input in disguise') is correctly stated, so this is a transparency strength, not a laundering failure — but the number should be presented as a pure judgment band, not as 'beta times premium.'

Volatility floor of ~45-55% is on the optimistic-compression side. Realized 5y is 57.5% and 10y 68.7%; assuming decay to 45-55% over 10-15yr assumes float-deepening/ETF dampening that the post-ETF literature does NOT yet demonstrate (ETF era is <2yr and vol has not visibly compressed). Defensible as a directional call but the lower bound (45%) is aggressive; a 50-60% band is better supported by the realized series.

corr_value_eq ~0.35 is essentially the realized 5y figure (0.367) — fine, but the JSON itself flags the source is silent on a value cut, so this cell is realized-data-driven, not literature-driven. Should be labeled as such rather than implying the factor literature supports a growth>value split for BTC.

Minor: 'top-quintile coin strategy ~11.2%/week' is a cross-sectional alt-coin long-short result, not a BTC-specific number, and BTC (largest coin) loads NEGATIVELY on size — so this figure should never be read as a BTC return proxy. The JSON mostly handles this but the cited_outputs juxtaposition (11.2%/week next to '66%/yr BTC premium') invites misreading.

Missing critique: the Liu-Tsyvinski momentum/attention predictability is SHORT-HORIZON (1-4 week) and in-sample on 2014-2018 data; subsequent out-of-sample work (e.g., post-2018 replications) finds the crypto momentum/attention premia decay substantially, mirroring equity-factor decay. The cons mention 'decay' generically but do not cite that the very predictability the academic strand rests on has weakened out-of-sample — a sharper version of the existing con.

Missing critique: survivorship / dead-coin bias in the cross-sectional factor construction. Liu-Tsyvinski-Wu's coin universe and the size premium are sensitive to delisted/dead coins; the size premium in particular is partly a microcap-illiquidity / survivorship artifact. Not mentioned.
Round-2 correction (vol): Vol floor raised from 45% to ~57%; gold-corr (0.05-0.15) left unchanged per instruction (factor is on the do-not-touch list).
verdict.corrections: Present the ~9-12% nominal appreciation explicitly as a judgment band, NOT as 'beta x premium' — the stated 1.5-2x equity beta on a 7-9% ERP would imply ~11-18%, which conflicts with the ~10% anchor; reconcile by stating the number is anchored to the realized-decay curve and capped below trailing-5y, with the factor logic as a sanity check rather than the generator. Widen the volatility band to ~50-60%/yr (drop the 45% floor); the ETF era is too short to evidence compression below realized 57.5%. Label corr_value_eq (~0.35) and the growth>value split as realized-data-driven, since the factor literature is silent on a value cut. Add two cons: (a) the academic short-horizon momentum/attention predictability has decayed out-of-sample, weakening the empirical backbone; (b) the cross-sectional size premium is partly survivorship/microcap-liquidity artifact. Clarify that '11.2%/week' is an alt-coin cross-sectional long-short result and BTC loads negatively on size, so it is not a BTC return proxy.

approaches.name: Options-Implied Risk-Neutral Forward & Vol Surface (Deribit DVOL / RND)
approaches.description: This approach extracts what the listed BTC options market prices: a risk-neutral (Q-measure) forward and a full implied-volatility surface (Deribit DVOL is the VIX-style 30-day variance-swap distillation of that surface). From the cross-section of strikes one recovers a risk-neutral density (RND) of the terminal price; from the term structure one reads the market's annualized vol expectation by tenor. Crucially, the risk-neutral forward equals spot times cost-of-carry (futures basis / funding) — under Q the drift is the financing rate, NOT a real-world expected return — so the options surface delivers volatility and a no-arbitrage forward but says nothing directly about 10-15yr appreciation. A CMA only "falls out" if you (a) extrapolate the (downward-sloping, short-dated) vol term structure to a 10-15yr horizon, and (b) graft on a real-world risk premium from a separate P-density estimate (e.g. Martin/Chabi-Yo lower bounds), since the options alone are silent on drift.
key_drivers: Implied volatility surface (level, skew, term structure) across Deribit/CME strikes and expiries
Risk-neutral forward = spot x cost-of-carry (futures basis / perpetual funding rate); the Q-drift is the risk-free/financing rate, not expected return
Risk-neutral density (RND) shape from the second derivative of call prices vs strike (Breeden-Litzenberger) — fat right tail, lognormal-plus-jump
Variance risk premium: gap between implied (Q) and realized (P) variance, the wedge that must be modeled to get from price to physical return
Pricing kernel / risk-aversion needed to convert Q-density to P-density and thus recover an expected return (Almeida-Grith-Miftachov; Martin lower bound)
Option liquidity and longest-available tenor — caps the horizon at which the surface is observable (months, not years)
pros: Purely market-implied and forward-looking: aggregates the positioning of sophisticated option traders in real time, no backward-looking sample dependence
Best-in-class for the VOLATILITY input of a CMA — DVOL and the term structure give a clean, daily, tradeable estimate of expected vol, far better grounded than a historical stdev
No-arbitrage discipline: the forward and RND are internally consistent and replicable, immune to the spurious-regression problems that plague S2F/Metcalfe
Captures the full distribution (skew, kurtosis, crash risk), not just a point — useful for tail-aware / left-tail CMA scenario work

The RND-vs-realized comparison yields a defensible variance risk premium and, with a pricing-kernel assumption, an option-implied expected-return lower bound (Almeida et al. ~66%/yr at 1mo; Martin bound 65.6%) — a genuinely market-anchored premium number
Galaxy and desks use it precisely as a 'maturing into a macro asset' read: the surface's flattening/declining vol IS the decay signal a forward CMA needs
cons: Fundamentally cannot produce an expected appreciation. The risk-neutral forward drifts at the risk-free/funding rate by construction; equating that to a CMA return implies ~0% real appreciation, which is economically wrong for the asset. Any appreciation figure must be imported from a separate model — the options surface is silent on drift. This is the central, disqualifying limitation for a return CMA.

Horizon mismatch is severe: liquid BTC options extend ~6 months (Deribit) to ~12-13 months (CME, through next December); there is NO 10-15yr option. Extrapolating a 30-day DVOL or a 6-month surface to a 10-15yr CMA is a heroic, unvalidated stretch — the term structure is estimated, not observed, at the relevant horizon.

The P-density / pricing-kernel step that rescues an expected return is fragile: estimates swing from ~44% to ~102%/yr across vol regimes (Almeida-Grith-Miftachov), are only 27-day horizon, and assume the short-dated risk premium persists — exactly the assumption a maturing-asset CMA should reject.
Variance risk premium is large and time-varying (1mo VRP collapsed from ~15% to ~2.5% around the 2024 halving), so even the vol read is regime-dependent and can overstate forward vol.

Risk-neutral != physical: short-dated RNDs are dominated by hedging/skew demand and crash insurance, not long-run fundamentals — using them as a 10yr distribution conflates options demand with macro expectation.
Liquidity/venue concentration (Deribit dominant, now Coinbase-owned) and thin deep-OTM long-dated strikes make the long end of any extrapolated surface noisy and manipulable.

Marketing risk: 'options imply $250k' headlines (Galaxy 2026) are wide risk-neutral ranges, NOT directional forecasts; the same surface assigns near-equal odds to $50k and $250k by end-2026. Treating the high tail as an expected value launders a vol read into a return claim.
