approaches.rich_notes:
METHODOLOGY. The options-implied family has two distinct deliverables and it is essential not to conflate them: (1) the risk-neutral forward, which by no-arbitrage equals spot x cost-of-carry — i.e. the futures price / perpetual-funding-implied forward — and whose drift under Q is the risk-free/financing rate, NOT a real-world expected return; and (2) the implied-volatility surface, distilled by Deribit's DVOL into a single VIX-style 30-day annualized vol via variance-swap replication (select two expiries bracketing 30 days, build the smile from order-book depth of 2 BTC across 5 levels, discard ITM and sub-5%-delta wings, interpolate, EMA-smooth over 240 ticks). DVOL=90 => expected daily move ~4.5% (DVOL/sqrt(365)). The surface also yields a full risk-neutral density via Breeden-Litzenberger (second derivative of call price wrt strike); Hou/Hardle et al. (2019, arXiv:1901.04770) and the peer-reviewed Hou et al. (JFE 2020, SVCJ stochastic-vol-with-jumps) and Cao & Celik (Financial Innovation 2021) formalize this.

THE CENTRAL PROBLEM FOR A RETURN CMA. Options price risk, not direction. The risk-neutral measure embeds the market price of risk, so the Q-density's mean is the forward (carry), and the entire premium an investor actually earns is the Q-to-P wedge — invisible in option prices without an external pricing-kernel/risk-aversion assumption. Therefore THIS APPROACH CANNOT, BY CONSTRUCTION, OUTPUT AN EXPECTED APPRECIATION. Any 'options imply X% return' claim is either (a) reading the upper tail of a wide risk-neutral range as an expectation (the Galaxy 2026 '$250k' headline — the SAME surface assigns near-equal odds to ~$50k and ~$250k by EOY 2026, and Galaxy itself calls 2026 'too chaotic to call' and frames the $250k-by-2027 number as a SEPARATE, non-options long-run view), or (b) smuggling in a P-density from a different estimator.

THE ONE LEGITIMATE RETURN SIGNAL — and its limits. Almeida, Grith & Miftachov (2024, arXiv:2410.15195) do the honest thing: they estimate the Q-density from options (SVI vol surface -> RND) AND a P-density from realized returns, and back out the physical premium. They report a Bitcoin Premium averaging ~66%/yr, option-based lower bounds of 65.6% (Martin) and 84.8% (Chabi-Yo & Loudis), a variance risk premium ~14%, and a Sharpe ~0.8 (≈2x S&P). BUT every one of these is a 27-DAY HORIZON number on monthly options (3-120 days), and it swings from ~44% (low-vol regime) to ~102% (high-vol regime). Extrapolating a one-month, regime-conditional risk premium to a 10-15yr CMA is precisely the error a maturing-asset CMA must avoid. The variance risk premium is also unstable — Bitfinex/desk data show 1-month VRP collapsing from ~15% to ~2.5% around the April 2024 halving.

HORIZON MISMATCH. Liquid BTC options reach ~6 months on Deribit and ~12-13 months on CME (six consecutive months plus two December contracts, so through next December). There is no multi-year option; a 10-15yr CMA horizon is 10-20x beyond the observable surface. The long end of any extrapolated term structure is unobserved, thin in deep-OTM long-dated strikes, and venue-concentrated (Deribit dominant, now Coinbase-owned). So the 'CMA' is an extrapolation, not a measurement.

WHAT IT IS ACTUALLY GOOD FOR IN A CMA. The volatility input. DVOL and the term structure are the best available forward vol estimate and far superior to a historical stdev. The realized-vs-implied comparison (BVIX^2 ~0.72 risk-neutral vs BRV ~0.58 realized annual variance in Almeida et al.) gives a defensible VRP. And the surface's flattening / declining DVOL over time is itself the maturation/decay signal a forward CMA wants — Galaxy frames exactly this: 'options pricing and volatility trends indicate bitcoin is maturing into a more macro-like asset rather than a high-growth trade.'

MY SYNTHESIS LOGIC. For appreciation I refuse to report the carry-rate forward as a 'return' (that would imply ~0% real, absurd as a CMA). Instead I take the family's only honest return artifact — the option-implied physical premium — and apply the empirical-anchor decay (full-window 142% -> 10y 65% -> 5y 17% nominal) projected forward, landing ~10% nominal / ~7% real as a 10-15yr center. This is explicitly a judgment overlay, NOT an options output. For volatility I extrapolate the declining DVOL/term-structure to ~50% (below the 57% trailing-5y realized, far above equities). Correlations are NOT producible from a single-asset options surface at all, so all five are pure judgments anchored to the trailing-5y realized matrix with mild mean-reversion: growth-eq ~0.45, value-eq ~0.30, FI ~0.15, TIPS ~0.20, gold ~0.10 (realized gold corr has been ~0.03-0.05, near zero; the digital-gold co-movement the thesis wants simply is not in the data, and the options approach is silent on it).

BOTTOM LINE. As a CMA method, options-implied is the gold standard for the VOL and tail inputs and a disciplined source for a SHORT-HORIZON risk premium, but it is structurally incapable of delivering a 10-15yr expected appreciation or any cross-asset correlation. Used alone it would force a near-0% real return CMA; used as headline-tail readings it launders a vol signal into a fake forecast. Its proper role is to supply the volatility/distribution leg of a CMA whose return leg comes from a different (e.g. stock-to-flow-rejected, demand-adoption, or building-block-premium) model.

issues: Author misattribution: arXiv:2410.15195 'Risk Premia in the Bitcoin Market' has FOUR authors — Caio Almeida, Maria Grith, Ratmir Miftachov, AND Zijin Wang. The research cites it as 'Almeida, Grith & Miftachov' throughout, dropping Wang. Minor but a real citation error.

Imprecise attribution of the '~44% to ~102%' range. Verified against the paper, but this spread is NOT the Bitcoin-Premium point-estimate range across regimes. The BP point estimates are 62% (low-vol) to 69% (high-vol). The 43.99%-102.27% range mixes two cross-sections: Martin lower bound in LV (43.99%) vs Chabi-Yo upper-method in HV (102.27%). The con sentence 'swings from ~44% to ~102%/yr across vol regimes' conflates method-choice with regime, overstating regime sensitivity of the central estimate.

Missing critique: Breeden-Litzenberger RND extraction is an ill-posed inverse problem. The second derivative of call price wrt strike amplifies bid-ask/microstructure noise, forcing heavy SVI smoothing and arbitrary tail extrapolation — so the 'full distribution / fat right tail' the pros tout is partly an artifact of the smoothing kernel, especially in the thin deep-OTM strikes the research already flags as noisy. This estimation fragility is not raised.

Missing critique: Deribit options are inverse (coin-margined, BTC-settled). The Q-measure numeraire is BTC, not USD, so the 'risk-free/financing rate' that defines the Q-drift is a crypto-native funding/basis rate, not a USD risk-free rate. This complicates the clean 'forward = spot x cost-of-carry' story and the Q-to-P conversion. The research treats carry/funding loosely without flagging the inverse-option numeraire subtlety.

Missing critique: peso-problem / survivorship in the P-density. The 66% physical premium is backed out from a short, upward-biased realized sample (same bias driving the 142%->17% appreciation decay). So the 'one legitimate return signal' inherits BTC's realized-return overstatement — the Q-to-P wedge is contaminated by the same small-sample bias the research warns about elsewhere, undercutting it as an 'honest return artifact' even at 1mo.

Gold-corr synthesis (0.10) is a mild upward nudge above the realized ~0.03-0.05, justified only by 'a maturing digital-store-of-value thesis.' This is disclosed, but it is the one place the synthesis leans on narrative the data and the method itself contradict (research admits 'the digital-gold co-movement the thesis wants simply is not in the data').

Round-2 correction (vol): Vol floor raised from 45% to ~57% (forward-implied alone cannot justify a floor below realized in a sub-2yr ETF sample); gold-corr (~0.10) left unchanged per instruction (options on do-not-touch list).
verdict.corrections: Fix the citation to four authors: Almeida, Grith, Miftachov & Wang (2024). Re-describe the '44%-102%' figure precisely: BP point estimates are 62% (low-vol) to 69% (high-vol) annualized; the wider 43.99%-102.27% band is the spread across the two lower-bound METHODS (Martin LV vs Chabi-Yo HV), and time-series lower bounds exceeded 200% in stress and ~50-100% in calm 2019 — so cite it as method×regime spread, not regime spread. Keep the 66%/yr (annualized from 1mo options), Martin 65.64%, Chabi-Yo 84.78%, VRP 14%, Sharpe 0.8 (~2x S&P 0.5) — all verified correct. Pull the gold correlation down to ~0.05 (the realized value) rather than nudging to 0.10, since the method produces no cross-asset moment and the data shows ~0. Add the three missing critiques (B-L ill-posedness, inverse-option numeraire, peso/survivorship contamination of the P-density premium) to cons.

approaches.name: Equilibrium / Game-Theoretic Security-Utility Pricing
approaches.description: This family treats Bitcoin not as a cash-flow asset but as a token whose fundamental value is the present value of a stream of net transactional benefits (Biais et al., JoF 2023) and/or the equilibrium price that simultaneously clears asset demand and induces enough mining hashrate to keep the chain secure against attack (Chen 2024 security-utility Nash equilibrium; Houy 2014; Alden's fee-based security model). Value is endogenous: today's price depends on expected future prices (because transactional usefulness and security both scale with price), which yields a self-referential fixed point. A 10-15yr CMA does NOT fall out cleanly — these models are explicitly positive (explaining price formation and volatility) rather than normative forecasts. The one robust quantitative takeaway is decompositional: in calibration, only a minority of Bitcoin return variance maps to changes in net transactional benefits; the majority is "extrinsic" / sunspot volatility, so any point forecast inherits enormous uncertainty and the models predict perpetual high vol and multiple equilibria rather than a single expected return.
key_drivers: Net transactional benefits: the flow utility of holding/using BTC for transactions and store-of-value, indexed empirically (Biais et al.)
Self-referential fixed point: fundamental value depends on future prices, generating multiple equilibria and sunspot (extrinsic) volatility even with constant fundamentals
Security budget = block subsidy + transaction fees; must remain large enough that cost-to-attack > attack payoff (Chen, Houy, Alden)
Endogenous hashrate via free-entry zero-profit miner condition: F^-1(H) = P*(B+Phi)/H
Halving dynamics: as block subsidy B -> 0, security must be carried by fees Phi; viability of the fee market is the central open question
Attack-cost / security-utility coupling: higher price -> larger security budget -> more attack resistance -> supports demand (reflexive loop)
Fixed supply Q clears against speculative + transactional demand D(P, security)
pros: Genuinely peer-reviewed (Journal of Finance) and microfounded; derives value from first principles rather than curve-fitting, unlike S2F/Metcalfe
Honestly explains why BTC is so volatile: multiple equilibria + sunspots are a feature of the model, not noise to be assumed away
Provides a falsifiable lower-bound discipline — the chain is only worth holding if the fee-funded security budget can deter attack as subsidy decays, tying long-run value to real adoption/fee demand
Avoids the 'no cashflow so unvaluable' dead-end by identifying transactional-benefit and security streams as the economic substitute for cashflow
Comparative statics (halving lowers P and H together; fee market must develop) give a coherent narrative for the appreciation-decay path
cons: Produces essentially NO usable point CMA: no closed-form steady-state price, no expected-return number, no volatility forecast, no correlation outputs — the papers explicitly decline to forecast
Multiple-equilibria / sunspot result means the model is consistent with almost any price path, which is intellectually honest but useless for a single 10-15yr expected return

The fee-based-security terminal state is unsolved: Chen, Houy and Alden all flag 'whether fee demand can fund security' as an OPEN question — the long-run equilibrium may not exist or may be fragile (tragedy-of-the-commons free-riding on security)
Net-transactional-benefit indices are noisy proxies; calibration shows fundamentals explain only a minority of return variance, so the 'fundamental' anchor is weak
Reflexivity (price -> security -> value) makes the model prone to self-fulfilling collapse as well as boom; it does not pin down which equilibrium prevails

These academic models are frequently conflated in marketing with S2F/Metcalfe, which the literature largely REJECTS as spurious: S2F is a regression of two non-stationary series (spurious cointegration, serially correlated residuals) that broke decisively post-2021 (predicted ~$100k+ in 2022, BTC crashed); naive Metcalfe network-value fits are likewise overfit and non-robust. Do not let the rigorous equilibrium work launder the discredited scarcity/network curves.

approaches.rich_notes:
METHODOLOGY. Two distinct but related academic strands, plus practitioner work, share the 'value = transactional-benefit + security, not cashflow' premise.

(1) Biais, Bisière, Bouvard, Casamatta & Menkveld, 'Equilibrium Bitcoin Pricing,' Journal of Finance 78(2), 2023, pp. 967-1014 (the seed DOI 10.1111/jofi.13119 in the prompt resolves to the published 10.1111/jofi.13206). General-equilibrium overlapping-generations-style model: 'The fundamental value of the cryptocurrency is its stream of net transactional benefits, which depend on its future prices.' Because current fundamentals depend on FUTURE prices, the pricing equation is self-referential -> multiple equilibria and SUNSPOTS -> 'extrinsic volatility, that is, cryptocurrency prices fluctuate even when fundamentals are constant.' They build empirical indices of net transactional benefits and calibrate; key qualitative result: 'part of the variations in Bitcoin returns reflects changes in net transactional benefits, but a LARGER share reflects extrinsic volatility.' This is the single most important, citable, peer-reviewed quantitative-flavored finding in the whole family — and it is a humility result, not a price target. No expected return, vol, or correlation numbers are published.

(2) Liang Chen, 'A Game-Theoretic Foundation for Bitcoin's Price: A Security-Utility Equilibrium,' arXiv 2508.06071, 2024 (working paper, NOT peer-reviewed). Defines a 'Rational-Expectations Security-Utility Nash Equilibrium' (RESUNE). Market clears on fixed supply Q: D(P*, ς(P*,H(P*))) = Q (Eq.6), with free-entry miner zero-profit condition F^-1(H) = P*(B+Phi)/H (Eq.2), where B=block subsidy, Phi=fees, H=hashrate, ς=security via a global-games coordination model. NO closed-form price, NO steady-state appreciation/vol, only comparative statics (halving lowers P and H jointly) and a VAR for empirical testing. Explicitly: 'as B->0, miner revenue becomes entirely dependent on fees' and 'whether the demand for block space can generate such fees is a critical open question for Bitcoin's future.' So the terminal equilibrium is unsolved.

(3) Nicolas Houy, 'The Economics of Bitcoin Transaction Fees,' SSRN 2014 — early game-theoretic treatment of the fee market and the zero/positive-fee equilibria; foundational for the security-budget strand (couldn't fetch full text, 403; cited from secondary summaries and its canonical role).

(4) Lyn Alden, 'Bitcoin: Fee-Based Security Modeling' (practitioner, ~2021). Most concrete numbers, but practitioner not academic: argues long-run security spend should be ~0.5-1.5% of market cap/yr; 2020 snapshot ~2.5% of $203.5B cap, ~$5B miner revenue, ~$44 all-in cost/tx; frames the transition as 'middling risk.' Quotes Satoshi: 'in 20 years there will either be very large transaction volume or no volume.' No price target — binary framing: sufficient fee demand sustains security and value, or BTC fails the transition.

BRUTAL HONESTY ON S2F/METCALFE. The prompt's mandate: this rigorous equilibrium work is routinely conflated in marketing with stock-to-flow and Metcalfe curves, which the academic/quant literature LARGELY REJECTS in naive form. S2F (PlanB) regresses two non-stationary I(1) series (price on stock/flow ratio) -> classic SPURIOUS regression; residuals are serially correlated; Engle-Granger/Johansen 'cointegration' claims do not survive proper specification (see Burger's multi-part review; Matt Paz 'Falsifying Stock-to-Flow'). The model fit 2015-2021 then BROKE: it implied ~$100k+ in 2022, BTC fell to ~$16k. Naive Metcalfe (value ∝ users^2 / active addresses^2) is an overfit, non-robust curve with no stationary error-correction. NONE of this belongs in a CMA except as a cautionary note; the equilibrium models above are the defensible version of 'fundamental' Bitcoin pricing and they pointedly do NOT produce the tidy exponential price targets the scarcity/network curves advertise.

WHY THE CMA IS A JUDGMENT, NOT A MODEL OUTPUT. The family is positive, not normative — it explains volatility and price formation, declines to forecast. My synthesized_outputs are MY extrapolation under the family's logic, anchored to the prompt's realized-decay baseline (142->65->17 %/yr). Scripted extrapolation (decaying the growth RATE ~10%/yr with a ~7% mature-risk-asset floor over 15yr) yields ~9% nominal average, ~7% terminal, ~6.5% real — I report ~8-10% nominal / ~6-7% real. Vol stays high (~55-70%) precisely BECAUSE the model predicts persistent sunspot/extrinsic volatility and multiple equilibria. Correlations are weak/unstable: the demand side is speculative risk-on (gives modest + to growth equities, near-zero to fixed income, mild + to gold via the store-of-value/security framing). Critically, this family does NOT validate a tight BTC-gold correlation or an inflation-hedge property — value here is transactional-benefit + security, not a CPI or scarcity claim — so the 'digital gold' thesis gets only weak, qualified support (corr_gold ~+0.1 to +0.3). All correlation/vol numbers are reasoned judgments, flagged as such, since the source literature is silent.

issues: Citation audit: all five representative sources verify with correct author/title/year/venue. Biais et al., 'Equilibrium Bitcoin Pricing,' Journal of Finance 78(2), 2023, pp. 967-1014 (the published DOI 10.1111/jofi.13206 is correct; the noted seed DOI 10.1111/jofi.13119 collision is handled correctly). The paper's core claims (fundamental value = stream of net transactional benefits depending on future prices; sunspots/multiple equilibria/extrinsic volatility; 'a LARGER share reflects extrinsic volatility') are quoted accurately and not overstated. No fabrication.

Chen 2024 (arXiv 2508.06071) is correctly labeled a working paper, NOT peer-reviewed. The cited equation F^-1(H)=P*(B+Phi)/H (Eq.2), the global-games 'security = 1 minus P(51% attack)' definition, and the verbatim open-question quote ('whether the demand for block space can generate such fees is a critical open question') all verified against the paper's HTML. Correctly stated that it yields only comparative statics + a VAR, no point forecast.

Houy 2014 (SSRN 2400519) verified; the research's characterization is actually conservative relative to the source. Houy's headline result is stronger than 'open question': he shows a non-binding block-size limit with competitive fees 'cannot guarantee the very existence of Bitcoin in the long-term.' The cons section could legitimately cite this as a near-impossibility result, not merely an unsolved one. Minor under-claim, not an error.

Alden number is slightly imprecise but in-bounds: the ~2.5%-of-market-cap 2020 security-spend snapshot and the ~0.5-1.5% long-run target verify. The '$44 all-in cost/tx' figure is an Alden-specific all-in metric distinct from the ~$2.86 average sender FEE — these are different quantities and the research labels it 'all-in cost/tx' correctly, so no conflation. Practitioner (non-academic) tag is accurate.

S2F/Metcalfe rejection is well-founded and not laundering hype: the spurious-regression critique (two non-stationary I(1) series, serially correlated residuals, post-2021 break with ~$100k+ predicted in 2022 vs ~$16k realized) is consistent with the published literature (e.g., MDPI J. Risk Financial Manag. 17(10):443 and multiple quant reviews). Matt Paz 'Falsifying Stock-to-Flow' is correctly cited as an independent critique, not academia. The mandate to keep these OUT of the CMA except as a cautionary note is honored.

Synthesized appreciation (~8-10% nom / ~6-7% real) is a defensible extrapolation but should be flagged as on the OPTIMISTIC edge of the realized-decay path. Decaying 142->65->17 the research's own '%/yr terminal ~7%' implies the NEXT regime point is well under 17%, not 9% average — the ~9% average is buoyed by a ~7% mature-asset floor that this family does NOT endorse (the model produces no floor; it permits collapse equilibria). The number is reasonable as judgment but is a modest upward lean past what the family supports.

Synthesized vol (~55-70%) is the most defensible synthesized figure and is, if anything, slightly LOW against the scripted baseline (57-103% realized). The model's persistent-sunspot prediction justifies elevated vol; keeping the floor at 55% rather than letting it decay toward equities is correct and consistent with the literature.

corr_gold (+0.1 to +0.3) is honest and correctly REFUSES the tight digital-gold/inflation-hedge story; this aligns with the ~0 realized gold correlation in the baseline. No issue — this is the framing working as intended.

Missing critique (minor): the synthesis does not surface that the Biais et al. calibration is in-sample and the net-transactional-benefit indices are not out-of-sample validated, so even the 'minority of variance from fundamentals' result is fragile. Also absent: the Budish (2018) 'economic limits' / cost-to-attack-must-exceed-flow critique, which is the canonical academic argument that a fee-only security budget is structurally insufficient at scale — a stronger, more citable version of the cons section's open-question point.
Round-2 correction (corr_gold): Gold-corr re-centered from 0.1-0.3 to 0.0-0.10; vol (55-70%) left unchanged per instruction — the equilibrium/sunspot row correctly resists compression.
verdict.corrections: Add a one-line caveat that the ~8-10% nominal synthesized appreciation leans to the optimistic edge of the family's own logic: the model provides NO mature-asset floor (it permits collapse equilibria), so the ~7% terminal floor is an imported assumption, not a model output — a fully model-consistent reading would admit a materially wider/lower band. Optionally strengthen the cons by citing Houy's actual result (competitive-fee + non-binding block size 'cannot guarantee the very existence of Bitcoin in the long-term') and Budish (2018) on the cost-to-attack > flow constraint, which are stronger, more citable forms of the fee-market-viability concern. No correction needed to vol, gold, or the S2F/Metcalfe handling — those are accurate.

approaches.name: Discounted-Utility / Monetary-Premium DCF (Moneyness Analogue)
approaches.description: This family forces Bitcoin into a DCF-style frame even though it has no cashflow, by treating its "moneyness" — the utility flow from serving store-of-value / medium-of-exchange / unit-of-account functions — as an implicit dividend, then discounting a terminal monetary-premium value. Two academic sub-strands exist. (1) A market-to-fundamental ratio strand (Liu & Zhang's Price-to-Utility / PU ratio) proxies the store-of-value "utility" via on-chain UTXO staking ratios and asks whether price is rich or cheap to that utility, predicting LONG-horizon (not short) returns via mean-reversion of the ratio. (2) A unified-discounting strand (Papadogiannis; "Valuing Scarcity") models scarcity as a latent state variable whose "monetization function" maps into pseudo-cashflows or a terminal resale value, discounted at an effective rate c_eff = f(benchmark cost of capital c, belief-distortion ratio K). A 10–15yr CMA does not fall out cleanly: the model yields a fair-value LEVEL (or a rich/cheap signal), and an expected return only emerges by assuming the price-to-utility ratio mean-reverts AND the underlying utility/TAM grows along an adoption S-curve — i.e., the CMA is really a TAM-penetration forecast wearing DCF clothing.
key_drivers: Utility/moneyness proxy growth — on-chain activity, active addresses, transaction value, and UTXO staking ratio (Liu-Zhang use staking ratio as the store-of-value proxy)
Total addressable market (TAM) of the monetary functions BTC competes for — gold, offshore/store-of-value wealth, FX/settlement, central-bank reserves — and BTC's penetration share of each
Effective discount rate c_eff = benchmark opportunity cost c times belief-distortion ratio K (Papadogiannis); a very high required return reflecting adoption/survival risk
Probability of monetary adoption / survival — implicit Pr(BTC becomes a durable global store of value) that scales the terminal value
Mean-reversion speed of the market-to-fundamental (PU) ratio — converts a level signal into an expected return
Terminal resale / monetary-premium value at horizon end (no perpetuity of cashflows; value is entirely the terminal moneyness stock)
Macro/liquidity regime — real rates and money-supply growth shift the convenience yield on a non-yielding monetary asset
pros: Honest about the absence of cashflow — instead of faking a dividend it explicitly models a utility/monetary-premium flow or a terminal scarcity value, which is the economically correct object for a non-productive asset

Provides a falsifiable rich/cheap signal: the PU ratio is empirically shown to predict LONG-horizon BTC returns out-of-sample and to beat buy-and-hold and naive market-timing in backtests (Liu & Zhang)
Grounds the proxy in classic monetary theory (medium-of-exchange / store-of-value / unit-of-account) and unique blockchain accounting (UTXO), rather than ad hoc curve-fitting

The unified-discounting variant (Papadogiannis) restores algebraic comparability with equities/gold under one DCF identity, which is exactly what a CMA committee needs to slot BTC next to other building blocks

Naturally accommodates appreciation DECAY: as the TAM penetration S-curve flattens and the PU ratio normalizes, implied forward returns fall toward a gold-like drift — the right shape for a 10–15yr CMA
cons: Garbage-in: the 'utility' proxy is a choice, not a fact. UTXO staking ratios, active addresses, and on-chain volume are gameable, regime-dependent, and only loosely tied to monetary value; the PU ratio's predictive edge is in-sample/backtest and over a short, bull-dominated history (2011–2020).

It is TAM-penetration forecasting in DCF costume. The number that drives everything — Pr(adoption) and terminal share of gold/FX/reserves — is an unfalsifiable prior. Marketing 'academic' DCFs (ARK $1.2–2.4M by 2030; VanEck $2.9M by 2050 ~15% CAGR) are sensitive almost entirely to the penetration assumption, not the discounting math.

Sibling naive models are REJECTED by the peer-reviewed econometrics. Stock-to-Flow regressions are spurious: S2F and price are both non-stationary (I(1)/trending), Engle–Granger cointegration fails its own preconditions, residuals are serially correlated, and the model broke post-2021 (predicted ~$100k in 2022; BTC crashed). Metcalfe/PM ratios likewise have little short-run predictive power and treat all users identically. The PU-ratio paper itself concedes traditional fundamental-to-market ratios fail short-term.

The effective discount rate c_eff and belief-distortion K (Papadogiannis) are not independently observable — they are calibrated to fit observed price, so the framework can rationalize almost any valuation ex post (low falsifiability).

No native volatility or correlation output. The family produces a fair-value level / expected return; vol and the correlation vector must be imported from realized data or asserted — so it contributes nothing to the risk side of a CMA on its own.

Survivorship and reflexivity: 'utility' rises with price (more holders/activity when number-go-up), so utility-as-fundamental and price are mutually endogenous — undercutting the claim that one anchors the other.

cited_outputs.appreciation_nominal: n/a (academic PU/scarcity papers publish fair-value/relative-value signals, not a 10-15yr annualized CMA). Marketing cousins in the same family that DO publish a number: VanEck ~15%/yr nominal to 2050 (base $2.9M); ARK ~53%/yr base / 32% bear / 72% bull CAGR to 2030.
cited_outputs.volatility: n/a (source silent — PU/DCF papers output value, not a forward vol; Liu-Zhang only plot realized BTC return distributions)
cited_outputs.corr_gold: n/a (source silent — gold appears only as a TAM benchmark for penetration share, not as a published correlation)

synthesized_outputs.appreciation_nominal: ~10-13%/yr (judgment, not a computed stat). Under this approach's own logic the PU ratio mean-reverts and the monetary-premium TAM follows a decaying adoption S-curve, so forward return must extrapolate BTC's appreciation DECAY (142->65->17%/yr as it matured), not its level. I blend a front-loaded ~25-30% early window decaying toward a terminal gold-plus drift, giving ~10-13% annualized over a 10-15yr horizon — close to VanEck's 15% base but haircut for adoption/survival risk and ratio normalization.
synthesized_outputs.appreciation_real: ~7-10%/yr (nominal less ~3% long-run inflation); explicitly a judgment under the model's terminal store-of-value premise, with wide error bars.
synthesized_outputs.volatility: ~55-60%/yr annualized. The DCF/moneyness frame implies vol compresses as the monetary premium matures, but the floor is held AT realized trailing-5y ~57% — the sub-2yr ETF sample does not yet evidence compression below realized — still multiples of equity vol over 10-15yr.
synthesized_outputs.corr_growth_eq: +0.30 to +0.45 (judgment). As a high-beta, liquidity-sensitive monetary call option, BTC's monetary premium expands in risk-on/easy-money regimes, co-moving with long-duration growth equities; I expect this to persist but soften as adoption broadens.
synthesized_outputs.corr_value_eq: +0.10 to +0.20 (judgment). Weaker macro/liquidity linkage to value equities than to growth.
synthesized_outputs.corr_fi_nominal: -0.10 to +0.10 (judgment, near zero). The convenience-yield-on-money channel makes BTC react to real rates and money growth, not coupon duration; sign flips by regime (debasement-hedge vs risk-asset).
synthesized_outputs.corr_tips: -0.20 to +0.10 (judgment). To the extent the thesis is a real store of value, BTC should lean negatively to real yields (like gold) — rising real rates raise the opportunity cost of a non-yielding monetary asset and compress its premium.
synthesized_outputs.corr_gold: ~0.0-0.10 (judgment). The model treats gold as the primary TAM BTC penetrates, so by construction it needs BTC and gold to share a debasement/real-rate factor — yet realized co-movement is only intermittently and mildly positive, averaging ~0. This is the load-bearing contradiction: you cannot value BTC off gold's TAM (which assumes substitution / co-movement) while observing near-zero realized gold correlation. I keep it at the bottom of the 0.0-0.15 band, not the high correlation the moneyness narrative implies.

approaches.rich_notes:
METHODOLOGY. The defining move of this family is to supply the missing 'cashflow' of a DCF by reinterpreting Bitcoin's monetary utility as the payoff. Three concrete academic implementations:

1) Liu & Zhang, 'Cryptocurrency Valuation: An Explainable AI Approach' (arXiv 2201.12893, 2022/2023; presented at Computing Conf., acknowledges Campbell Harvey, Lin William Cong, Ye Li). They build a market-to-fundamental ratio, the Price-to-Utility (PU) ratio, drawing on classic monetary economics and constructing fundamental proxies for all three money functions: medium-of-exchange, store-of-value, and unit-of-account. The innovation is proxying store-of-value via STAKING RATIOS derived from Bitcoin's UTXO accounting (i.e., coins dormant/held = store-of-value demand). Verbatim findings: 'different from the stock market, fundamental-to-market ratios have little predictive power on short-term BTC returns'; 'PU ratio... effectively predict[s] long-term BTC returns [better] than alternative methods'; the Price-to-Metcalfe (PM) ratio 'has better potential... than PE and NVT ratios' but 'treats users with different token amounts indifferently and overlooks inactive users who hoard.' A PU-guided trading strategy beats buy-and-hold and market-timing in backtest. This is a RELATIVE-value / long-horizon return-predictability result, NOT a CMA — there is no published 10-15yr appreciation, vol, or correlation figure. Fig.1 only plots realized BTC return distributions over 1/7/30/90/180/360-day windows, 2011-2020.

2) Papadogiannis, 'Unifying DCF Valuation Across Traditional and Cryptoassets' (SSRN 5363661, posted 2025-07-23) and the companion dual-risk papers (SSRN 5252774, 5278419, 5226017). Core identity: separate a benchmark discount rate c (external opportunity cost) from a valuation-distortion ratio K (belief-based deviation from unbiased expectations); their interaction gives an effective discount rate c_eff that rationalizes investor-implied valuations. Cryptoassets that 'lack income streams' are valued via a terminal RESALE value plus, for DeFi, synthetic staking yields. Back-tests on VTI (equity), GLD (gold), BTC-USD using only observable total-return prices and a chosen benchmark rate. CRITIQUE: because c and K are reverse-engineered from observed price, the framework is descriptive/rationalizing rather than predictive — it can fit any price, so it does not independently pin a forward CMA.

3) 'Valuing Scarcity: A General Framework' (Financial Economics Letters, Anser Press, 2025). Thesis: 'scarcity is the fundamental economic origin of value across all asset classes'; scarcity is a latent, time-varying state variable estimated by state-space methods; 'monetization functions map these scarcity states into observable or forecasted cash flows,' giving a universal DCF that establishes algebraic equivalence between terminal-value assets (BTC, gold) and income assets (equities, bonds). Abstract publishes no BTC fair value.

4) CFA Institute, 'Bitcoin Valuation: Four Methods' (2023) + Cryptoassets Valuation Guide. The four: Alternatives Comparison (BTC at gold's ~$11.5T cap implies >$500k/coin — a pure TAM/penetration argument), Production Cost (floor), US-Dollar-Policy/liquidity assessment, and Long-Term-Holder conviction (a moneyness/HODL proxy that maps to Liu-Zhang's staking-ratio store-of-value idea). CFA explicitly provides NO discount rate, no probability model, no expected-return calc — confirming the family's CMA-output gap.

HOW A CMA FALLS OUT (and why imperfectly): expected return = [terminal monetary-premium value (TAM x penetration x Pr(adoption)) / price today]^(1/H) - 1, plus any mean-reversion of the current PU ratio. Every load-bearing input — penetration share of gold/FX/reserves, Pr(survival), c_eff — is a prior. This is why the 'academic DCF' and the marketing DCF converge in structure: ARK (2030 bear/base/bull $500k/$1.2M/$2.4M = 32%/53%/72% CAGR; TAM ~$200T ex-gold, penetration 1%/2.5%/6.5%) and VanEck ($2.9M base by 2050 ~15% CAGR; 5-10% of intl trade settlement + reserve share) are the same TAM-penetration engine. They belong in this row as the practitioner expression of the academic frame, but must be flagged as penetration-assumption-driven, not discounting-driven.

BRUTAL-HONESTY / REJECTED COUSINS. The naive scarcity models in the same CFA 'four methods' list are rejected by econometrics and must not be laundered: (a) Stock-to-Flow (PlanB) — S2F and price are non-stationary/trending; OLS is spurious with serially-correlated residuals; Engle-Granger cointegration tests fail their own preconditions (Burger/Stolte, Amdax). Predicted ~$100k in 2022; BTC crashed instead — a clean out-of-sample failure and structural break. (b) Metcalfe's law / network-value models — better than NVT/PE per Liu-Zhang but still weak short-run, ignore holding concentration and dormant hoarders, and suffer the same non-stationarity. (c) Reflexivity problem cuts the whole family: 'utility' (active addresses, on-chain volume, staking ratio) rises WITH price, so the fundamental and the price are endogenous, weakening the anchor.

WHY MY SYNTHESIZED NUMBERS. The task's realized baseline shows appreciation decaying 142->65->17%/yr with maturity (decay ratios ~0.46 then ~0.26). A 10-15yr CMA under THIS model's logic must continue that decay toward a terminal store-of-value drift, because both the PU ratio mean-reverts and the adoption S-curve flattens. I take a front window ~25-30% decaying to a terminal gold-plus ~7%, blending to ~10-13% nominal / ~7-10% real over the horizon — deliberately below VanEck's 15% to haircut adoption/survival risk. Vol ~45-55% and falling. Correlations are judgments the model does NOT itself produce: I anchor corr_gold modestly positive (+0.15 to +0.30) — central to the digital-gold thesis but realized co-movement has been weaker and more intermittent than the narrative claims; corr to growth equities highest (+0.30 to +0.45) via the liquidity/risk-on channel; corr to TIPS mildly negative via the real-rate opportunity-cost channel (the gold analogue). All correlation and vol figures are reasoned judgments, not computed statistics, and carry wide error bars.

issues: MISATTRIBUTION: The CFA Institute 'Bitcoin Valuation: Four Methods' (2023) article is authored by Rob Price, CFA, NOT Robert Stammers. Verified at the cited URL. Everything else in that citation is verbatim correct: the four methods (alternatives comparison, production cost, US-dollar/liquidity policy, holder conviction), the gold ~$11.5T cap implying >$500k/coin, and the absence of any discount rate / probability model / expected-return calc. Fix the author name; the rest stands.

OVERSTATED CRITIQUE: The Burger/Stolte (Amdax) S2F takedown is presented as a clean 'Engle-Granger cointegration fails its own preconditions' rejection. In reality the SAME author (Burger) raised spurious-regression in Part II but then in Part III/IV verified that cointegration DID hold under certain specifications (partly walking back the pure-spurious claim). The cited Part-II link supports the spurious concern, but framing it as a final cointegration-fails verdict overstates the literature. The independent fact that S2F broke out-of-sample post-2021 (predicted ~$100k in 2022, BTC crashed) is correct and survives regardless.

VOL FLOOR BELOW REALIZED: Synthesized vol of ~45-55% declining sits below the stated realized baseline of ~57-103%. Starting the FORWARD band at 45-55% when the realized floor is 57% requires an aggressive vol-compression assumption (speculator->allocator shift). The argument is legitimate but the bottom of the band (45%) is optimistic versus the anchor and should be widened up or floored near ~55%.

GOLD-CORR LEANS INTO NARRATIVE DESPITE DISCLAIMER: corr_gold +0.15 to +0.30 sits above the stated realized ~0 gold correlation. The synthesis is admirably honest (it flags this as 'load-bearing' and concedes realized co-movement is 'weaker and more intermittent than the narrative claims'), but still publishes a positive band over a ~0 realized anchor. For the keystone digital-gold number, the band should be re-centered toward 0 (e.g. 0.0 to +0.20) to match realized rather than the thesis.

MISSING CRITIQUE - non-ergodicity / sample size: The whole CMA hinges on the PU-ratio MEAN-REVERSION SPEED, but BTC has only ~1.5 monetary cycles of history (2011-2020 in the cited Liu-Zhang sample, bull-dominated). The mean-reversion speed is effectively unidentified statistically; this is a deeper problem than the listed in-sample/backtest con and is not surfaced.

MISSING CITATION - Cong, Li & Wang 'Tokenomics: Dynamic Adoption and Valuation' (Review of Financial Studies, 2021) is the canonical structural dynamic-asset-pricing model for tokens with endogenous user adoption and is the natural rigorous academic counterpart to this family. It is omitted despite Lin William Cong being explicitly acknowledged in the Liu-Zhang paper this row leans on.
Round-2 correction (corr_gold/vol): Gold-corr re-centered from 0.15-0.30 to 0.0-0.10 with the TAM-substitution contradiction explicit; vol floor raised from 45% to ~57% (named by critic).
verdict.corrections: Author of the CFA 'Four Methods' article is Rob Price, CFA, not Robert Stammers (fix the representative_sources entry). Re-center corr_gold toward the realized ~0 anchor (e.g. 0.0 to +0.20) rather than +0.15 to +0.30, since the research's own text concedes realized co-movement is near-zero/intermittent. Raise the vol floor: forward vol band should not start below the realized floor of ~57% without an explicit aggressive-compression caveat (e.g. ~50-60% declining, not 45-55%). Soften the Burger/Stolte framing from 'cointegration fails its own preconditions' to 'spurious-regression concern raised; cointegration contested' since the same author later found cointegration held under some specs. Add the non-ergodicity / ~1.5-cycle sample caveat to the mean-reversion-speed con, and add Cong-Li-Wang (RFS 2021) as a representative structural source. Appreciation 10-13% nominal is defensible but is at the upper edge of a strict decay extrapolation; widen the lower error bar.

approaches.name: Adoption S-Curve / Logistic Demand Growth
approaches.description: This approach models Bitcoin not as a discounted-cashflow asset (it has none) but as a network good whose value is a function of adoption. Demand is assumed to diffuse along a logistic S-curve borrowed from prior technology-diffusion analogs (internet, mobile phones, automobiles, social media), and network size is mapped to value via a Metcalfe-type link (value scales roughly with users^~1.5-2) and/or a fixed total-addressable-market the asset is converging on (a share of monetary gold's ~$15-22T cap, or a fraction of global savings/M2). A 10-15yr CMA falls out mechanically: you posit a terminal adoption level and date (e.g. Blockware's 10% of population by 2030 off a 60% net-entity CAGR; Timmer's ~25% of monetary gold), draw the logistic path to it, convert end-state network size or TAM share into a terminal price, and annualize from spot. Crucially the same logic that produces large near-term multiples also forces appreciation to DECELERATE as you climb the curve toward the inflection and saturation, so the forward 10-15yr CAGR is far below realized history.
key_drivers: Terminal addressable market (TAM): share of monetary gold (~$6T at 25% per Timmer), or share of global M2 / savings / sovereign reserves
Adoption ceiling and timing: terminal user/entity penetration (e.g. 10% of population by 2030) and the date of the logistic inflection point
Net-entity / user growth rate (Blockware: ~60% trailing-10yr CAGR of cumulative net entity growth), which is itself decaying
Metcalfe exponent linking users to value (theoretical 2; empirically estimated ~1.5-1.69, and contested)
Diffusion analog chosen (internet/mobile = gentler slope; social media/smartphones = steeper) — the analog choice dominates the answer
Real interest rates and monetary inflation as a demand multiplier on the adoption curve (Timmer overlays -2% to +2.5% real-rate regimes)
Supply scarcity / issuance decay (halvings) and ETF-driven float reduction as a demand-side amplifier (Standard Chartered, Grayscale)
Per-coin price derived from terminal market cap / circulating (effectively fixed ~21M) supply
pros: Honest about the asset's nature: it values a no-cashflow network on adoption + monetary demand rather than forcing a DCF that cannot exist
Mechanically transparent and decomposable — terminal TAM, adoption ceiling, timing, and Metcalfe exponent are each separately debatable and stress-testable

Naturally produces appreciation DECAY: as penetration rises toward the inflection/saturation, marginal new adoption falls and CAGR compresses, which matches realized history (142%->65%->17%) and is the correct shape for a 10-15yr forward CMA
TAM-share framing (e.g. fraction of monetary gold or global savings) gives a defensible, bounded ceiling rather than open-ended extrapolation
Used by serious institutions (Fidelity/Timmer, Grayscale, Standard Chartered) with explicit macro overlays (real rates, money supply), not just price extrapolation
Internally consistent with a 'digital gold' thesis: ties terminal value to a recognizable store-of-value benchmark
cons: The Metcalfe link to value is largely REJECTED by peer-reviewed work: regressions of price on users are spurious (both series non-stationary/trending; significance vanishes under time fixed-effects; IV studies find the transaction-count effect insignificant or negative across PoW coins) — naive Metcalfe valuation launders autocorrelation as causation

The companion S2F supply model is similarly discredited: halvings act as structural breaks, the fit collapses out-of-sample (Plan-B paths missed badly post-2021), and the apparent fit largely reflects correlation with log-time-since-genesis (~80% Pearson)

Answer is dominated by unfalsifiable analog choice and terminal-date assumptions — choosing 'social media' vs 'landline' adoption slopes swings the price target by an order of magnitude with no objective tie-breaker
Survivorship/selection bias in analogs: only technologies that DID saturate are used; the curve assumes success rather than testing it
No native volatility or correlation output — the framework is a point/path price target, so vol and all cross-asset correlations must be imported from realized data or judgment
Practitioner targets are promotional and serially revised (Standard Chartered cut 2026 target $300K->$150K->$100K within months), so 'cited' numbers are unstable and not CMA-grade

Confuses a long-run equilibrium ceiling with a forward expected return: even if the $1M+ TAM is right, the probability-weighted and time-discounted CMA is much lower, and the models rarely present a true expectation (Timmer himself calls them 'not predictions')
Adoption can stall or reverse (regulation, a superior protocol, loss of the store-of-value narrative); logistic curves have no mechanism for de-adoption

synthesized_outputs.corr_tips: ~0.25-0.35. Slightly higher than nominal FI given the store-of-value/inflation-hedge narrative and explicit real-rate channel; realized 0.15->0.25->0.30.
synthesized_outputs.corr_gold: ~0.0-0.10. Realized is ~0 (-0.01 -> +0.045). The adoption thesis's own 'share-of-monetary-gold' logic ASSERTS the correlation should rise toward gold, but that is precisely the unsupported claim: for BTC to take gold's store-of-value share the two must co-move, yet realized co-movement is ~0 and not trending up. I hold the central estimate at the bottom of the 0.0-0.15 band and treat the 'rising toward gold' story as narrative, not data.

approaches.rich_notes:
METHODOLOGY. The family has three interlocking pieces, often blended: (1) a logistic/S-curve DEMAND path borrowed from technology-diffusion analogs; (2) a Metcalfe-type USERS->VALUE map (value ~ n^a, theoretical a=2); (3) a terminal TAM the asset converges on (share of monetary gold, M2, global savings, or sovereign reserves). A CMA is produced by fixing a terminal adoption level + date, drawing the logistic to it, mapping end-state to price, and annualizing.

TIMMER (Fidelity). 'Bitcoin as exponential gold.' Demand side: settled on internet + mobile-phone adoption as the relevant S-curves; 'the slope of the adoption curve determines the size of the network, which per Metcalfe's Law determines the value... even the slightest change in slope can have a profound impact on valuation.' Overlays a regression of monetary-policy regimes (-2% to +2.5% real rates) and money-supply growth. Supply side: a modified Plan-B S2F ('exponential gold'). Headline anchors: BTC could capture ~25% of the ~$6T 'monetary gold' market (=> ~$1.5T+ cap), and one demand path values a coin at ~$1.2M by 2030 (~1,970% upside). He REPEATEDLY disclaims these as 'not predictions... merely attempts at visualizing the use case.' That disclaimer is the tell: this is a scenario ceiling, not an expectation, and must not be read as a CMA. His 2026 tactical view ('year off,' support $65-75K) underlines that he himself does not treat the curve as a near-term return forecast.

BLOCKWARE. Pure diffusion-of-innovations (Rogers) framing. Uses cumulative net-entity growth with a ~60% trailing-10yr CAGR to project 10% of global population adopting by 2030; current ~0.36% places BTC still in the 'innovators' band. Compares to autos/electricity/smartphones/internet/social media ('newer network technologies adopted faster than expected'). Explicitly 'conceptual... not investment advice.' No per-coin CMA; the value-mapping step is left implicit.

STANDARD CHARTERED / KENDRICK. Adoption expressed through ETF inflows + supply scarcity + portfolio-optimization underweight. Path $150K(26)/$225K(27)/$300K(28)/$400K(29)/$500K(30). Notably the 2026 target was cut $300K->$150K->$100K within ~3 months as corporate-treasury and ETF-flow pillars weakened — vivid evidence that practitioner adoption targets are unstable and promotional, NOT CMA-grade inputs.

GRAYSCALE. '2026: Dawn of the Institutional Era.' Two drivers: macro demand for alt store-of-value (high public debt / fiat risk) + regulatory clarity (spot ETPs, GENIUS Act, market-structure legislation). Argues the four-year halving cycle is breaking down into steadier institutional inflows. Qualitative adoption thesis; no explicit long-horizon CMA number.

ACADEMIC VERDICT (must not be laundered). The Metcalfe valuation link is largely REJECTED in peer-reviewed work: Civitarese (2018) finds price and wallet-connections do NOT cointegrate; high R^2 in users-on-price regressions is spurious because both series are non-stationary/trending (classic spurious regression + autocorrelation); IV/causal studies on block-level data across PoW coins find the transaction-count effect insignificant or negative. Wheatley/Sornette (Royal Society Open Sci 2019) calibrate the exponent at ~1.69 (not 2) and find Metcalfe support is regime/bubble-dependent. The companion S2F model fares worse: halvings act as STRUCTURAL BREAKS not smooth scarcity, fit collapses out-of-sample (Plan-B's $100K+/$288K paths missed badly post-2021), and ~80% of the apparent S2F fit is correlation with log-time-since-genesis (MDPI JRFM 2024; multiple ECM critiques). So: the DEMAND-curve narrative may have economic content (a network/store-of-value good plausibly diffuses), but the QUANTITATIVE value-mapping (Metcalfe, S2F) that turns it into a price target is statistically unsound. Treat the targets as scenario ceilings, not estimates.

HOW I SYNTHESIZED. The brief's instruction is decisive: a 10-15yr forward CMA must extrapolate BTC's appreciation DECAY (full-window 142% -> 10yr 65% -> 5yr 17% nominal), not its historical level. The S-curve framework AGREES with this shape — appreciation is highest on the lower limb and decelerates through the inflection toward saturation. By 2026, with ~$1.3-2T cap and growing institutional ownership, BTC is plausibly entering the inflection region. Anchoring to a bounded TAM (~25% of ~$20T monetary gold = ~$5T, ~3x current) over 12-15yr gives ~8-12%/yr; allowing the adoption tail to keep rising and TAM to grow pushes my central nominal estimate to ~12-15%/yr (real ~9-12%), with an explicitly wide cone (bear ~3-5% nominal if adoption stalls; bull ~20-25% if BTC captures a gold-scale monetary role early). This is a JUDGMENT consistent with the approach's own logic, deliberately far below the promotional $500K-$1.2M paths because those are undiscounted, unprobability-weighted ceilings on sub-decade horizons. Vol ~50% extrapolates the 103->69->57% decay. Correlations: I let realized trends continue (rising vs equities as BTC institutionalizes) with ONE thesis-driven adjustment — gold correlation, realized ~0, should RISE toward ~0.15 (up to ~0.3) because the adoption thesis is explicitly a 'digital gold' / share-of-monetary-gold story, so the marginal buyer increasingly overlaps gold's store-of-value/macro-hedge allocator. All five correlations are judgments under this approach's logic, not computed statistics.

CAVEAT FOR THE CMA TABLE. This row's 'cited_outputs' are deliberately mostly 'n/a' for vol and correlations because the family produces price PATHS, not a covariance structure — any vol/correlation attached to it in practice is imported, not native. Do not represent the practitioner price targets as expected returns.

issues: GOLD-TAM ARITHMETIC IS INTERNALLY INCONSISTENT (the most serious quantitative flaw). The synthesis math uses '~25% of ~$20T monetary gold = ~$5T cap, ~3-4x current.' But Timmer's OWN cited figure (correctly stated elsewhere in the same row) is 25% of ~$6T = ~$1.5T -- which roughly EQUALS today's BTC cap (~$1.3-1.5T), implying ~0x upside, not 3-4x. The row silently swaps Timmer's $6T monetary-gold base for a $20T base to manufacture the 3-4x multiple. Verified May-2026 data: total above-ground gold ~$31-32T at ~$4,570/oz; the 'monetary' subset is ~$14-16T, so a $15-22T figure is defensible ON ITS OWN, but it is NOT Timmer's number and the row should not attribute the resulting multiple to his framework. The two anchors disagree ~3x and the synthesis picks the bullish one without flagging it.

PETERSON 2018 VENUE MIS-TAGGED. The row labels it 'Peterson... (Ledger / SSRN).' The paper was published in the CAIA 'Alternative Investment Analyst Review' (Vol 7, pp 9-18), not Ledger. (Peterson has a SEPARATE 2019 paper in the journal Ledger -- the row appears to conflate the two.) Citation is real and correctly attributed to Peterson/SSRN abstract 3078248, but the journal tag is wrong.

CIVITARESE CHARACTERIZATION IS ONE-SIDED. The row/notes say Civitarese 'rejects Metcalfe' (no cointegration -- TRUE). But the same paper explicitly states Metcalfe's Law 'consistently predicts the trend in the value of Bitcoin' and that reverse causation (returns -> new wallets) cannot be ruled out. Citing it purely as a rejection launders a mixed result into a clean negative.

MDPI 2024 SLIGHTLY OVERSTATED AS NEGATIVE. Accurate that S2F/Metcalfe explain in-sample but fail out-of-sample. Omits that the paper's headline positive result is a SUCCESSFUL out-of-sample blended market-timing strategy. Fair for the valuation claim, but the 'S2F/Metcalfe fail out-of-sample' framing cherry-picks the negative half.
WHEATLEY/SORNETTE EXPONENT: row says 1.69, published best estimate is ~1.7 (1.69 in the SSRN/arXiv version). Trivially correct -- no issue, noted only for completeness.

MISSING ACADEMIC CRITIQUE: GENERALIZED-METCALFE / SARDINING. The cons cover spurious-regression and S2F well, but omit the strongest structural critique of network-value models -- that 'active addresses/entities' is gameable and non-monotonic with real users (one entity = many addresses and vice versa via custodial ETF/exchange consolidation). Post-ETF, coins move OFF-chain into custodians, so on-chain entity counts UNDERCOUNT adoption exactly when institutional adoption accelerates -- breaking the users->value map in the very regime (Grayscale/StanChart 'institutional era') the bull case relies on. This is a first-order objection the row does not raise.

GOLD-CORRELATION JUDGMENT IS THESIS-DRIVEN, NOT DATA-DRIVEN, AND CUTS AGAINST THE SCRIPTED BASELINE. Realized gold corr is ~0 (-0.01 to 0.045) per the anchor. The synthesis raises it to ~0.15 (up to 0.3) purely because the 'digital gold' narrative SAYS it should rise. That is exactly the kind of narrative-laundering the cons warn against -- importing a thesis-implied number over a measured ~0. It is labeled a judgment, which is honest, but it is the one correlation that contradicts realized data and should carry a wider/lower central than 0.15.
Round-2 correction (corr_gold/vol): Gold-corr re-centered from 0.10-0.25 to 0.0-0.10 with the substitution contradiction explicit; vol floor raised from 45% to ~57%.
verdict.corrections: ["State the TAM math from Timmer's ACTUAL base ($6T monetary gold x 25% = ~$1.5T) AND a refreshed-2026 base ($14-16T monetary subset x 20-25% = ~$3-4T), and show they bracket roughly 0x to ~2.5x current cap -- NOT a clean 3-4x. Annualized over 13.5yr: from ~$1.4T to ~$3.5T is ~6-7%/yr, to ~$5T is ~9-10%/yr. The honest nominal central should sit ~7-11%/yr (not 12-15%), with the 12-15% reserved for an explicit bull/TAM-growth scenario, because the pure bounded-gold-share anchor on Timmer's own numbers gives mid-single-digits to ~10%.", "Re-tag Peterson 2018 to 'Alternative Investment Analyst Review (CAIA)', not Ledger.", "Soften the Civitarese gloss to 'no cointegration (rejects a stable long-run Metcalfe equilibrium), though it finds Metcalfe tracks the trend and cannot rule out reverse causation.'", "Add the ETF/custodial address-consolidation critique to the cons: on-chain entity counts undercount adoption precisely in the institutional regime, breaking the users->value mapping the bull case needs.", "Lower the gold-correlation central from ~0.15 toward ~0.05-0.10 (realized is ~0), keeping the upside cone but anchoring the center on data, not narrative.", "Note the MDPI paper found a successful BLENDED out-of-sample timing strategy, so frame it as 'individual S2F/Metcalfe predictors fail out-of-sample' rather than a blanket failure."]

approaches.name: Portfolio Sizing / Risk-Budget Allocation
approaches.description: This approach does NOT produce a standalone expected-return CMA for Bitcoin. Instead it treats BTC as a small "satellite" sleeve and sizes it by its marginal contribution to total portfolio risk (volatility × correlation × weight), not by a return forecast. The canonical output is an allocation band (BlackRock: 1-2%; CoinShares: ~3.6% per +100bps of added risk budget; Grayscale: a conservative single-digit satellite) chosen so BTC's share of portfolio risk stays comparable to a known reference exposure (e.g. a single Magnificent-7 stock contributing ~4% of risk in a 60/40). A 10-15yr CMA falls out only implicitly: the sizing exercise assumes BTC's long-run volatility declines as it matures and that its correlation to equities/bonds is low-and-unstable, but it is explicitly return-agnostic — the allocation is "right-sized" so that even a total loss is a survivable 1-2% drag, while the upside is left as an unmodeled convex option. Expected return is an INPUT the practitioner must supply elsewhere; this family's contribution is the risk-budget envelope, not the alpha.
key_drivers: BTC standalone annualized volatility (and its assumed decay path as the asset matures) — the dominant input
BTC's correlation to the existing 60/40 (low but rising and unstable, especially post-2021/post-ETF)
The allocation weight itself, solved so BTC's marginal risk contribution hits a target (e.g. 2-5% of total portfolio risk)
A reference risk anchor — BlackRock benchmarks to a single Magnificent-7 stock (~4% of portfolio risk)
Investor's chosen incremental risk budget (CoinShares: +100bps annualized risk => ~3.6% weight)
Rebalancing rule (CoinShares: quarterly, funded equally from stocks and bonds)
Survivability / max-drawdown tolerance — the allocation is sized so a -100% BTC outcome is bearable
Expected return is deliberately NOT a driver — the method is return-agnostic by construction
pros: Honest about what is knowable: BTC's risk (vol, correlation) is far more estimable than its 10-15yr return, so sizing on risk rather than a fabricated return forecast is methodologically cleaner than S2F/Metcalfe/DCF-style models
Naturally caps tail damage — a 1-2% sleeve makes even a total loss a survivable drag, which suits an asset with genuine ruin risk
Empirically grounded and reproducible: risk contributions are computed from a covariance matrix on real return data, satisfying the scripted-analysis discipline
Asset-manager versions (BlackRock, CoinShares, Grayscale) are institutionally vetted and widely adopted as the de facto framing for advisor allocations
Framework-agnostic to the bull/bear return debate — usable by skeptics and believers alike since it doesn't require endorsing a price target
Directly answers the practical question an allocator actually asks ('how much?') rather than the unanswerable one ('what's fair value?')
cons: It is NOT a return model — it cannot, by itself, produce the expected-appreciation figure a CMA requires; you must bolt on a return assumption from another family, so as a standalone CMA approach it is incomplete

Garbage-in on volatility and correlation: estimates are dominated by a short, regime-unstable sample (BTC ETPs only since ~2015), and the assumed vol-decay path is an unverifiable assumption that drives the whole answer

Correlation is the load-bearing input and it is non-stationary: BTC-S&P rolling correlation jumped from ~0 to ~0.5-0.7 post-2021/post-ETF, eroding the diversification premise the sizing relies on — the 'low correlation' that justifies a 2% slot may not persist

Risk-budgeting tacitly assumes a positive (or at least non-negative) Sharpe; if BTC's forward return is poor, an 'optimally risk-sized' allocation still loses money — right-sizing the risk does not make the bet good

Mean-variance / risk-parity optimizers are notoriously sensitive to input error and routinely corner-solution into BTC when fed high historical returns, so backtested 'optimal' weights overstate the case (in-sample overfitting)
Asset-manager sources have a conflict of interest (BlackRock IBIT, Grayscale, CoinShares all sell BTC products) — the 1-2% 'reasonable' framing is marketing-adjacent, not peer-reviewed
Says little about gold specifically: treats BTC's near-zero gold correlation as a feature without resolving whether BTC competes with or complements a gold sleeve in the same risk budget
