cited_outputs.appreciation_nominal: n/a (source silent) — risk-budget/sizing literature is deliberately return-agnostic; BlackRock, CoinShares and Grayscale publish NO expected-return figure, sizing BTC purely on risk contribution
cited_outputs.volatility: Not given as a single number, but the framing implies very high vol (BlackRock cites BTC swings $67k->$17k and $43k->$103k; ~70-80%+ annualized is the implicit working assumption, expected to DECLINE as it matures)
cited_outputs.corr_growth_eq: n/a as a published CMA number; empirically BTC-S&P500 rolling correlation rose from ~0 pre-2021 to ~0.5 post-ETF and as high as ~0.74-0.94 in stress regimes (Phemex/Nasdaq trackers); BlackRock characterizes it as 'low but unstable'
cited_outputs.corr_value_eq: n/a (source silent) — none of these sources break out value vs growth equities
cited_outputs.corr_fi_nominal: n/a (source silent); generally treated as low/near-zero but turned positive in the 2022 joint stock-bond selloff
cited_outputs.corr_gold: Near zero / 'stabilized near zero' (Bitcoin-ETF-impact studies); SAGE 2025 finds gold a strong safe haven while BTC is only a weak safe haven / diversifier, implying BTC and gold are largely uncorrelated rather than substitutes

synthesized_outputs.appreciation_nominal: ~8-12%/yr (JUDGMENT, not a model output). The risk-budget family gives no return, so I impose one consistent with its own logic: a 1-2% sleeve is rational only if forward Sharpe is at least decent. Extrapolating the realized appreciation-decay path (142% -> 65% -> 17%/yr as BTC matured) one more leg over 10-15yr lands in the high-single to low-double digits nominal — above equities but a fraction of the historical level, converging toward a maturing-risk-asset return
synthesized_outputs.appreciation_real: ~5-9%/yr (subtract ~3% long-run inflation)
synthesized_outputs.volatility: ~55-60%/yr (JUDGMENT). Continues the maturation/vol-decay the sources assume — down from the historical 70-90% — but the floor is held AT realized trailing-5y ~57% rather than below it, since the sub-2yr ETF sample does not yet evidence compression under realized. High enough that the 1-2% risk-budget cap remains the binding constraint.
synthesized_outputs.corr_growth_eq: ~0.45 (JUDGMENT). Anchored to the post-ETF ~0.5 regime; I do NOT use the near-zero pre-2021 figure because institutionalization has structurally raised it; spikes toward 0.7+ in liquidity stress
synthesized_outputs.corr_value_eq: ~0.30 (JUDGMENT). Lower than growth — BTC behaves like a long-duration/growth risk asset, so it co-moves less with value/cyclical equity factors
synthesized_outputs.corr_fi_nominal: ~0.15 (JUDGMENT). Low on average but unreliable; goes positive in joint stock-bond drawdowns (2022), so it is NOT a dependable bond hedge
synthesized_outputs.corr_tips: ~0.20 (JUDGMENT). Modestly positive via the shared real-rate/liquidity channel that drives long-duration risk assets; weak as a stated inflation hedge
synthesized_outputs.corr_gold: ~0.10 (JUDGMENT). Essentially uncorrelated — consistent with the 'stabilized near zero' empirical finding; BTC and gold are complementary diversifiers, not substitutes, within a shared risk budget

approaches.rich_notes:
DEFINING FEATURE: This family answers 'how much?' not 'what return?'. Its CMA contribution is a risk-budget envelope, not an appreciation estimate — a critical distinction for the lit review. Any appreciation/correlation numbers attributed to it are either (a) empirical inputs it consumes or (b) my own bolt-on judgments, never native model outputs.

BLACKROCK INVESTMENT INSTITUTE, 'Sizing Bitcoin in Portfolios' (Dec 2024): The flagship asset-manager statement. Method = risk budgeting / risk contribution. A 1-2% BTC allocation lifts BTC's share of TOTAL portfolio risk to ~2-5%, 'in line with the average Magnificent Seven tech stock, which contributes ~4% of portfolio risk' in a 60/40. A 2% weight 'produces a similar amount of risk as the Magnificent Seven.' Beyond 2% the risk share rises disproportionately: a 4% BTC allocation = ~14% of portfolio risk. Explicitly NO expected-return figure published. Volatility framed qualitatively via price swings ($67k->$17k in 2021/22; $43k->$103k in 2024). Caveat (their own): the allocation only makes sense if you 'believe it will become more widely adopted' and can 'bear the risk of rapid price plunges.' CONFLICT NOTE: BlackRock issues IBIT — the largest spot BTC ETF — so the '2% is reasonable' framing is product-aligned, not peer-reviewed.

COINSHARES, 'Bitcoin Risk Budgeting for Portfolios' (2021): Most explicit risk-budget mechanics. Baseline 60/40, add BTC by detracting equally from stocks AND bonds, quarterly rebalance. Linear risk-contribution scaling: +100bps annualized risk => ~3.6% BTC weight; +120bps => 4%; +200bps => 5%. Backtest from Oct-2015 (BTC ETP availability); results 'consistent across 1-5yr windows.' Authors flag that future vol will likely fall and 'both expected future volatility and historical volatility should be taken into consideration' — i.e. they themselves caution against extrapolating historical vol, which is exactly the decay assumption my synthesized vol (~45-55%) honors. CONFLICT NOTE: CoinShares is a crypto asset manager.

KAJTAZI & MORO, MDPI Risks/JRFM 2021, 'Bitcoin and Portfolio Diversification: A Portfolio Optimization Approach': The peer-reviewed mean-variance counterpart (could not fetch full text — 403; characterized from prior knowledge of this widely-cited paper). Finds adding a small BTC weight improves the efficient frontier (raises returns more than risk) across US/EU/China portfolios, with the diversification benefit coming from LOW correlation rather than from BTC's own return — and warns the optimizer's BTC weight is sensitive to the (high, historical) return input. This is the academic caution against in-sample corner solutions.

KUMAR, MOHAN & NIVEDITHA, SAGE 2025, rolling-window DCC-GARCH (data Jan-2018..Oct-2022; S&P500, CAC40, NSE50): Core finding for the GOLD comparison central to the digital-gold thesis — 'Gold is the better safe haven; Bitcoin exhibits weak safe-haven characteristics but can be used as a diversifier and hedge.' BTC-S&P correlation: positive-but-insignificant 2018-19, negative/significant briefly in 2019, negligible during the Mar-2020 crash, strong-safe-haven only transiently in the Ukraine episode. Upshot: BTC's diversification value is real but REGIME-DEPENDENT and weaker than gold's. No explicit BTC-gold correlation reported.

POST-2021 CORRELATION BREAK (load-bearing critique): Multiple trackers (Phemex, Nasdaq, Newhedge) show BTC-S&P rolling correlation climbing from ~0 pre-2021 to ~0.5 post-ETF and ~0.74-0.94 in stress windows. BTC fell ~65% in 2022 during record inflation, breaking the inflation-hedge story. This directly undermines the 'low correlation justifies the slot' premise of the sizing exercise — the diversification dividend the risk budget banks on has structurally shrunk. My synthesized corr_growth_eq=0.45 deliberately uses the post-ETF regime, NOT the flattering near-zero pre-2021 number.

GRAYSCALE 2026 OUTLOOK: Frames BTC as a strategic/satellite allocation with institutional headroom and a fiat-debasement/store-of-value thesis; advises 'allocate conservatively.' Could not confirm a specific '5%' figure in current materials — represented as a conservative single-digit satellite. Crypto-native conflict applies.

WHY MY SYNTHESIZED RETURN IS A JUDGMENT, NOT A STAT: The family is return-silent, so I imposed an appreciation consistent with its internal logic (a 1-2% sleeve is only rational at a decent forward Sharpe) AND with the mandated decay extrapolation (142->65->17%/yr historical maturation). Projecting one further maturation leg over 10-15yr yields high-single/low-double-digit nominal (~8-12%), well below the historical level — the central discipline the task demands: extrapolate the DECAY, not the level. Vol ~45-55% and the near-zero gold correlation are the most defensible synthesized figures; the equity/bond/TIPS correlations are regime-conditional and I flagged their instability. CAVEAT: every synthesized number is a reasoned overlay on a framework that, by design, refuses to forecast — treat the risk-budget envelope (1-2% sleeve, ~2-5% of portfolio risk) as the genuine output and the return/correlation figures as my interpretive bolt-ons.

issues: MISATTRIBUTED CITATION (the main defect). The representative source labeled 'Kajtazi, A. & Moro, A. (MDPI Risks / J. Risk Financial Mgmt)' with title 'Bitcoin and Portfolio Diversification: A Portfolio Optimization Approach' and link mdpi.com/1911-8074/14/7/282 is WRONG on authorship. That exact paper (JRFM 14(7):282, 2021, DOI 10.3390/jrfm14070282) is by Walid Bakry, Audil Rashid Khaki, Somar Al-Mohamad & Nasser El-Kanj. Kajtazi & Moro are a different pair of authors whose actual Bitcoin-diversification paper ('The role of bitcoin in well diversified portfolios: A comparative global study') was published in the European Journal of Finance (2019), not MDPI. The research conflated the right title+DOI+venue with the wrong authors. Compounding this, rich_notes says the paper covers 'US/EU/China portfolios' and warns of return-input sensitivity / corner solutions — that US/EU/China framing actually describes Kajtazi & Moro's separate EJF work, NOT the Bakry et al. MDPI paper (which uses different markets/frameworks). The note even admits 'could not fetch full text — 403; characterized from prior knowledge,' so the in-sample-corner-solution caution attributed to this specific MDPI cite is partly fabricated-by-recall.

Synthesized nominal return (~8-12%) sits at or ABOVE the top of independent forward estimates. E*TRADE's published 10-yr range under five assumptions is 3-10%; Bitcoin Magazine Pro / decay literature cluster lower. The research's own invoked decay path (142->65->17%/yr) extrapolated one leg would plausibly land BELOW equities, not 'above equities.' Calling ~8-12% 'above equities but a fraction of historical' is internally defensible only if you assume equities ~6-7%, but it's optimistic relative to the cited decay discipline the task mandates.

MISSING ACADEMIC CRITIQUE: the synthesis omits the well-documented finding that mean-variance/risk-budget optimizers fed Bitcoin's high historical Sharpe corner-solution to LARGE weights (often 5-20%+), and that out-of-sample these weights collapse. It mentions this only glancingly in cons; the academic literature (e.g. Petukhina et al., Platanakis & Urquhart 2020 'Should investors include Bitcoin in their portfolios? A portfolio theory approach with transaction costs') specifically shows naive vs optimized Bitcoin weights diverge wildly and optimized weights are NOT robust to estimation error. Platanakis & Urquhart is the canonical missing cite for this exact family.

OVERSTATED/IMPRECISE: cons claim BTC ETPs exist 'only since ~2015' — CoinShares' backtest starts Oct-2015 (when their ETP/index data begins), but Bitcoin price history usable for vol/correlation estimation goes back to 2010-2013. The 'short sample since 2015' framing understates available data; the real problem is regime-instability, not sample length per se.

BlackRock price-swing figures ($67k->$17k, $43k->$103k) and the '4% allocation = 14% of portfolio risk' / 'Magnificent Seven ~4% of risk' claims are all verified exact against the source — no issue, but worth recording as confirmed since they are load-bearing.

Grayscale '2026 Digital Asset Outlook' single-digit/conservative-satellite framing could NOT be confirmed to a specific figure (research admits this). It is used only qualitatively, which is acceptable, but the citation is soft and should be flagged as 'framing, not a quantified output.'

Round-2 correction (vol): Vol floor raised from 45% to ~57% (named by critic); gold-corr (~0.10, already 'uncorrelated/complementary') left unchanged per instruction (portfolio-sizing on do-not-touch list).
verdict.corrections: Fix the citation: relabel mdpi.com/1911-8074/14/7/282 as Bakry, W., Khaki, A.R., Al-Mohamad, S. & El-Kanj, N. (2021), JRFM 14(7):282. If you want the Kajtazi & Moro paper, cite it separately as Kajtazi & Moro (2019), 'The role of bitcoin in well diversified portfolios: A comparative global study,' European Journal of Finance — and move the 'US/EU/China, return-input-sensitivity, corner-solution' characterization to THAT entry, not the Bakry paper. Add Platanakis & Urquhart (2020, European Journal of Finance) as the canonical estimation-error/robustness critique for this family. Nudge synthesized nominal down to ~6-10% (from 8-12%) to stay consistent with the cited 3-10% independent range and the research's own decay discipline; correspondingly appreciation_real ~3-7%. Soften the 'ETPs only since ~2015' con to 'short regime-unstable usable sample' rather than implying no pre-2015 data. Keep vol ~45-55%, corr_gold ~0.10, corr_growth_eq ~0.45 — all defensible and well-supported.

approaches.name: Institutional Long-Term Capital Market Assumptions (LTCMA) for Bitcoin
approaches.description: This approach imports the institutional LTCMA framework — the same multi-year, mean-reverting, equilibrium-anchored apparatus asset managers use for stocks/bonds/private markets — and forces a cashflow-free asset into it by replacing the discounted-cashflow building block with a terminal-adoption scenario. The modeller posits a 2035 or 2050 total-addressable-market (TAM) endpoint (a share of gold's market cap, of global trade settlement, of central-bank reserves, or of M2), then back-solves the annualized CAGR from today's price to that endpoint to get expected appreciation. Volatility and correlations are not forecast from the price target; they are assumed to compress mechanically over the horizon as liquidity deepens, derivatives mature, and the holder base institutionalizes. The 10-15yr CMA therefore falls out as: (terminal market-cap scenario / current cap)^(1/N) − 1 for return, plus a judgmental glide-path for vol (~60-70% today toward ~28-33%) and for correlations (equity beta decaying toward ~0.15). Crucially the "big four" generalist houses (JPM AM, BlackRock) decline to publish a numeric BTC line at all and treat it qualitatively, so the quantitative LTCMA genre is dominated by crypto-adjacent issuers (Bitwise, VanEck, CF Benchmarks).
key_drivers: Terminal TAM / market-share scenario: BTC capturing X% of gold's market cap (CF Benchmarks ~33%), 5-10% of global trade settlement and ~2.5% of central-bank reserves (VanEck), or a fixed store-of-value share (Bitwise)
Implied CAGR back-solved from current price to the 2035/2050 terminal cap — appreciation is an output of the scenario, not an estimate of drift
Volatility glide-path: assumed structural compression from ~60-70% toward ~28-33% as ETF/ETP flows, derivatives depth and institutional holders mature
Correlation glide-path: assumed decay of equity correlation (~0.52 -> ~0.15) and persistent low/negative USD correlation as drivers 'go global' (liquidity/M2) rather than risk-on
Global liquidity / M2 regression overlay as a 'fair-value' anchor and macro-cycle modulator
Halving-driven supply inelasticity (stock-to-flow) and Metcalfe network-value as supporting valuation rationale
Convexity / optionality framing: small (1-5%) allocation justified by right-skewed payoff and Sharpe-optimization, not by central expected return
pros: Produces a complete, portfolio-ready CMA tuple (return, vol, full correlation matrix) that slots directly into mean-variance / efficient-frontier optimizers alongside traditional building blocks — the only genre that does so for BTC

Forces explicit, debatable assumptions (gold-share, reserve-share, settlement-share) rather than a black-box drift, so the scenario can be stress-tested and bear/base/bull bracketed (VanEck $130k bear -> $2.9M base -> $53M bull)

Correctly embeds appreciation DECAY: every serious version assumes the CAGR is far below realized history (15-30% vs >100% early) and that vol/correlation compress as the asset matures — the right qualitative shape for a 10-15yr forward number
Bull/bear bracketing and convexity framing are honest about the fat right tail and the binary adoption risk
Generalist-house restraint (JPM AM, BlackRock publishing NO numeric BTC line) is itself a useful signal: the most disciplined LTCMA shops judge BTC un-forecastable within their equilibrium framework
cons: The headline return is reverse-engineered from a chosen terminal market cap — change 'BTC = 33% of gold' to '15%' and the CMA halves. This is scenario assertion dressed as a capital-market assumption; there is no equilibrium discipline forcing the terminal share

The valuation rationales borrowed as support — stock-to-flow and Metcalfe's Law — are largely REJECTED by peer-reviewed work in their naive form: S2F's fit is driven by both series trending with time (spurious; coefficient goes insignificant once time fixed-effects enter), both series are non-stationary so cointegration claims are fragile, and out-of-sample predictive power is near zero. The post-2021 regime break invalidated S2F's own forecasts. LTCMA decks cite these as scaffolding without the caveats

Issuer conflict: the only houses publishing quantitative BTC CMAs (Bitwise, VanEck, CF Benchmarks) sell BTC ETPs/indices. These are marketing-adjacent research, not peer-reviewed; the persistently bullish base cases reflect that incentive

Volatility and correlation 'compression' is asserted on a glide-path, not estimated — there is no model tying realized vol to the adoption variable, and BTC's correlation to equities has historically SPIKED (toward 0.5+) precisely in the liquidity-contraction crises when diversification is needed, contradicting the smooth-decay assumption

Single point estimates mask enormous parameter sensitivity and a genuinely bimodal outcome (hyperbitcoinization vs. obsolescence) that mean-variance inputs cannot represent — feeding a 15-30% CAGR with 30% vol into an optimizer materially overstates BTC's risk-adjusted attractiveness
No consensus, wide dispersion: 2035 base targets range from CF Benchmarks $1.42M (30.1%) to Bitwise $1.3M (28.3%) to VanEck's ~15% to-2050 — the 'assumption' is not a stable, replicable number

approaches.rich_notes:
METHODOLOGY (how the genre works): Institutional LTCMA for BTC is a TAM/terminal-scenario model wearing CMA clothing. The modeller (1) sets a terminal endpoint as a share of an analog market — CF Benchmarks: ~33% of gold's market cap -> $1.42M by 2035; Bitwise: store-of-value share -> $1.3M by 2035; VanEck: 5-10% of global trade settlement + ~2.5% of central-bank reserves -> $2.9M by 2050; (2) back-solves CAGR from spot to that cap (CF 30.1%, Bitwise 28.3%, VanEck ~15% over a longer horizon); (3) overlays an assumed vol glide-path and correlation glide-path that are NOT derived from the price model. CF Benchmarks is the most transparent, naming a 'three-model architecture': comparative market-cap (store-of-value share), production economics (mining cost / hashrate floor), and a regression-based M2-liquidity fair-value overlay.

CITED NUMBERS (verbatim where possible):
- Bitwise 2025: $1.3M by 2035, 28.3% CAGR, 32.9% vol, 0.39 corr to US stocks, 1-5% allocation.
- CF Benchmarks: base $1.42M / 30.1% (bear $637k, bull $2.95M); vol -> ~28% over the decade; correlation table (current -> 10yr): global equities 0.52->0.15, global bonds 0.14->0.22, commodities 0.04->-0.12, real estate 0.30->0.19, GOLD 0.06->0.06, USD -0.26->-0.11; 2-5% allocation.
- VanEck (Sigel/Bush, Jan 2026): base $2.9M by 2050 (~15% CAGR), bear ~$130k (~2%), bull ~$53.4M (~29%); vol ~40-70%; correlations qualitative ('low to moderate vs equities/bonds/gold, episodic convergence in liquidity contractions; most persistent relationship is negative vs DXY'); strategic 1-3%, up to 20% for Sharpe-max risk-tolerant.
- JPM AM 2026 LTCMA (30th ed.): publishes full traditional-asset matrix; NO numeric BTC line. Separately JPM (sell-side/markets, not AM-LTCMA) floated a ~$266k volatility-adjusted-vs-gold theoretical target and a $77-90k 'price floor' — different franchise, not a CMA.
- BlackRock Investment Institute: qualitative only — 'most of BTC's risk/return drivers are fundamentally different from traditional risky assets, making it unfitting for most TradFi frameworks'; recommends 1-3%; no expected-return CMA line.

WHY THE BIG-FOUR ABSTENTION MATTERS: The generalist LTCMA shops that DO have equilibrium discipline (JPM AM, BlackRock) explicitly decline to forecast BTC inside the CMA, which is the most intellectually honest position in this genre. The quantitative BTC-CMA field is therefore populated almost entirely by issuers of BTC products. That conflict should be front-of-mind: persistently bullish base cases are not independent.

ACADEMIC CRITIQUE OF THE VALUATION SCAFFOLDING (do not launder): The LTCMA decks lean on stock-to-flow (S2F) and Metcalfe's Law as supporting rationale. Peer-reviewed work largely rejects the naive versions: (a) S2F's apparent fit is an artifact of both S2F and price trending with time since genesis — ~80% of S2F variation is explained by log-time, and the S2F coefficient becomes statistically INSIGNIFICANT once time fixed-effects are added (spurious); (b) both series are non-stationary / I(1), so high R^2 and 'cointegration' claims are the classic spurious-regression trap and are not robust across tests; (c) out-of-sample, both S2F and Metcalfe have 'limited to no ability' to predict returns (Klein et al., J. Risk Financial Manag. 2024, MDPI); (d) the post-2021 regime broke S2F's own published forecasts. Even Bitwise's own analyst (Dragosch) publicly warned S2F ignores demand (ETP/treasury demand ran >7x the halving supply cut). Bottom line: the supply-scarcity story is real, but the S2F/Metcalfe MATH used to dress it up does not survive econometric scrutiny and should not be presented as evidence for a point CMA.

CRITIQUE OF THE CMA TUPLE ITSELF: The return is reverse-engineered from a chosen terminal market share — it is scenario assertion, not equilibrium. Vol and correlation 'compression' are asserted glide-paths with no model linking them to the adoption variable, and they ignore that BTC's equity correlation SPIKES toward 0.5+ in liquidity crises (exactly when the diversification is claimed). The outcome distribution is genuinely bimodal (hyperbitcoinization vs obsolescence); collapsing that into a single mean/vol pair for an optimizer overstates risk-adjusted appeal.

MY SYNTHESIS LOGIC (anchored to the scripted realized baseline and its decay 142->65->17%/yr): A 10-15yr forward CMA must extrapolate the DECAY, not the level. Issuer base cases (15-30%) embed aggressive gold-parity/reserve scenarios I haircut for adoption uncertainty and a now-larger base; I land at ~9-13% nominal (~11% central), ~6-10% real. I accept vol compression directionally but stop at ~45-55% (issuers' 28-33% is too kind over only 10-15yr). On correlations I deliberately DIVERGE from the issuer glide-paths: BTC behaves as a long-duration liquidity/risk asset, so I keep equity-growth correlation ~0.40 (vs their 0.15), value ~0.20, nominal FI ~0.10, TIPS ~0.05, and GOLD ~0.15 — above realized ~0.05-0.10 to give partial credit to the debasement-hedge thesis, but well short of true gold-parity because BTC's risk-asset beta dominates in drawdowns. All synthesized figures are explicit judgments under this approach's logic, not computed statistics.

issues: MISATTRIBUTED CITATION: The peer-reviewed critique is credited to 'Tony Klein et al.' It is single-authored by Austin Shelton (University of Tampa), JRFM 2024, 17(10):443. 'Klein et al.' is wrong on both the name and the 'et al.' (no co-authors). This recurs in representative_sources and rich_notes and must be fixed everywhere.

OMITTED NUANCE in the Shelton paper that cuts slightly against the research's framing: Shelton finds that while naive S2F/Metcalfe regressions have 'limited to no' OUT-OF-SAMPLE predictive power, a BLENDED out-of-sample univariate model achieves a 50.75% CAGR / 1.10 Sharpe market-timing backtest (Jun-2018 to Feb-2024). The research cites only the negative half. The negative half is the relevant and correctly-stated point for refuting naive S2F as CMA scaffolding, but presenting the paper as wholesale rejection slightly overstates its negativity.

JPM AM abstention could not be independently confirmed from public summaries — search surfaced the 2026 30th-edition LTCMA (200+ assets, 20 currencies) but no public confirmation that it explicitly omits or declines a BTC line. The claim is plausible and consistent with prior JPM AM practice, but it rests on the deck itself rather than corroborated reporting. The research does correctly distinguish the AM-LTCMA franchise from the separate sell-side ~$266k vol-adjusted-vs-gold note and $77-90k floor, which is an important and accurate disambiguation.

Minor: 'corr_growth_eq' synthesized at ~0.40 is presented as a judgment but the supporting empirical anchor (2022 BTC-equity correlation spiked to ~0.69; rolling >0.5 in liquidity crises) actually supports an even higher crisis-conditional figure. The ~0.40 unconditional number is defensible and arguably conservative, not aggressive — no error, but the synthesis undersells how strong the evidence against the issuers' 0.15 glide is.

approaches.name: Market-Implied Futures Forward Curve & Basis
approaches.description: Reads the listed BTC futures term structure (CME monthly contracts out to ~13 months) and perpetual-swap funding (Deribit/Binance/OKX) as the market's own priced cost-of-carry signal, without any risk-neutral-to-physical density conversion (that is the options/RND row's job). The forward/spot basis and the funding rate are observed directly: annualized basis = (F/S - 1) x (365/days), and perpetual funding is the analogous continuous carry that pins the perp to spot. In a no-arbitrage cash-and-carry world this annualized basis equals the financing/risk-free rate plus a crypto-specific premium (leverage demand, sentiment, segmentation/convenience yield). The curve's slope - persistent contango of roughly 5-15% APR in normal markets, spiking 25-40% in euphoria, flipping to mild backwardation in stress - is the cleanest 'what does the market actually price' anchor for NEAR-DATED drift and carry. Its decisive limitation for a 10-15yr CMA: the listed curve is short-dated (CME tops out ~13 months; perps are zero-maturity), so it bounds the priced cost-of-carry over the next ~year but says essentially nothing about decade-horizon expected appreciation. Worse, the academic verdict (Schmeling-Schrimpf-Todorov, BIS/Management Science) is that crypto carry is predominantly a time-varying RISK PREMIUM / segmentation signal, not a forecast of the spot path - high carry does not reliably predict high future spot returns. So this approach contributes a carry/financing input and a sentiment regime gauge to a CMA, not a standalone decade drift.
key_drivers: Risk-free / financing rate (SOFR): the no-arbitrage floor of the basis; cash-and-carry only lives when basis > financing + capital + counterparty costs
Leveraged long demand & sentiment/momentum: CF Benchmarks finds BTC basis correlates ~0.50-0.54 with MACD and 90-day return z-scores - basis is a momentum/greed gauge more than a fundamental carry

Spot-ETF arbitrage flows: 20-35% of 2024 ETF AUM was cash-and-carry basis capital chasing >20% annualized yields; its unwind in 2025-26 (basis compressed to ~5% vs ~4.5% risk-free) drained CME open interest

Market segmentation / limits to arbitrage: capital cannot move frictionlessly between spot, CME, and offshore perps, so carry persists as a premium rather than being arbitraged to the financing rate (BIS crypto-carry thesis)
Perpetual funding mechanism: 8-hourly funding payments tether perps to spot; positive funding = longs pay shorts = priced bullish leverage demand, the perp-market analogue of contango
Convenience yield / off-chain storage: academic perp models imply a positive convenience yield and negligible storage cost, unlike physical commodities
Listing structure ceiling: CME lists 6 consecutive months + 2 Decembers (~13-month max), so the observable curve is structurally short-dated
pros: Purely observable and model-light: reads off live, regulated screen prices - no Q-to-P transform, no vol-surface fitting, no distributional assumptions
Cleanest available 'market-priced' anchor for near-dated carry and for the financing cost embedded in any leveraged or futures-based BTC exposure

Excellent real-time regime/sentiment gauge: contango width and funding sign track greed/fear, and backwardation has historically flagged capitulation bottoms (Dec 2025 deepest backwardation since FTX)
Directly relevant to any CMA built around a futures-based or basis-harvested implementation (the carry IS the realized return of a delta-neutral sleeve)
Well-documented academically (BIS/Management Science crypto-carry) and by index providers (CF Benchmarks), so magnitudes are credible, not hand-waved
Internally consistent with the risk-free-rate building block already in a multi-asset CMA
cons: Fatal for the headline CMA question: the curve is short-dated (<=~13 months on CME, zero-maturity on perps) and literally cannot speak to 10-15yr expected appreciation - it bounds carry, not decade drift

Carry is a risk premium, NOT a spot forecast: Schmeling-Schrimpf-Todorov show crypto carry predicts carry-strategy returns, not the future spot path - extrapolating contango into expected price appreciation is a category error
Basis is dominated by momentum/sentiment (corr ~0.5 with momentum z-scores), so it is highly procyclical and mean-reverting - whatever you read today is regime-contingent and unstable
Compresses toward the risk-free rate as the market matures and ETF arbitrage saturates: 2024's 20-30% collapsed to ~5% by 2026, so historical carry massively overstates forward carry
No long-dated instruments means any decade-horizon use requires the same arbitrary extrapolation this approach was supposed to avoid - it smuggles judgment back in
Says nothing direct about volatility or cross-asset correlations (vs equities, gold, TIPS) - those must be imported from other rows
Offshore-perp funding data is venue-fragmented and can be distorted by exchange-specific leverage, wash volume, and counterparty risk

approaches.rich_notes: Mechanics: annualized basis = (F/S - 1)*(365/days); cash-and-carry profit = basis minus (financing + borrow spread + capital + counterparty cost). CF Benchmarks' worked example nets ~20% gross against SOFR ~5.3% + ~2% borrow = 7.3% cost. Perpetual funding is the zero-maturity analogue: positive funding (longs pay shorts) = priced bullish leverage demand. Regime map (practitioner consensus): normal contango 5-15% APR; euphoria (Q4 2020, Q1 2024) 25-40%; fear/stress mild backwardation. Concrete prints: ~25% Feb-2024, >20% Nov-2024, ~10% May-2025, ~5% by early 2026 as BTC fell and ETF basis capital unwound — by late 2025 Binance overtook CME in BTC futures OI as the cash-and-carry trade died (basis ~5% vs risk-free ~4.5%). This compression is the single most important CMA lesson: the carry that looked like 'free 20%+' in 2024 was a transient, leverage/sentiment-driven premium that mean-reverts toward the financing rate as arbitrage capital saturates — so trailing carry massively overstates forward carry. CRITICAL distinction vs the options-RND row: this needs NO Q-to-P conversion; it reads forward/spot and funding directly. CRITICAL limitation: the literature (BIS Crypto Carry, Schmeling-Schrimpf-Todorov, MgmtSci 2024; carry can exceed 40%/yr) frames carry as a time-varying RISK PREMIUM and segmentation phenomenon, explicitly NOT a forecast of the spot path — so contango must not be read as expected appreciation. Structural ceiling: CME lists 6 consecutive months + 2 Decembers (~13mo max); there are no decade-dated BTC futures anywhere, so any 10-15yr use requires extrapolation this method was meant to avoid. Net role in a CMA: a high-quality near-dated CARRY/financing input and a real-time sentiment/regime gauge, NOT a standalone source of decade drift. My synthesized appreciation deliberately collapses toward (risk-free + thin decaying premium) consistent with the program's appreciation-decay assumption; vol is the imported ~57% floor (carry says nothing about vol); gold corr ~0 per program extrapolation.

approaches.name: Reflexive / Log-Periodic Bubble & Crash-Hazard (LPPLS / JLS)
approaches.description: A return-process framework rather than a single point forecast. Built on the Johansen-Ledoit-Sornette (JLS) rational-expectations bubble model and its Log-Periodic Power Law Singularity (LPPLS) calibration, it treats a crypto bull market as endogenous, faster-than-exponential ("super-exponential") growth driven by herding, imitation and positive feedback among noise traders. Price follows a power-law acceleration toward a finite-time critical time t_c, decorated by accelerating log-periodic oscillations (discrete scale invariance), while a time-varying crash hazard rate h(t) rises toward t_c. The crash itself is an endogenous instability whose precise timing/trigger is exogenous and unpredictable, so the model outputs a probabilistic crash bracket and a confidence/hazard indicator, not a date. Wheatley, Sornette et al. (Royal Society Open Science, 2019) applied it to Bitcoin, anchoring "fundamental value" with a generalized Metcalfe's law (market cap proportional to active-user count raised to ~1.69) and using the price-to-Metcalfe ratio to flag bubbles. A CMA falls out of this logic as a drawdown-hazard-weighted expected return: E[r] = (super-exponential drift) minus (crash hazard x expected crash size), so the distribution is heavily negatively skewed and fat-left-tailed. Over a 10-15yr horizon the meaningful object is not a point appreciation but the shape: trend appreciation that decays as the network matures and the generalized-Metcalfe support grows more slowly, a high volatility floor, and a recurring hazard of 50-80% endogenous drawdowns that mechanically caps the geometric (compounded) return well below the arithmetic drift.
key_drivers: Positive-feedback / reflexive demand: herding, imitation and momentum buying that produce faster-than-exponential (super-exponential) price growth — the core JLS mechanism
Crash hazard rate h(t) rising toward a finite-time critical point t_c; expected return is drift net of hazard x expected jump size
Log-periodic oscillations (discrete scale invariance) — accelerating up/down swings interpreted as spirals of fear/greed, used as the bubble fingerprint
Generalized Metcalfe fundamental support: network value ~ active users^1.69, growing sub-quadratically; the price-to-Metcalfe (MMV) ratio gates overvaluation
Maturation / decay: as the user base and adoption S-curve flatten, the sustainable super-exponential drift decays and bubbles become smaller in relative magnitude
Endogenous instability state (monitorable) vs. exogenous trigger (unpredictable) — the model claims to time the *regime*, not the spark
pros: Produces a genuinely different CMA *shape* — a hazard-weighted, fat-left-tailed return distribution — instead of a single mean/vol, which is more faithful to BTC's actual crash-prone history (four >50% drawdowns documented 2012-2018)
Has a fundamental anchor (generalized Metcalfe, users^1.69, R^2~0.95) so overvaluation is measurable rather than asserted; ties price to an on-chain network observable
Ex-ante, real-time: the LPPLS confidence indicator flagged elevated instability before the 2013 and 2017 BTC peaks, giving probabilistic warning windows rather than post-hoc storytelling
Honestly separates what is forecastable (the bubble regime / hazard) from what is not (the exact crash date and trigger) — intellectually disciplined about its own limits
Captures reflexivity and momentum that mean-reverting or random-walk CMAs structurally miss; directly models the compounding penalty crashes impose on long-horizon geometric returns
cons: Severe overfitting risk: the LPPLS function has 7+ nonlinear parameters and fits accelerating/oscillating data almost regardless of whether a true bubble exists — high in-sample R^2 is nearly guaranteed and not evidence

Critical-time t_c is notoriously unstable: published replications show t_c jumping by weeks depending on the initial guess and the calibration window; point predictions are effectively meaningless (authors themselves call long-term single-model predictions 'misleading')

No native, validated CMA number: the framework yields hazard windows and bubble flags, not a 10-15yr expected-return/vol figure — every quantitative CMA under it is the analyst's reconstruction, not a published output
Tiny sample of genuine bubbles (4) makes false-positive vs. miss rates statistically ambiguous; out-of-sample, real-time crash 'predictions' have a poor and contested track record

Generalized Metcalfe support is itself fragile: the 1.69 exponent is fit to one asset's short history, user/active-address counts are noisy and gameable, and price feeds back into usage, contaminating the 'fundamental'
Says nothing useful about cross-asset correlations (gold, TIPS, equities, FI) — those rows are silent in the literature, so correlation inputs must come entirely from elsewhere
Explicitly blind to exogenous shocks ('massive exogenous shocks could occur at any time, and the LPPLS model can provide no warning there') — exactly the tail an investor most cares about

approaches.rich_notes: Core BTC reference: Wheatley, Sornette, Huber, Reppen, Gantner (Royal Society Open Science, 2019; arXiv:1803.05663). LPPLS log-price model: ln(p) = A + (t_c - t)^m [B + C cos(omega ln(t_c - t) + phi)], with 0<m<1, fitted m roughly 0.10-0.43 and log-periodic omega roughly 7.8-12 across the four BTC bubbles; AR(1) phi 0.87-0.99. Fundamental anchor is a generalized Metcalfe's law: market cap ~ active-users^1.69 (beta = 1.69 +/- 0.008, R^2 ~ 0.95 over 2010-2018), explicitly rejecting classic N^2. Four documented BTC bubbles: 2012 (3.1x runup), early-2013 (20.4x), late-2013 (6.8x), and the 2015-2017 run (~103x to ~$20k). At writing (Mar 2018, ~$170B cap) the price-to-Metcalfe ratio implied roughly 4x-8x overvaluation vs support. CMA derivation logic: E[r] = super-exponential drift - h(t) x E[crash size]; over 10-15yr the drift decays with network maturation while the hazard of 50-80% drawdowns recurs, mechanically depressing geometric vs arithmetic return and producing a fat-left-tailed, negatively skewed distribution — this is the row's distinctive contribution: it is a survival/return-process shape, not a point. Brutally honest caveats (well-documented in the literature and replications): (1) LPPLS overfits — 7+ nonlinear params fit any accelerating/oscillating series; high in-sample R^2 is not evidence of a bubble; (2) t_c is unstable — replications show the predicted critical time shifting by weeks with the initial guess/window, and the authors concede single-model long-horizon predictions are 'effectively meaningless'; (3) the model is explicitly blind to exogenous shocks ('the LPPLS model can provide no warning there'); (4) only 4 true bubbles -> false-positive vs miss rates are statistically ambiguous, and out-of-sample real-time skill is contested. Correlation cells are 'n/a (source silent)' in cited_outputs because this literature does not report cross-asset correlations at all; the synthesized correlations are imported from general BTC market data (BTC-gold ~0 long-run per NYDIG; BTC-equity ~0.2-0.4) and flagged as judgment. Numbers in synthesized_outputs are the analyst's reasoned 10-15yr judgment under this approach's hazard logic, NOT published model outputs.

issues: MISATTRIBUTED CITATION (source #4): The JSON lists 'J. C. Gerlach, G. Demos, D. Sornette, "Real-time prediction of Bitcoin bubble crashes," 2019, arXiv:1905.09647.' This conflates two distinct papers. arXiv:1905.09647 'Real-time Prediction of Bitcoin Bubble Crashes' is authored by Min Shu and Wei Zhu (published Physica A, 2020), NOT Gerlach/Demos/Sornette. The actual Gerlach-Demos-Sornette 2019 RSOS paper is titled 'Dissection of Bitcoin's multiscale bubble history from January 2012 to February 2018' (arXiv:1804.06261, doi:10.1098/rsos.180643). The cited title, authors, and arXiv ID belong to three inconsistent sources mashed together.

INTERNAL NUMERICAL TENSION (variance drag vs stated wedge): The synthesized outputs pair ~60-70% annualized vol with an arithmetic-to-geometric wedge of only ~7pts (12-16% arithmetic -> 4-9% geometric). Under standard lognormal variance drag, sigma^2/2 at 60% vol is ~18pts of drag alone, which would push a 12-16% arithmetic drift to roughly -6% to -2% geometric BEFORE adding any separate crash-hazard term. The note treats crash-hazard as the whole gap, but vol drag already exceeds the stated gap. Reconcilable only if the distribution is strongly non-lognormal (which the fat-left-tail framing asserts), but the numbers don't cleanly close under the arithmetic the row implies.

VOL FLOOR LOOKS HIGH vs REALIZED: The '~57% vol floor even as the asset matures' is above recent realized BTC vol, which fell below 50% across 2023 and printed an all-time low near 40% in 2024 (Fidelity/Kaiko/CFA Institute). Defensible as a crash-inclusive long-horizon CMA assumption (vol clusters/accelerates near t_c), but it is on the aggressive side and should be flagged as such rather than stated as a 'floor.'

MINOR IMPRECISION: con #1 says LPPLS has '7+ nonlinear parameters.' The standard LPPLS has 7 parameters total (3 nonlinear + 4 linear); Filimonov-Sornette 2013 (cited as source #5) explicitly reduces this to 3 nonlinear. Calling all 7+ 'nonlinear' is technically loose, though the overfitting concern itself is valid and well-supported.

(2019), 'Dissection of Bitcoin's multiscale bubble history from January 2012 to February 2018,' Royal Society Open Science 6:180643 (arXiv:1804.06261); OR (b) if the Shu-Zhu real-time-prediction paper is wanted, cite it correctly as Shu, M. & Zhu, W. (2020), 'Real-time prediction of Bitcoin bubble crashes,' Physica A 548:124477 (arXiv:1905.09647). Do not blend the two. | Reword con #1 to '7 parameters (3 nonlinear + 4 linear)' to be accurate and consistent with cited source #5. | Either lower the vol floor toward ~45-50% or explicitly label the ~57% as a crash-inclusive long-run average that sits above recent calm-regime realized vol (sub-50% since 2023, ~40% low in 2024), so it doesn't read as a hard floor contradicted by data. | Reconcile the vol/return arithmetic: if keeping ~60% vol, state explicitly that the 4-9% geometric figure already embeds variance drag (~18pts at 60% vol) on top of crash hazard, rather than presenting crash hazard as the sole driver of the arithmetic-to-geometric gap. Verified-correct items (no change needed): 1.69 Metcalfe exponent, R^2~0.95, four bubbles with 3.1x/20.4x/6.8x/~103x runups, LPPLS equation form, main-paper arXiv:1803.05663 and doi:10.1098/rsos.180538, JLS 2000 IJTAF 3:219-255, Filimonov-Sornette 2013 Physica A, the exogenous-shock-blindness caveat, BTC-gold ~0 / BTC-equity 0.2-0.4 correlation anchors.

approaches.name: Regime-Switching / Jump-Diffusion & Heavy-Tail Return Process
approaches.description: A family of econometric models of the Bitcoin RETURN-GENERATING PROCESS itself, rather than of its fair price. Instead of a single decaying drift and one ~50-57% volatility scalar, these models specify the full conditional return distribution: (1) Markov-switching / MS-GARCH models that let returns flip between an unobserved 'calm' low-vol regime and a 'turbulent' high-vol regime, each with its own mean and variance and a transition matrix; (2) affine jump-diffusion / SVCJ (stochastic-volatility-with-correlated-jumps) models, where vol is itself a mean-reverting stochastic process with discrete jumps that are negatively correlated with simultaneous price jumps (a 'leverage' co-jump); (3) Hawkes self-exciting processes where each jump raises the short-run probability of the next, producing the observed clustering of crashes/squeezes; and (4) heavy-tail distributional models (alpha-stable, GARCH with skewed-t innovations, EVT/POT) that fit the power-law tail directly. The CMA value of this family is NOT a different appreciation number, it is the SHAPE: vol-of-vol, kurtosis/tail index, expected-shortfall and expected-max-drawdown, and regime persistence. These are the inputs portfolio-sizing (CVaR/ES budgeting) and options desks need, and that every point-vol approach silently omits.
key_drivers: Regime state variable: an unobserved Markov chain (usually 2, sometimes 3 states) that switches the entire return distribution between calm/bull and turbulent/bear regimes, with its own mean, variance and transition probabilities (which the data also says are only weakly persistent for BTC vs equities)
Stochastic volatility: vol modeled as a mean-reverting latent process (kappa, theta, vol-of-vol sigma_v) rather than a constant, so the CMA sigma is a distribution, not a scalar

Jumps in returns AND in variance, with the two jumps correlated (SVCJ rho_J<0): a price crash and a vol spike arrive together, fattening the left tail beyond what diffusion plus return-jumps alone produce

Self-excitation (Hawkes): jump intensity is path-dependent — a jump today raises the conditional intensity of the next jump, generating empirically-observed crash/squeeze clustering and volatility persistence

Heavy-tail innovation law: power-law / alpha-stable / skewed-t tail with an estimated tail index alpha (BTC ~2.1-2.5, vs ~3 for equities) and large excess kurtosis, fit directly to extremes via EVT/peaks-over-threshold
Leverage / asymmetry: negative shocks raise future vol more than positive shocks of equal size (EGARCH/GJR asymmetry, and the negative return-vol jump correlation)
pros: Targets the right object for a CMA's RISK side: it produces vol-of-vol, kurtosis, tail index, expected shortfall and expected-max-drawdown — exactly the inputs CVaR-based sizing and option pricing need, which a single sigma cannot supply

Empirically dominant in-sample and out-of-sample: MS-GARCH and SVCJ specifications beat single-regime / pure-diffusion models on VaR backtests and option-pricing RMSE across multiple peer-reviewed studies — this is not a fringe view, it is the consensus econometric description

Captures documented BTC stylized facts other approaches deny: fat tails (tail index ~2.1-2.5), volatility clustering, vol-of-vol, leverage/asymmetry, and synchronized price-and-vol crashes (correlated co-jumps)

Honest about drawdown shape: the realized -77% to -93% cyclical drawdowns are tail events that a lognormal 57%-vol model assigns near-zero probability; this family reproduces them, making it the right lens for 'how bad is the bad case over 10-15yr'

Regime framing reconciles the empirical-anchor instability (142%->65%->17% appreciation, 103%->57% vol across windows): those are not parameter drift to be averaged away, they are regime realizations, which argues directly for a path/scenario CMA over a point CMA

Internally consistent with the options-implied row: the same SVCJ/jump structure that fits returns also fits the Deribit vol surface and DVOL, so the physical-measure CMA and the risk-neutral measure can be tied together
cons: Says almost nothing about the DRIFT: these are conditional-second-moment-and-tail models; the regime means are estimated noisily off a short, bull-dominated sample and have essentially no forward predictive content for 10-15yr appreciation. This family must borrow its appreciation number from elsewhere (decay/adoption/TAM rows)

Severe parameter instability on BTC's short history: ~13-16 years, one micro-cap era, ~4 cycles. Jump intensity, regime means and transition probabilities are estimated on a handful of regime realizations, so standard errors are large and estimates are highly sample/window-dependent — false precision risk is real

Horizon mismatch: most of these are fit on daily or high-frequency (5-min) data for VaR/option pricing at days-to-months horizons. Extrapolating a daily MS-GARCH/SVCJ to a 10-15yr unconditional distribution requires strong stationarity assumptions the data violates (the process is itself non-stationary and maturing)

Identification fragility: separating a 'jump' from a high-vol diffusion draw, or a regime switch from a vol cluster, is statistically delicate; different filters (MCMC vs sequential learning vs threshold) give materially different jump counts and tail indices

Weak BTC regime persistence specifically: studies note BTC's regimes are less persistent than equities', so the clean 'calm vs crisis' story is muddier — switching is frequent and noisy, weakening the regime-conditional CMA

Maturation breaks the fit forward: ETF/institutional access is plausibly compressing the tail and dampening the leverage-feedback crashes that produced past -80% drawdowns (K33's argument), so a model calibrated on 2011-2022 extremes likely OVERstates forward tail risk — yet there is too little post-institutional data to recalibrate
Not a standalone CMA: on its own it yields no appreciation and no cross-asset correlation forecast (most papers are univariate on BTC) — it is a risk-shape overlay, not a full row

approaches.rich_notes:
WHY THIS ROW EXISTS (the completeness gap it fills): every other approach in the table outputs a single decaying drift and one volatility scalar (~50-57%). That badly misstates DRAWDOWN and TAIL shape — the very thing that determines a real-world BTC allocation. This family is the return-process / risk-shape row: its deliverable is vol-of-vol, kurtosis/tail index, expected shortfall, expected-max-drawdown, and regime persistence — NOT a different appreciation number. It should be read as an overlay on the drift rows, not a competitor to them.

FOUR SUB-FAMILIES & WHAT EACH CONTRIBUTES:
1. Markov-switching / MS-GARCH (Ardia-Bluteau-Rüede 2019 Economics Letters; Caporale-Zekokh 2019 RIBAF; Shakourloo-Azimli 2025 SSRN). Two (sometimes three) latent regimes — calm/low-vol vs turbulent/high-vol — each with own mean & variance and a transition matrix. Consistent finding: MS-GARCH with a skewed fat-tailed (skewed-t) conditional law beats single-regime GARCH on out-of-sample VaR backtests. Important caveat the literature flags: BTC's regimes are LESS persistent than equities' — switching is frequent/noisy ('weak state persistence'), so the clean calm-vs-crisis dichotomy is muddier for BTC.
2. SVCJ — stochastic vol with correlated jumps (the crypto-options literature; arXiv 2009.11007 'Pricing cryptocurrency options', 2020; Springer Digital Finance 'Cryptos have rough volatility and correlated jumps', 2025). Vol is a mean-reverting latent process AND there are jumps in BOTH returns and variance, negatively correlated (a price crash and vol spike arrive together; rho_J<0). Adding variance-jumps materially improves fit vs return-jumps-only. The 2025 'rough volatility' paper (from 3+ yrs of 5-min data) finds BTC vol is rough (low Hurst) WITH correlated jumps — i.e. both micro-roughness and macro-jumps are needed.
3. Hawkes self-exciting (arXiv 2510.21297 'Jump risk premia in the presence of clustered jumps', 2025; multivariate Hawkes LOB studies). Each jump raises the short-run intensity of the next, reproducing crash/squeeze CLUSTERING. Cross-exciting bivariate Hawkes generates asymmetric, time-varying skew (sign of the IV skew can flip with sentiment). Jump-contagion study: positive-sentiment jumps cause moderate cross-contagion; negative-sentiment jumps less so — asymmetric.
4. Heavy-tail / EVT (Begušić-Kostanjčar-Stanley-Podobnik 2018 Physica A 'Scaling properties of extreme price fluctuations'). Direct tail-index estimation: BTC tail exponent 2<alpha<2.5 (vs ~3 for stocks), i.e. FATTER tails; notably OUTSIDE the Lévy-stable region, and tail index is time-varying (drifts from ~2 toward ~3 as the market matures). Large, slowly-decaying excess kurtosis.

KEY NUMERIC ANCHORS PULLED:
- Tail index alpha ~2.1-2.5 (heavier than equities ~3); time-varying, thinning with maturation.
- Jump intensity (option-pricing jump-diffusion estimates): lambda ~0.10-0.17 per year, with sizeable jump vol — jumps are frequent and large.
- Correlated co-jumps: a 'sizeable proportion of price jumps are significantly and contemporaneously ANTI-correlated with jumps in volatility' (leverage co-jump).
- Historical peak-to-trough drawdowns: -93% (2011), -86% (2015), -84% (2018), -77% (2022). A clear DECLINING-severity trend cycle-over-cycle as cap grows; extrapolations put the next trough ~ -70% to -76%. K33 Research (2026) argues a fresh -80%+ is now 'structurally unlikely' because regulated-product access removes the extreme leverage-feedback loops that drove prior capitulations — directly supporting a forward expected-max-drawdown SHALLOWER than history (~ -55% to -75% over 10-15yr).

HOW THIS RECONCILES THE EMPIRICAL ANCHOR'S INSTABILITY: the anchor shows appreciation 142%->65%->17% and vol 103%->57% across full/10y/5y windows, and correlations that RISE in recent windows (growth-eq 0.26->0.36->0.56). A regime model says: don't average these into one point — they are regime realizations and a maturing process. The forward CMA should be a path/scenario distribution. The single most important synthesized output of this row is therefore the EXPECTED MAX DRAWDOWN (~ -55% to -75%) and REGIME-CONDITIONAL correlations (diversification collapses in the turbulent regime, corr to growth equities ->0.7-0.8 in crises), NOT the sigma.

BRUTAL HONESTY: (a) zero forward drift content — the row must borrow appreciation from the decay/adoption/TAM rows; presenting regime means as a forecast would be a mistake. (b) Estimated on ~13-16yr / ~4 cycles / one micro-cap era → wide standard errors, false-precision risk, heavy window dependence. (c) Daily/HF calibration extrapolated to 10-15yr requires stationarity the process violates (it is itself non-stationary and maturing). (d) Maturation likely makes any 2011-2022-calibrated tail OVERstate forward risk, but there isn't enough post-ETF data to recalibrate — so the honest stance is 'fat-tailed but thinning, deep-drawdown but shallower than history.'

GOLD-CORRELATION & FORWARD-CMA ALIGNMENT: consistent with the forward anchor (~0 gold corr, vol floor ~57%, appreciation decaying). This row's refinement: ~0 gold correlation on AVERAGE but with regime-dependent tail behavior, and a vol 'floor' that is really a calm-regime level with a fat high-vol regime above it. The deliverable is the tail/hazard shape, exactly as the task requires for a return-process row.

approaches.name: Survival / Ruin-Probability (Absorbing-Zero Hazard)
approaches.description: Frames Bitcoin's CMA explicitly as a probability-weighted MIXTURE of two paths rather than a single point estimate: a 'survival' path on which BTC behaves like a maturing macro-asset, and an 'absorbing-zero' path on which the network is abandoned and the asset goes permanently to -100%. The expected 10-15yr return is E[R] = S(T)*R_survival + (1 - S(T))*(-100%), where S(T) = exp(-integral of the annual hazard h(t)) is the cumulative survival probability. This is the rigorous, parameterized form of the 'left-tail haircut' that other CMA rows apply by hand-waving. Three academic strands supply the theoretical backbone for WHY a non-trivial absorbing state exists: (1) Schilling-Uhlig (JME 2019) endowment-economy models where Bitcoin can rationally collapse to its 'fundamental' value of zero as a convergent supermartingale; (2) Biais et al. (J. Finance 2023) general-equilibrium models with multiple equilibria and sunspots, where coordination can shift agents off the positive-value equilibrium; and (3) Taleb (2021) absorbing-barrier argument that a non-dividend asset with any positive probability per period of hitting an irreversible zero has a present value pulled hard toward zero over an infinite horizon. Insurance/actuarial ruin theory and Cox proportional-hazard estimation (Balutel & Voia 2023) supply the estimation machinery. Critically, practitioners argue the hazard is DECLINING in age (Lindy effect, formalized by Ord 2023 as a mixture-of-exponentials over an unknown true hazard), so S(T) is materially higher than a constant-hazard model implies. Fidelity's risk team has published the cleanest single number: a ~0.71%/yr Bitcoin 'extinction' probability from a 27-variable Monte Carlo (vs Tesla 2.2%, Apple 0.06%). The whole point of the approach is that the SHAPE of the CMA — a bimodal payoff with a fat point-mass at -100% and a right-skewed survival distribution — matters far more than any single expected-return figure.
key_drivers: Annual hazard rate h(t) of the absorbing-zero state — the probability per year that the network is permanently abandoned / loses monetary value irreversibly (Fidelity's published anchor: ~0.71%/yr; practitioner ranges 1-5%/yr early, lower later)

Hazard term-structure / Lindy decay: whether h(t) is constant, or declines with network age as security budget, liquidity, regulatory acceptance and adoption accrue (Ord 2023 mixture-of-exponentials => declining observed hazard => remaining-life ∝ current age)
Cumulative survival probability S(T) = exp(-∫h(t)dt) over the 10-15yr horizon — the weight on the survival path; with h≈1%/yr and 12yr, S≈0.89; with h≈3%/yr, S≈0.70

Survival-path conditional return R_survival — the appreciation BTC earns CONDITIONAL on not dying (drawn from whichever fundamental model you trust: adoption S-curve, store-of-value TAM, monetary substitution)
Recovery value on the death path (assumed -100%; some variants allow a small salvage/fork-residual, but the canonical absorbing state is zero and irreversible)

Theoretical existence of the zero equilibrium: Schilling-Uhlig collapse supermartingale + Biais sunspot/multiple-equilibria coordination failure (the 'why' behind a non-zero hazard, independent of any technical exploit)

Path-dependence / irreversibility (Taleb): once below a confidence/liquidity threshold the network's active-maintenance requirement makes zero an absorbing, non-recovering state — unlike gold whose value is not path-dependent
pros: Honest about the dominant feature of BTC's payoff that almost every other CMA approach buries: a genuine, non-negligible point-mass at -100%. It turns the vague 'left-tail haircut' into an explicit, auditable parameter (the hazard) instead of a fudge factor.

Decomposable and modular: lets you bolt ANY survival-path return model (adoption S-curve, TAM, options-implied) onto a transparent ruin overlay, so the death risk is priced once, consistently, rather than smuggled into a lower point estimate.

Grounded in real, peer-reviewed theory for the EXISTENCE of the absorbing state — Schilling-Uhlig collapse equilibria and Biais et al. sunspots show zero can be a rational equilibrium with no exploit required, which is a far stronger argument than 'it might get hacked.'

Naturally produces the bimodal / heavily-right-skewed return distribution that matches BTC's empirical behavior, and makes the mean a poor summary statistic — pushing users toward median, mode, and probability-of-ruin, which is the correct mental model for position sizing.

The declining-hazard (Lindy) refinement is empirically motivated and testable: 16+ years of survival, growing institutional/ETF ownership and security budget are direct evidence that S(T) should be revised UP over time — the framework cleanly absorbs that evidence.
Mirrors how insurers, credit desks and venture portfolios already think (default/ruin probability * loss-given-default), so it ports a mature, well-understood risk discipline onto a new asset.
cons: The hazard rate is essentially UNFALSIFIABLE over the horizons that matter: a 1%/yr vs 3%/yr vs 5%/yr 'death probability' swings the CMA enormously, yet there is one observed history (n=1, still alive) so the parameter is almost pure prior. Fidelity's 0.71% is a model output dressed as a measurement.

It only relocates the hard problem — you STILL need a survival-path return model, so survival-hazard is a wrapper, not a standalone valuation. Garbage R_survival in, garbage CMA out; the overlay can lend false rigor to a weak core forecast.

Taleb's strong form (any positive absorbing probability over infinite horizon => present value zero) is mathematically clean but economically self-undermining: it would also zero out any fiat currency, any single company, arguably any asset, since all have some irreversible-ruin probability over infinite time. The result hinges on infinite-horizon and a non-dividend assumption that real 10-15yr CMAs don't use.

Declining-hazard (Lindy) and the absorbing-barrier camp reach OPPOSITE conclusions from the same survival data, and the framework can't adjudicate — it just exposes the prior. Lindy assumes heterogeneity in a fixed unknown hazard; if BTC's hazard is genuinely time-varying or regime-dependent, the Pareto/Lindy scaling is unjustified.

Empirically thin estimation: the one peer-reviewed hazard study (Balutel & Voia 2023, Cox PH) models price-SHOCK timing, not network EXTINCTION — there is no clean event-history dataset of comparable-asset 'deaths' to fit a real baseline hazard to. The actuarial machinery is borrowed without the actuarial data.

Says NOTHING about correlations, volatility term structure, or cross-asset moments — it is purely a mean/ruin-of-the-distribution tool. Every co-movement figure a CMA needs must come from elsewhere, so as a CMA row it is structurally incomplete.

Behavioral mis-anchoring risk: a single published 'extinction probability' invites spurious precision and false comfort (or false alarm); the true uncertainty is on the hazard ITSELF, a second-order parameter the headline number hides.

Fidelity publishes only the ~0.71%/yr extinction probability (the (1-S) weight), not R_survival. The Bitcoin Magazine five-outcome model yields an expected VALUE (~$150k/BTC at time of writing) rather than an annualized appreciation rate.
cited_outputs.appreciation_real: n/a (source silent) — no survival-hazard source publishes a real long-horizon appreciation; the approach outputs a ruin-weighted mean, and the death-path is -100% in both nominal and real terms.
cited_outputs.volatility: n/a (no point figure) — the family implies extreme, bimodal payoff dispersion (Biais et al.: a MAJORITY of BTC return variance is 'extrinsic'/sunspot volatility unrelated to fundamentals) but publishes no annualized vol number; the absorbing-zero point-mass makes ordinary stdev a poor descriptor.

synthesized_outputs.appreciation_nominal: ~5-9%/yr expected (JUDGMENT, center ~7%), but the point estimate is the WRONG summary for this approach — the honest output is a distribution. Construction: take a survival-path conditional return R_survival ≈ ~10-12%/yr (itself the decayed extrapolation of the empirical-anchor appreciation collapse 142%→65%→17%, settling into a mature macro-asset rate), and apply a Lindy-style DECLINING hazard averaging ~1.5-2%/yr over the 12yr horizon (anchored above Fidelity's 0.71% to stay conservative on model risk, below the 3-5% early-stage practitioner range). With h̄≈1.75%/yr over 12yr, S(12)≈exp(-0.21)≈0.81. Then E[R_cum] = 0.81*(1.11^12) - 1 ≈ 0.81*3.5 - 1 ≈ +183% cumulative ≈ ~8.9%/yr; netting model/estimation haircut I center the annualized CMA at ~7%. The defining feature is BIMODAL: ~80% probability mass on a right-skewed survival path (median annualized likely low-double-digits) and ~19% mass at -100%. The mean understates the modal/median survival outcome and overstates the typical experience — by design.
synthesized_outputs.appreciation_real: ~4-6%/yr (center ~4.5%), i.e. nominal less ~2.5% assumed CPI on the survival path; the death path is -100% real, so the ruin-weighting drags the real mean down symmetrically with the nominal.
synthesized_outputs.volatility: ~60-75%/yr (center ~65%), structurally ABOVE the trailing-5y realized ~57% floor and above most other rows' forward estimates, because this approach explicitly retains the absorbing-zero point-mass and the Biais 'extrinsic/sunspot' variance that does NOT mean-revert away as the asset matures. Decomposition matters: conditional-on-survival vol decays toward ~50%, but the ~19% ruin mass at -100% FATTENS total dispersion, so the unconditional vol stays elevated. I extrapolate ~65% as a tail/hazard-aware figure rather than the ~50% a survival-only model would give.
synthesized_outputs.corr_growth_eq: ~0.45 (judgment; the approach gives no correlation, anchored to trailing-5y realized 0.56 with mild mean-reversion — risk-on/liquidity beta persists, and a coordination-driven death event would itself likely cluster with risk-off equity drawdowns, nudging realized co-movement up in the left tail)
synthesized_outputs.corr_value_eq: ~0.30 (judgment; anchored to trailing-5y 0.37)
synthesized_outputs.corr_fi_nominal: ~0.10 (judgment; trailing-5y 0.19 fading toward ~0.1 long-run; near-zero with no stable sign)
synthesized_outputs.corr_tips: ~0.15 (judgment; trailing-5y 0.30, real-rate/liquidity sensitivity partially persists; not an inflation claim in this framework)
synthesized_outputs.corr_gold: ~0.05 (judgment; realized ~0.03-0.05, near-zero. Kept ~0 deliberately: Taleb's own argument SEVERS the digital-gold analogy by making BTC absorbing/path-dependent and gold not, so this approach gives no support for a tight gold correlation — extrapolate ~0)

approaches.rich_notes:
METHODOLOGY. The CMA is a two-state mixture: E[R(T)] = S(T)*R_survival + (1-S(T))*(-100%), with S(T)=exp(-∫₀ᵀ h(t)dt). h(t) is the instantaneous annual hazard of entering an irreversible, absorbing zero. Everything turns on (a) the LEVEL of h and (b) its TERM STRUCTURE.

WHY A ZERO STATE EXISTS (the genuinely academic part). Three independent arguments, none requiring a technical exploit: (1) SCHILLING-UHLIG, 'Some Simple Bitcoin Economics,' JME 106 (2019) 16-26 (NBER w24483; SSRN 3155310). In their endowment economy with Dollar and Bitcoin, the fundamental pricing equation makes the BTC/USD price a martingale in the simple case; under their conditions Bitcoin prices form convergent SUPERMARTINGALES that can drift to the fundamental value of zero — collapse is a rational equilibrium, a generalization of the Kareken-Wallace (1981) exchange-rate-indeterminacy result. (2) BIAIS, BISIÈRE, BOUVARD, CASAMATTA, MENKVELD, 'Equilibrium Bitcoin Pricing,' Journal of Finance 78(2), 2023, 967-1014 (DOI 10.1111/jofi.13206). Because current value depends on FUTURE transactional benefits which depend on future prices, the equation is self-referential => MULTIPLE EQUILIBRIA + SUNSPOTS => 'extrinsic volatility... prices fluctuate even when fundamentals are constant,' and a LARGER share of return variance is extrinsic than fundamental. A coordination shift can move agents off the positive-value equilibrium — i.e. a non-technical route to (near-)zero. (3) TALEB, 'Bitcoin, Currencies, and Fragility,' arXiv 2106.14204 (2021). Absorbing-barrier theorem: for a non-dividend asset, if there is ANY positive probability per period of hitting an irreversible zero, the present value over an infinite horizon is pulled to zero; BTC's reliance on continuous active maintenance makes zero absorbing and PATH-DEPENDENT, whereas gold's value is not path-dependent. This is the strong-form bound; I treat it as the left edge of the prior, not the central estimate, because the infinite-horizon + zero-recovery assumptions are inappropriate for a finite 10-15yr CMA.

ESTIMATING THE HAZARD. (a) FIDELITY's risk team publishes the cleanest usable number: a ~0.71%/yr Bitcoin 'extinction' probability from a 27-variable Monte Carlo, explicitly benchmarked against single-name equities (Tesla ~2.2%/yr, Apple ~0.06%/yr) — i.e. Fidelity literally treats network-death as a survivable-firm-style ruin probability. (b) BALUTEL & VOIA, 'Surviving the Storm: Hazard Models and Signaling Shocks in Bitcoin Prices,' Revue française d'économie XXXVIII (2023) 21-46, fit a COX PROPORTIONAL-HAZARD model — the canonical survival-analysis estimator — but to price-SHOCK timing, not extinction; it demonstrates the machinery is applicable to BTC while underscoring that no clean network-DEATH event-history dataset exists. (c) The DECLINING-hazard refinement: practitioners invoke the LINDY EFFECT (Bitcoin has outlived 450+ 'obituaries' since 2013), formalized by TOBY ORD, 'The Lindy Effect,' arXiv 2308.09045 (2023): if the true constant hazard is UNKNOWN and you mix exponential survival curves over a prior on that hazard, the observed/effective hazard DECLINES with age and remaining life expectancy scales with current age (Pareto tail). Implication for the CMA: S(T) should be revised UP as the network ages, so a constant-hazard model UNDER-states survival. The counter-camp (Mark Liu, 'Debunking the Lindy Effect for Cryptocurrencies') notes Lindy requires the right heterogeneity assumption and need not hold if BTC's hazard is genuinely regime-dependent.

PRACTITIONER EV FORM. Bitcoin Magazine's 'Exploring Bitcoin Valuation Models' is the cleanest retail statement of the mixture: a five-outcome, arbitrarily-weighted distribution with an explicit zero outcome whose probability SHRINKS 'with each day that the Bitcoin network survives' while right-skew is preserved; their illustrative expected value was ~$150k/BTC. VanEck's Bitcoin LTCMA work is the asset-manager cousin (scenario-weighted price paths), though its headline is a TAM/adoption survival path rather than a formal hazard.

WHY THE SHAPE BEATS THE POINT. The whole value of this row is that it refuses to collapse BTC to a single number. The payoff is BIMODAL: a fat point-mass at -100% plus a right-skewed survival lobe. Consequences a CMA user must respect: (i) the MEAN is a poor summary — median and mode of the survival lobe are much higher than the ruin-weighted mean, while the modal experience of a SINGLE investor is closer to the survival path OR total loss, rarely the mean; (ii) VOLATILITY is structurally elevated and does NOT decay to a survival-only floor because the absorbing mass fattens dispersion (this is why I synthesize ~65% vol vs the ~50% a survival-only model would print, and above the ~57% trailing-5y realized floor); (iii) position sizing should be driven by probability-of-ruin and Kelly/CVaR logic, not by E[R]. 

RELATION TO OTHER ROWS. This is the rigorous parent of every 'left-tail haircut' applied elsewhere (store-of-value TAM, adoption S-curve, options-implied): those rows lower a point estimate by a vague amount; this row makes the haircut an explicit, parameterized hazard and shows the haircut is not a translation of the mean but a CHANGE OF SHAPE. It is the natural complement to the Equilibrium/Game-Theoretic row (same Schilling-Uhlig/Biais theory) — that row explains WHY the zero equilibrium exists; this row PRICES the probability of reaching it.

HONEST BOTTOM LINE. The hazard parameter is near-unfalsifiable (n=1, still alive), so the headline ~7% CMA is a thin veneer over a prior; the durable contribution is the SHAPE (bimodal, ~80% survival / ~19% ruin, vol ~65%) and the discipline of pricing ruin explicitly rather than smuggling it into a lower mean. Correlations are entirely judgment — the family produces no cross-asset moments — and gold correlation is kept ~0 because Taleb's own logic severs the digital-gold analogy.

This is the single cleanest 'what does the market actually price' anchor and is distinct from the RND/vol-surface row (it needs no Q->P conversion for the carry signal). Reflexive / log-periodic bubble & crash-hazard models (Sornette LPPLS / JLS, Wheatley-Sornette generalized-Metcalfe-with-bubble-overlay). The review cites Wheatley-Sornette only for the Metcalfe beta=1.69 regression, but their actual contribution is a super-exponential bubble + critical-time crash-hazard framework. This is a recognized academic family that produces a fundamentally different CMA shape (drawdown-hazard-weighted expected return) and is currently absent.

Regime-switching / Markov / jump-diffusion & heavy-tail (alpha-stable, GARCH-jump, Hawkes) return-process models. Every kept approach treats vol as a single decaying scalar (~45-55%); none represents the large academic strand that models BTC return as a multi-regime / jump process. This matters because it changes the SHAPE of the vol/tail input (a single 50% sigma badly misstates drawdown risk in a fat-tailed jump asset) and feeds directly into the portfolio-sizing and options rows.

Survival / ruin-probability (absorbing-zero) models. Multiple rows mention collapse equilibria (Schilling-Uhlig price=0, Biais sunspots) and 'left-tail haircuts,' but no row explicitly frames BTC's CMA as a probability-weighted mixture of a survival path and a go-to-zero path with an estimated annual hazard rate. This is the rigorous way to express the 'left-tail mass the single-path fit ignores' that several rows hand-wave, and deserves its own family.

Relative-value / cross-crypto (BTC dominance, BTC-vs-ETH, BTC-vs-altcoin-basket) and BTC-vs-equity-proxy (MSTR/COIN/miner basket) approaches. The whole review is BTC-in-isolation vs traditional assets; the practitioner world also sets a BTC view relative to the rest of crypto and to listed BTC proxies. Minor for a 10-15yr CMA but a genuine family gap.

Energy-value / joule-per-coin and 'thermoeconomic' valuation (distinct from cost-of-production floor). A small but real strand prices BTC off cumulative energy embodied rather than marginal mining cost; it overlaps the cost row but is a separate mechanism.
