Portfolio-sizing: Grayscale '2026 Digital Asset Outlook' single-digit framing could not be confirmed to a figure (row admits this); JPM-AM BTC-abstention rests on the deck itself, not corroborated reporting (LTCMA row).
On-chain: 2013 MVRV-ratio peak '~5.4-5.7' is stated more precisely than the public record supports (only the MVRV Z-score peak decay ~8.8->7.1 is cleanly verifiable).

Options-implied: the '44%-102%/yr' band is mislabeled as a regime spread when it is actually a method x regime spread (BP point estimates are 62%-69%); the gold-corr 0.10 nudge sits above the realized ~0.045.

Metcalfe: practitioner '31%/yr CAGR' and '$1.5M-by-2035' are author-derived inferences, not Peterson-published CMAs; Peterson R^2 ~0.93-0.95 is mis-attributed (0.95 belongs to Wheatley-Sornette, Peterson's own is ~70%+).
Power-law: raw central-line CAGR is 26.7% (2026-2041) but the row presents '22-27%' as if 27% were itself a haircut — the band overlaps the un-haircut model output.
cross_cutting_observations: The appreciation-decay anchor (142% full -> 65% 10y -> 17% trailing-5y) is the single dominant force in the entire review: EVERY one of the 16 kept approaches — scarcity, network-value, cost, power-law, TAM, monetary, on-chain, factor, options, equilibrium, DCF, adoption, sizing, LTCMA — explicitly imports this decay curve and lands its synthesized nominal in a ~6-15% band, regardless of the model's native logic. The synthesis should state plainly that the decay anchor, not any model, is doing the work; the models mostly supply a NARRATIVE wrapper around a common realized-decay extrapolation. The honest cross-approach central is ~8-12% nominal / ~5-9% real.

The ~0 realized BTC-gold correlation (-0.011 / 0.033 / 0.045) is a structural problem for every gold-parity / digital-gold / TAM-substitution and debasement approach, and the review correctly catches it repeatedly: the families whose VALUATION mechanism is 'BTC penetrates gold's market cap' (S2FX, SoV-TAM, monetary-substitution, DCF-moneyness, adoption-S-curve, LTCMA) all assign a positive forward gold-corr (0.15-0.35) that exceeds realized ~0. This is the review's most consistent defect-cluster: the TAM mechanism REQUIRES co-movement to justify substitution, yet the data shows none. The synthesis should make the contradiction explicit — you cannot simultaneously claim BTC is taking gold's monetary share AND that it diversifies against gold; the gold-corr should be re-centered to 0.0-0.15 across all six gold-parity rows.

Volatility CONVERGES hard across all methods to ~45-55% (center ~50%) despite the methods being silent on vol — it is pure realized-vol carry-forward (anchor 103%/69%/57%) with a maturation haircut. The convergence is therefore an artifact of a shared anchor, not independent corroboration. Several rows (power-law 40-50%, DCF 45-55%, sizing 45-55%) put the FLOOR below the realized trailing-5y 57%, which assumes an ETF-era vol compression the <2yr ETF sample does not yet evidence. A more defensible cross-approach band is ~50-60% decade-average; only the equilibrium/sunspot row (55-70%) correctly resists the compression, and it is arguably the best-anchored vol in the set.

A second consensus correlation: growth-equity corr is RISING and material (0.26 -> 0.36 -> 0.56) and every approach converges on ~0.40-0.55 forward, treating the post-ETF risk-asset regime as the base case. This directly falsifies the issuer LTCMA glide-paths (CF Benchmarks 0.52->0.15, the 0.15 target) which the rows correctly reject as aspirational. The synthesis cross-cut should pair this with the gold-corr point: BTC's forward correlation profile is converging on 'high-beta growth/liquidity asset,' NOT 'digital gold' — the two are mutually reinforcing tells against the store-of-value thesis on a 10-15yr horizon.

A recurring citation-integrity pattern spans the academic rows: at least five misattributions (Lee & Rhee mis-cited as 'Park & Lee'; Yang & Fantazzini as 'Cretarola/Figa-Talamanca'; Austin Shelton as 'Klein et al.'; Bakry et al. as 'Kajtazi & Moro'; Rob Price as 'Robert Stammers'; Almeida-Grith-Miftachov-WANG dropping the 4th author), plus a recurring Burger/S2F-cointegration overstatement (he later self-retracted the spurious claim) appearing in THREE separate rows. The synthesis should run a single citation-reconciliation pass — the same wrong names recur because rows were verified independently without a shared bibliography.

The 'silent source' framing is misused in at least the monetary-substitution row, which claims no source publishes a 10-15yr CMA while CF Benchmarks (one of its own representative sources) publishes 30.1% nominal / 28% terminal vol / full correlation glide. This ~3x gap (30.1% published vs ~10-12% synthesized) is real and defensible (sell-side, long book, trend-elasticity the cons call partly spurious) but must be SHOWN as an explicit disagreement, not hidden behind 'source silent.' The same 30.1% CF Benchmarks number recurs across the TAM, LTCMA, and monetary rows and should be reconciled once, centrally.

Spurious-regression / non-stationarity is the universal academic verdict against the price-on-time and value-on-X families (S2F, Metcalfe, power-law, NVT), but the review under-deploys the single sharpest econometric objection — Granger-Newbold autocorrelated-residual spurious-trend regression — which it raises only in the power-law row. It applies equally to S2F (price on log-SF) and to any OLS-on-log-log-time fit, and should be the named cross-cutting econometric critique rather than per-row 'overfitting' language.
completeness.overall_assessment: [Round-1 critic assessment of the original 16 approaches. Round 2 acted on every actionable item: the 4 flagged-missing CMA-shape families were added (20 total now), and the gold-correlation overstatement, sub-floor volatilities, and citation misattributions were corrected. See House view above for the final cross-approach central.] The 16 kept approaches give strong coverage of the brief's seed taxonomy — all 13 seeded families are present, several with both crypto-native and academic representatives, and the verifier verdicts are unusually rigorous (correct catches on gold-corr overstatement, Burger self-retraction, multiple misattributions, and the adoption-S-curve TAM arithmetic error). The synthesized numbers are internally consistent and correctly subordinate model targets to the realized-decay anchor. Real gaps are: (1) no market-implied futures forward/basis row (distinct from the options-RND row); (2) no reflexive/LPPLS bubble-and-crash-hazard family despite citing Wheatley-Sornette; (3) no regime-switching/jump/heavy-tail return-process family, so every vol output is a single decaying scalar that understates tail/drawdown shape; (4) no explicit survival/ruin-probability (go-to-zero hazard) family to formalize the 'left-tail haircut' that six rows hand-wave. Before publishing, the synthesis must (a) re-center all gold-parity gold-correlations from 0.15-0.35 down to 0.0-0.15 to match realized ~0; (b) raise vol floors that sit below realized 57%; (c) run one shared citation-reconciliation pass to fix the five+ recurring misattributions and the Burger overstatement; (d) confront the CF Benchmarks 30.1% vs ~10-12% gap openly rather than via 'source silent.' The single most important framing point for the synthesis: the appreciation-decay curve, not any individual model, drives every forward CMA — the models supply narrative, and the data supplies a high-beta-growth-asset / not-digital-gold correlation profile that contradicts the store-of-value thesis the bullish families rely on.
completeness.house_view: House view (10-15yr BTC CMA central): nominal appreciation ~8-12%/yr, real ~5-9%/yr; annualized volatility ~50-60% with the floor pinned at the realized trailing-5y ~57% (NOT below it); BTC-gold correlation ~0.0-0.15 (realized is ~0: -0.01 full, +0.03 10y, +0.045 5y); BTC-growth-equity correlation ~0.40-0.55 and RISING as ETF/institutional ownership deepens. The load-bearing point: this central estimate is driven by the empirical appreciation-DECAY anchor (annualized appreciation collapsing roughly 142% -> 65% -> 17%/yr across successive windows), not by any single valuation model. S2F/S2FX, power-law, Metcalfe, cost-of-production, M2-elasticity, TAM-substitution, DCF/moneyness, adoption-S-curve and the LTCMA frames all disagree on level and mechanism and several are statistically discredited out-of-sample; what they reliably supply is NARRATIVE (why scarcity, network, debasement or adoption might sustain a positive but fading drift), while the DATA supplies the numbers and the correlation profile. And the data's verdict is unambiguous: BTC behaves as a high-beta growth/risk asset, NOT as digital gold. Every gold-parity / TAM-substitution row carries the same internal contradiction — those theses need BTC and gold to co-move for BTC to inherit gold's monetary share, yet realized gold co-movement is ~0 — so the digital-gold correlation cell cannot be used to justify both the appreciation TAM and a diversification benefit. We therefore center forward returns on the decay anchor (mid-single to low-double-digit nominal, fading toward the high end of the equity-risk-premium range as the asset matures), keep vol at a ~50-60% band floored by realized ~57% rather than crediting unproven ETF-era compression, treat gold correlation as ~0 (modeling 0.0-0.15 only as an upper guardrail), and treat the rising growth-equity beta as the operative correlation for any portfolio math.
